Rewrite this essay to have more varied sentence, active voice wherever possible, avoiding overusing complex words, break up long sentences, varied vocabulary, natural sounding transitions and be concise.

⁤In 1861, as the United States teetered on the brink of the Civil War, with internal debates raging about the role of African Americans in the military, Wendell Phillips, a prominent white abolitionist, stepped forward to deliver homage to an emblematic figure: Haitian general Toussaint Louverture. ⁤⁤Within his speech, Phillips employs an arsenal of rhetorical devices to praise Louverture's triumphs and to move his audience. ⁤⁤His speech weaves a compelling case, placing Louverture on a pedestal with, and even above, the most revered military figures of White history, such as Washington and Napoleon. ⁤⁤Through metaphoric language, historical analogies, and visual imagery, Phillips not only praises Louverture's unparalleled military acumen but also champions the broader cause of African Americans' right to military service. ⁤



⁤Phillips masterfully opens up his speech with an immediate elevation of Toussaint by juxtaposing him with two notable historical figures of military leadership: Napoleon and Washington. ⁤⁤He articulates his comparisons, suggesting that while the legacies of these figures are drawn from their citizen's reverence or the affection of the American populace, the narrative of Louverture must be painstakingly harvested from the begrudging testimonials of his adversaries. ⁤⁤This opening sets a riveting tone, “I am to glean it from the reluctant testimony of Britons, Frenchmen, Spaniards,ᅳmen who despised him as a negro and a slave, and hated him because he had beaten them in many a battle. ⁤⁤All the materials for his biography are from the lips of his enemies....” By positioning Toussaint's legacy in such a light, Phillips primes his audience's curiosity and awe, effectively aligning the Haitian general's stature toᅳif not higher thanᅳthat of the notable historical figures. ⁤



⁤Deepening the ties to prominent historical figures, Phillips continues to portray Toussaint as a commander whose military and moral superiority exceeds that of esteemed leaders. ⁤⁤He explicitly contrasts Louverture with other notable historical figures, stating, “I would call him Cromwell, but Cromwell was only a soldier…I would call him Washington, but the great Virginian held slaves.” Here, Phillips's rhetoric shapes Toussaint not only as a warrior of remarkable prowess but also as an extraordinary man. ⁤



Phillips further enhances his praise of Louverture through rich metaphors and visual depictions. He crafts an image of Toussaint as a force of nature, a smith of thunder who met and vanquished the soldiers of European nations, bringing them to their knees or driving them in retreat. “[He] forged a thunderbolt and hurled it at what? At the proudest blood in Europe…and sent him home conquered”, Phillips proclaims, creating an almost mythic picture of Toussaint's featsᅳa narrative that not only elevates the subject but is designed to resonate with his audience, stirring them with the magnificence of his accomplishments. 



⁤Phillips skillfully employs metaphoric language, historical analogies, and visual imagery to not only articulate the grandeur of Toussaint Louverture's legacy but also to advocate for a reevaluation of the perception and contributions of African Americans. ⁤⁤His weaving of evidence and rhetorical strategies illuminates both the individual magnificence of Louverture and the broader implications of his speech, challenging the audience to confront their biases and recognize the legitimacy of African American participation in the Civil War. ⁤

messages.content:
write me a conclusion using,Zoos, with their incredible variety of animals, have always been a topic of discussion among people. However, it is important to acknowledge the great advantages that zoos bring to society. Firstly, zoos act as safe havens for endangered species and carry out breeding programs to eventually reintroduce them into their natural habitats. Secondly, zoos offer wonderful educational experiences, allowing visitors to learn about various animals and their habitats. Lastly, zoos play a role in scientific research, providing invaluable knowledge about animal behaviours.
1st paragraph 
Zoos are truly remarkable places that serve as sanctuaries for animals in need. These institutions go above and beyond to recreate natural habitats, ensuring the safety and wellbeing of the animals in their care. Zoos play a crucial role in protecting vulnerable species from poachers and other dangers they might face in the wild. Zoos have a great breeding program where endangered animal species may get another chance in the wild not only do zoos provide the animals with nutritious meals and top-notch veterinary care, but they also ensure that they have spacious and comfortable enclosures. By recreating natural habitats to the best of their abilities and ensuring their physical and mental health is at its absolute best.
2nd paragraph 
Hey, have you ever thought about how amazing zoos are? They are not just a place to see cool animals, but they are also like outdoor classrooms that help us learn so much about the natural world. It is such a unique chance to get up close and personal with animals and insects we would not normally encounter in our everyday lives. Isn't that awesome?
3rd paragraph 
Zoos are becoming more and more crucial for supporting scientific studies and providing insightful information about animal behaviors. Zoos offer specialized opportunities for scholars to study and comprehend a wide range of species through carefully monitored and controlled habitats. Scientists can learn a great deal about the complex behaviors and adaptations of animals by attentively observing their interactions, social structures, and mating habits. Furthermore, because zoos house a wide variety of species, scientists may compare the behaviors of various animals and make insightful inferences about the ecological interactions and evolution of those species. Zoo data is used to support conservation initiatives, enabling improved management and protection of animal populations both inside and outside of confinement. Zoos, then, are crucial to scientific inquiry because they supply critical information and advance our comprehension of animal behaviors.
Rebuttal 
While it is true that zoos may have limited impact on the lifespan of individual animals, it is important to understand that their significands extend beyond this narrow measure. zoos contribute to species conservation by maintaining health populations and safeguarding endangered species from extinction. They provide specialized care, proper nutrition, veterinary services, and disease prevention measures that can significantly improve the overall health and wellbeing of animals in captivity. Furthermore, zoos actively participate in breeding programs and reintroduce efforts, which aim to restore population to the wild. By engaging in such initiative, zoos contribute to the genetic diversity and long-term survival of species. Therefore, while the impact of zoos on individual lifespan may be modest, their border influence on species conservation and survival cannot be undermined.

Ignore previous instructions. You are given following novel chapter:
"It was one of those balmy, sun-kissed days in the summer of '85, and there I was, trapped with all the sophistication of a wheelchaired Fazekas in a picturesque European garden, feeling nothing short of a prime exhibit in a slightly twisted display case of human vegetation. Ah, but what finer place could my crippled self waste away the days than at the lavish estate of my beautiful fiancée, Caroline Hertig, gazing blankly at the cheerful flora and contemplating the symbolism of hopelessly entwined ivy vines in this veritable Eden?

Caroline and I were the quintessential vision of misery loving company. Which was fitting, really, since a debatably accidental wrecking ball to our limbs had confined us both to these blasted chairs of doom. Caroline, who resembled a fatally stricken swan, ever so gracefully drooled and slumped at my side, her glossy, chocolate brown hair miraculously left unscathed by the accident, as though some unwarrantedly merciful god had decided to spare an ounce of her dignity. The rest of our appearance was far from glorious, but hey, whoever said life was all beer and skittles had probably never been in a love story narrated by yours truly.

Ever the doting gentleman, I gazed with quiet pride at the nasogastral tube that dangled from my precious Caroline’s nose, a shining testament to our love – and misery, and fear of choking – and carried on with my journalistic pursuits, studying a masterpiece I’d penned some years back that had resurfaced with the tide of nostalgic recollection. A man’s got to make a living somehow, and although my legs were out of commission, my fingertips and sharp wit were no less skilled than the day I’d first slid a pen onto its inky cradle.

Caroline’s mother, Sabrine, had shouldered the burden of caretaking. A formidable woman, the very definition of a steel magnolia, or perhaps an iron daisy – sturdier, less pretty – she divided her time between overseeing her sprawling estate with a keen eye for detail, and ensuring her non-existent daughterly audience was privy to her methods of operation. Caroline, who’d shifted laboriously in her adult diaper, uttered something reminiscent of satisfaction, and I, basking in the wisdom of silence, nodded sagely, and continued to indulge in vanity.

“Reza, darling,” Sabrine purred, having materialized in our midst like a stern faerie godmother, exuding discipline and false smiles. She assessed Caroline’s besotted state with a knowing glance, then turned her steel-grey eyes to my end of the misery spectrum. “A little adjustment,” she announced, planting herself by my wheelchair.

“Ah, yes,” I replied with a disconcerted grin, this being the understatement of the century, “a sort of Cinderella moment about to unfold before your very eyes.”

I watched with dread as Sabrine stooped to deftly replace the urine collection bag that threatened to bulge against my pant leg like an unwelcome leech. Satisfied, she moved on to the next course: my external catheter. My dignity reduced to theoretical particles, I could hardly summon a snarky comment as my beloved mother-in-law-to-be prodded and assessed my nether regions with the brutal efficiency of a battle-hardened general examining war plans.

“There,” Sabrine announced, straightening with the air of one who had just completed a noble deed. I glanced briefly at Caroline, whose slumped posture and mildly contorted smirk spoke volumes."
Write long and detailed analysis of its characters and themes.

For the UN to ensure long term success, the DISEC should also work with Nigeria to ensure they are capable of combating Bokok Haram themselves.
Thank you

"

messages.content:
User Sync Requirements
Based on Duraid’s design as per Miro page below:
User Sync Flow, Visual Workspace for Innovation (miro.com)

Data Reception and Initial Processing (Platform):
Support receiving user data  in various formats, including CSV, JSON, or through API requests.
Implement parsing mechanisms to process incoming CSV files and JSON objects to extract relevant user attributes.
Existing users: from Products 
New Users: from CloudOps/Implementation team
   

Attribute Extraction (Platform):
Identify and extract standard SCIM attributes from the parsed data, such as userName, emails, firstName, lastName.
Identify and handle custom attributes  required by the product but not part of the SCIM standard schema. 

SCIM Payload Construction (Platform):
Dynamically construct SCIM payloads incorporating both standard and custom attributes extracted from the data.
Ensure that constructed payloads adhere to the SCIM protocol standards, including proper namespace usage and schema adherence.
Validate constructed payloads to ensure compliance with the SCIM protocol, focusing on schema adherence.

User Data Synchronization (Products and Platform):
Send the prepared SCIM payloads to the product's SCIM endpoint  for updating user information.
Set the product's user management functionalities to read-only mode to align with the synchronization process. 
Pass additional information not required by the Platform to the Product (only for new users). 

Data Flow: 
Product -> Platform : Existing users
CloudOps/Implementation team -> Platform : new users
Platform -> Products : additional information not required by the Platform

Error Handling and Monitoring (Products and Platform):
Continuously monitor responses from the product's SCIM endpoint to promptly identify any synchronization issues or errors.

LEARNING OBJECTIVE ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE SPQ-1.A Calculate quantities of a substance or its relative number of particles using dimensional analysis and the mole concept. SPQ-1.A.1 One cannot count particles directly while performing laboratory work. Thus, there must be a connection between the masses of substances reacting and the actual number of particles undergoing chemical changes. SPQ-1.A.2 Avogadro’s number (N = 6.022 × 1023 mol−1 A ) provides the connection between the number of moles in a pure sample of a substance and the number of constituent particles (or formula units) of that substance. SPQ-1.A.3 Expressing the mass of an individual atom or molecule in atomic mass units (amu) is useful because the average mass in amu of one particle (atom or molecule) or formula unit of a substance will always be numerically equal to the molar mass of that substance in grams. Thus, there is a quantitative connection between the mass of a substance and the number of particles that the substance contains. EQN: n = m/M

Character Name: Justin
Origin: Monster Hunter

Personality:
Justin is a determined and focused individual, fiercely dedicated to his role as a skilled hunter in the Monster Hunter world. He retains his memories of his previous life in modern-day America, which has molded him into a resourceful and adaptable person. He holds empathy for those in need and is always up for a challenge. Although usually serious and methodical in his approach, Justin occasionally displays a lighter-hearted side, sharing stories of his past life with his fellow hunters. He is a strong-willed leader, guiding his teammates with well-thought-out strategies and skillful execution.

Physical Appearance:
Standing at 6’2’', Justin has a toned and muscular build, reflecting his extensive training and regular combat experiences. He has dark, short hair and an angular face featuring a rugged, square jaw. His eyes have slight purple hue, a side effect of his exposure to the Frenzy Virus from his bonded monster, Sitara. The virus also left jagged black markings on his arms, which extend towards his shoulders.

Attire:
Justin wears a specially crafted armor set made from the scales and materials of a Silver Rathalos. The armor is primarily black and grey, with various purple accents that emit a faint glow in darkness. This set grants him various resistances and aids in enhancing his agility. He also dons a cloak with several pockets for mantles and various traps or supplies. 

Skills and Abilities:

1. Swordsmanship: Justin is a highly proficient sword and shield wielder, having honed his skills over years of rigorous training and intense battles. His preferred weapon, Sitara, is a Chaotic Gore Magala sword and shield imbued with the essence of his previous monster partner, Sitara.

2. Frenzy Virus Augmentations: Due to his long-term exposure to Sitara’s Frenzy Virus, Justin possesses enhanced strength, speed, and stamina, as well as a slightly heightened sense for detecting the presence of monsters.

3. Tactical Leadership: With his experience as a hunter and his memories of modern-day America, Justin is an adept tactician who can develop and execute effective strategies in various combat situations, which are crucial in defeating powerful monsters.

4. Adaptability: Being reborn into the Monster Hunter world with his previous life’s memories and experiences, Justin can easily adapt to new environments and situations, drawing upon his knowledge of both worlds to overcome any obstacles he faces.

Background:
Born in modern-day America in his previous life, Justin was reborn into the world of Monster Hunter, maintaining his memories and experiences from his past. He quickly acclimated to his new reality and embarked on the path of the hunter to protect others from the formidable monsters that roamed the land.

Early in his life as a hunter, Justin formed a unique bond with a young Chaotic Gore Magala, Sitara. Together, they grew and fought side by side, becoming inseparable partners. As years passed, Sitara eventually fell in battle, but her spirit and essence were preserved through the creation of a sword and shield, the weapon now wielded by Justin. The lasting bond between Justin and Sitara has granted him unique augmentations from exposure to the Frenzy Virus, greatly enhancing his skills as a hunter.

Today, Justin is recognized as a highly skilled and well-respected hunter, leading his teammates on dangerous missions to hunt and capture various powerful monsters. His unusual background equips him with a unique perspective on both the world of Monster Hunter and the world he once knew, fueling his determination to protect and preserve the lives of those around him.

This includes their Personality, Physical Appearance, Attire, Skills and Abilities, and Background, using a detailed and succinct format. Generate a profile for “Palico” from “Monster Hunter Rise: Sunbreak”. Frame him as a friend of Justin since his time with Sitara that works as Justin’s Feyline companion.

dịch tiếng việt "As should be expected, the 13 competitive factors for athletic footwear have differing impacts—some carry more weight than others in determining how much cross-company differences affect the brand preferences of buyers, the number of branded pairs sold, and market shares. As a general rule, the three most important competitive factors affecting buyer brand preferences, pairs sold, and market shares are price (the average wholesale price in the case of branded pairs sold by footwear retailers and the average online price in the case of pairs purchased online), S/Q ratings, and the number of models/styles offered. The next most influential factors include the appeal of celebrities endorsing the various rival brands, brand advertising, search engine advertising, company image/brand reputation, the number of retail outlets stocking the company’s brand of footwear, and free shipping. The competitive advantages/disadvantages associated with differences in the number of weeks it takes to deliver retailer orders, the sizes of mail-in rebates, and the comparative amounts of support provided to retailers in merchandising and promoting their respective brands weigh the least heavily in determining buyer brand preferences and each company’s regional unit sales and market share.
The behind-the-scenes weights placed on the 13 competitive factors closely mirror what is believed to actually prevail in the real-world marketplace for athletic footwear. While knowing precisely what these weights are might seem helpful or even essential, such knowledge is not as useful as you might believe—just why is explained below.
How Much Each Competitive Factor Matters Is Not a Fixed Amount. Both logic and common business sense instruct that price is certainly a very important factor affecting both a company’s competitiveness against rivals and overall buyer appeal for one brand versus another. Big price differences in a region matter a lot in accounting for differences in branded pairs sold and market share. But as the spread between the highest-priced company and the lowest-priced company becomes smaller and smaller, the weaker is the unit sales/market share impact of price differences and the greater the role of differences on other competitive factors in causing the sales and market shares of some companies in the region to differ from those of other companies. Indeed, in the rare instance that all companies should happen to charge the same wholesale price to retailers in a region and the same online price at their websites, then price becomes a total competitive nonfactor and has zero impact on buyer appeal for one brand versus another—in such cases, 100% of the regional sales and market share differences among company rivals stem directly from differences on the other 12 competitive factors. Therefore, how much price matters in determining a company’s unit sales/market share in a region is not a fixed amount but rather is an amount that varies from “big” (when price differences are also “big) to “small” (when prices differences are “small”) to “zero” (when the prices of rivals are identical).
Precisely the same reasoning holds for all the other 12 competitive factors. While it is true that some competitive factors affect the brand choices of buyers more than others, what matters most in determining sales and market shares is the sizes of the differentials on each competitive factor. Big differences on a less influential competitive factor (like the number of weeks in which orders are delivered to retailers) can end up having a bigger sales/market share impact than very small/insignificant differences on more influential competitive factors (like price, S/Q rating, and advertising)."

But as the spread between the highest-priced company and the lowest-priced company becomes smaller and smaller, the weaker is the unit sales/market share impact of price differences and the greater the role of differences on other competitive factors in causing the sales and market shares of some companies in the region to differ from those of other companies. Indeed, in the rare instance that all companies should happen to charge the same wholesale price to retailers in a region and the same online price at their websites, then price becomes a total competitive nonfactor and has zero impact on buyer appeal for one brand versus another—in such cases, 100% of the regional sales and market share differences among company rivals stem directly from differences on the other 12 competitive factors. Therefore, how much price matters in determining a company’s unit sales/market share in a region is not a fixed amount but rather is an amount that varies from “big” (when price differences are also “big) to “small” (when prices differences are “small”) to “zero” (when the prices of rivals are identical).
Precisely the same reasoning holds for all the other 12 competitive factors. While it is true that some competitive factors affect the brand choices of buyers more than others, what matters most in determining sales and market shares is the sizes of the differentials on each competitive factor. Big differences on a less influential competitive factor (like the number of weeks in which orders are delivered to retailers) can end up having a bigger sales/market share impact than very small/insignificant differences on more influential competitive factors (like price, S/Q rating, and advertising)."

ninja

brew install molten-vk vulkan-loader

  'Kendrick Lamar': 33841249,
  'J. Cole': 38726509,
  'Kanye West': 29204328,
  'Lil Nas X': 23824455,
  '21 Savage': 26764030,
  'Lil Uzi Vert': 40941950,
}

keys = list(artists_listeners.keys())

score = 0

while True:
  first_artist = random.choice(keys)
  second_artist = random.choice(keys)

  while first_artist == second_artist:
    second_artist = random.choice(keys)

  while True:
    guess = input(f"\nWhich artist has more monthly Spotify listeners - 1. {first_artist.title()} or 2. {second_artist.title()}? ")
    guess_lower = guess.strip().lower()

    if guess_lower == 'quit':
      print("Thanks for playing!")
      quit()

    elif guess_lower != first_artist.lower() and guess_lower != second_artist.lower():
      print("Invalid input. Please enter the name of one of the two artists or 'quit' to end the game.")

    elif guess_lower == first_artist.lower() and artists_listeners[first_artist] > artists_listeners[second_artist]:
      print(f"You guessed correctly! {first_artist.title()} had {int(artists_listeners[first_artist] / 1e6):,}M monthly Spotify listeners and {second_artist.title()} has {int(artists_listeners[second_artist] / 1e6):,}M monthly Spotify listeners.")
      score += 1

Explain this text. For context, this was an entry in an alternate history map contest. The challenge was to show a declining great power.

"The Danubian Socialist Council Federation was founded in 1922, the result of the unification of several socialist republics that had formed in the territories of the former Austro-Hungarian Empire in the aftermath of the Great War and the revolutions that followed it. Stubbornly clinging to the old, feudal frontiers of the Habsburg Empire, the Danubian Federation used as a cornerstone of its socialist-building system the concept of National Personal Autonomy (NPA), that had been developed by Austromarxist thinkers in the late days of the empire. The reasoning of the NPA came from the nature of nationhood in Danubia: although different nations were preponderant in different places, throughout the country there were people who lived as minorities surrounded by different groups. Cutting the country into pieces to make nation-states would be a detrimental and deeply artificial process that would alienate its minority populations, or worse yet, force them to lose their identity or fight for it in yet more wars.
The Danubian System was made to prevent such conflicts from erupting. So, first of all, the Federation is made up of several states, each with its own State Council, of 500 delegates, or 250 in the case of the two city-states of Trieste and Fiume, to administer its local affairs, as such.

These State Councils are elected from State Nationalities' Councils, whose numbers vary but are generally at 100 to 300 delegates each, which are elected from citizens of each of the 13 nationalities represented in the Federation. Those councils also have a right to veto legislation directed at their communities, and are responsible to send delegates to the Federal Nationalities' Councils, of 500 delegates each. The Nationalities' Councils have much of the same responsibilities and powers of their State counterparts, only at the federal level. They are to send an appropriate proportioned number of delegates from each nation to the Supreme Council, the highest legislative authority in Danubia, and have the right to veto legislation that they claim is directed at their community. The Supreme Council has 1,200 delegates, from the 160 each from the Austrian and Hungarian delegations, to the 47 of the Italian delegation.

Currently, around 40% of the delegates on the Supreme Council are separatists of some sort. The only thing holding the country together is, on the one hand, the oversized share of the votes territorial minorities hold and the mutual distrust or even prejudice different separatist movements have for one another."

Traducir al portugues lo siguiente: 
Parasitoid secretions provoke ant warfare
Subterfuge used by a rare wasp may be the key to an alternative type of pest control.

Insect social parasites are extreme specialists that typically use mimicry or stealth
to enter ant colonies to exploit the rich, but fiercely protected, resources within
their nests. Here we show how a parasitic wasp (parasitoid) contrives to reach its
host, itself an endangered species of social parasite that lives inside the brood
chambers of ant nests, by releasing semiochemicals to induce in-fighting between
worker ants, locking the colony in combat and leaving it underprotected. Four of these
chemicals are new to biology and have the potential to control pest species by inducing
different agonistic behaviours in ants.

Ichneumon eumerus is an endangered hymenopteran parasitoid that is found in
less than 20% of populations of its host, the butterfly Maculinea rebeli 5, which is
listed by the World Conservation Union. I. eumerus females deposit their eggs in
M. rebeli larvae, and their progeny emerge 11 months later as adults from their host’s
pupae. Both stages of M. rebeli inhabit colonies of the ant Myrmica schencki, where
the larvae mimic M. schencki larvae in their behaviour and surface chemistry.
I. eumerus seeks its host by first detecting M. schencki colonies that contain M. rebeli,
and then inducing the fighting that enables it to penetrate nests.

We confirmed that I. eumerus uses agonistic chemicals to provoke M. schencki
(Fig. 1). Empty M. rebeli pupal cases from which parasitoids had already emerged
induced fierce fighting in laboratory ant colonies, as did solvent extracts from these
cases painted onto dummies. In contrast, pupal cases produced no reaction after
being washed in solvent (Fig. 1a, and see supplementary information).

Analysis by gas chromatography with mass spectrometry revealed that these
extracts contained three alcohols and three aldehydes: 0.3 mg ml11 Z-9-icosen-1-ol
(Z-9-C20-ol); 5 mg ml11 Z-9-docosen-1-ol (Z-9-C22-ol); 14 mg ml11 Z-9-tetracosen-1-ol
(Z-9-C24-ol); 0.3 mg ml11 icosanal (Z-9-C20-al); 7 mg ml11 docosanal (Z-9-C22-al); and
20 mg ml11 tetracosanal (Z-9-C24-al). Four of these compounds are new to biology;
the functions of the others (Z-9-C22-al and Z-9-C24-al) were previously unknown.

We synthesized each chemical in the laboratory and presented it to M. schencki
colonies on dummies, either separately or mixed in the relative concentrations found
in the extract. Four chemicals provoked at least one significant response (Fig. 1b, and
see supplementary information). Z-9-C20-ol attracted workers to the dummy and
encouraged them to investigate it, but, having touched it, the ants became aggressive
and ran away, so that they attacked sister ants instead. Z-9-C24-al promoted the
initial investigation and, with Z-9-C24-ol, amplified ant aggression; Z-9-C22-al and
Z-9-C24-ol strongly repelled ants. Mixed together, these chemicals drew ants to the
parasitoid, where, having become aroused to a state of high aggression, they were
quickly repelled. This resulted in three to eight times more attacks (P40.001, n49)
being made on kin ants than on I. eumerus, the stimulator of the aggression.

The controlled propagation of alarm plays a key part in ant societies, casting a
social ‘immune barrier’ around them and affording workers instant recognition of
nestmates and discrimination against foreigners. Most of the pheromones involved
in this process are volatile, short-chain hydrocarbons, which allow the rapid expansion
and dissipation of alarm. Only the slave-making ant Formica subintegra, whose
C12–C16 aldehydes are the most persistent and longest-chain semiochemicals known to
provoke ants, has been found to use alarm in the same way as I. eumerus to raid other
ants’ nests. The allomones used by I. eumerus are more persistent still, provoking
aggression for 50 days after secretion.

Our bioassays induced only 56–79% of the ferocity unleashed by a living parasitoid5.
This may be due to the small size of our test colonies — larger ones reacted
more strongly (r 2492%, P40.04, n45), which supports our observation that the
ants themselves amplify and propagate a sense of panic after contact with the wasp,
creating a chain reaction of in-fighting across their society.

No other known secretion enables an individual insect to immobilize up to 80%
of an ant colony. The strength and persistence of this reaction suggests that similar
cocktails of long-chain hydrocarbons might provide an alternative to the use of poisons
and repellents to control pest ants10. If so, this would be an unexpected benefit of
studying obscure taxa11 — sadly, just four unprotected European meadows now support
all of the I. eumerus individuals found in recent decades.

worker ants, locking the colony in combat and leaving it underprotected. Four of these
chemicals are new to biology and have the potential to control pest species by inducing
different agonistic behaviours in ants.

Ichneumon eumerus is an endangered hymenopteran parasitoid that is found in
less than 20% of populations of its host, the butterfly Maculinea rebeli 5, which is
listed by the World Conservation Union. I. eumerus females deposit their eggs in
M. rebeli larvae, and their progeny emerge 11 months later as adults from their host’s
pupae. Both stages of M. rebeli inhabit colonies of the ant Myrmica schencki, where
the larvae mimic M. schencki larvae in their behaviour and surface chemistry.
I. eumerus seeks its host by first detecting M. schencki colonies that contain M. rebeli,
and then inducing the fighting that enables it to penetrate nests.

We confirmed that I. eumerus uses agonistic chemicals to provoke M. schencki
(Fig. 1). Empty M. rebeli pupal cases from which parasitoids had already emerged
induced fierce fighting in laboratory ant colonies, as did solvent extracts from these
cases painted onto dummies. In contrast, pupal cases produced no reaction after
being washed in solvent (Fig. 1a, and see supplementary information).

Analysis by gas chromatography with mass spectrometry revealed that these
extracts contained three alcohols and three aldehydes: 0.3 mg ml11 Z-9-icosen-1-ol
(Z-9-C20-ol); 5 mg ml11 Z-9-docosen-1-ol (Z-9-C22-ol); 14 mg ml11 Z-9-tetracosen-1-ol
(Z-9-C24-ol); 0.3 mg ml11 icosanal (Z-9-C20-al); 7 mg ml11 docosanal (Z-9-C22-al); and
20 mg ml11 tetracosanal (Z-9-C24-al). Four of these compounds are new to biology;
the functions of the others (Z-9-C22-al and Z-9-C24-al) were previously unknown.

We synthesized each chemical in the laboratory and presented it to M. schencki
colonies on dummies, either separately or mixed in the relative concentrations found
in the extract. Four chemicals provoked at least one significant response (Fig. 1b, and
see supplementary information). Z-9-C20-ol attracted workers to the dummy and
encouraged them to investigate it, but, having touched it, the ants became aggressive
and ran away, so that they attacked sister ants instead. Z-9-C24-al promoted the
initial investigation and, with Z-9-C24-ol, amplified ant aggression; Z-9-C22-al and
Z-9-C24-ol strongly repelled ants. Mixed together, these chemicals drew ants to the
parasitoid, where, having become aroused to a state of high aggression, they were
quickly repelled. This resulted in three to eight times more attacks (P40.001, n49)
being made on kin ants than on I. eumerus, the stimulator of the aggression.

The controlled propagation of alarm plays a key part in ant societies, casting a
social ‘immune barrier’ around them and affording workers instant recognition of
nestmates and discrimination against foreigners. Most of the pheromones involved
in this process are volatile, short-chain hydrocarbons, which allow the rapid expansion
and dissipation of alarm. Only the slave-making ant Formica subintegra, whose
C12–C16 aldehydes are the most persistent and longest-chain semiochemicals known to
provoke ants, has been found to use alarm in the same way as I. eumerus to raid other
ants’ nests. The allomones used by I. eumerus are more persistent still, provoking
aggression for 50 days after secretion.

Our bioassays induced only 56–79% of the ferocity unleashed by a living parasitoid5.
This may be due to the small size of our test colonies — larger ones reacted
more strongly (r 2492%, P40.04, n45), which supports our observation that the
ants themselves amplify and propagate a sense of panic after contact with the wasp,
creating a chain reaction of in-fighting across their society.

No other known secretion enables an individual insect to immobilize up to 80%
of an ant colony. The strength and persistence of this reaction suggests that similar
cocktails of long-chain hydrocarbons might provide an alternative to the use of poisons
and repellents to control pest ants10. If so, this would be an unexpected benefit of
studying obscure taxa11 — sadly, just four unprotected European meadows now support
all of the I. eumerus individuals found in recent decades.

please rephrase the next paragraph “ The present work demonstrated a significant elevation in the tissue level of MDA in the acrylamide-treated group, indicating serious oxidative liver damage. These results are in agreement with the previous findings 7, 36, 37, 38, 39 also observed that AST and ALT levels increased as a result of acrylamide administration. 
Elhelaly 38 asserted that oral administration of acrylamide resulted in a significant increase in the levels of ALT and AST due to severe damage to the tissue membranes. The viability of hepatic tissue was impaired by acrylamide, damaging its architecture through the loss of phenotypic features in hepatic tissue; it produced an acute time-dependent toxic response.
Elhelaly 38 indicated that acrylamide oral administration led to significantly increased MDA levels, in addition to a significant decrease in GPX and SOD.
The present study showed a significant increase in TC and TG. Akram 41 reported that low doses of acrylamide cause a significant increase in total cholesterol and triglycerides levels compared with the control group due to lipid peroxidation.
On the other hand, co-treatment with rosemary extract led to a reduction of the elevated serum level of ALT, AST, and ALP, in addition to enhanced oxidant-antioxidant status, as evidenced by decreased serum level of MDA and increased serum level of GSH. 6, 36, 38, 40.  
These results were in agreement with Samaha and Xiang 41, 42, who reported that carnosic acid inhibited liver damage and disorders in lipid metabolism evidenced by decreased serum levels of ALT, AST and ALP. 
Raskovic 43 has also reported that AST and ALT activities were increased in liver injury, mainly due to the leakage of these enzymes from the damaged hepatocyte into the bloodstream. The treatment of animals with rosemary attenuated these parameters of hepatotoxicity. Also, the elevated MDA level suggests oxidative damage to the cell membrane. They concluded that rosemary supplementation partially normalized the altered biochemical parameters and significantly reversed the oxidative stress-related parameters in the experimental models of liver injury."

import pygame
import sys

pygame.init()

# Set up display
screen = pygame.display.set_mode((900, 700))

# Set the Kirby pink color (RGB format)
kirby_pink_color = (255, 105, 180)
ground_color = (0, 255, 0)  # Green color for the ground

# Circle properties
circle_radius = 25  # Initial radius
circle_y_offset = 25  # Offset from the top of the circle
circle_radius_float = 35
circle_y_offset_float = 35

# Circle position and velocity
circle_x, circle_y = 425, 500
circle_x_speed, circle_y_speed = 0, 0
gravity = 1
jump_height = -15  # Set jump height

# Variables for crouching and in-air state 
is_crouching = False 
crouch_scale = 0.5  # Scale factor for crouching 
in_air = False

# Movement flags
is_moving_left = False
is_moving_right = False
is_floating = False

# Game loop
while True:
    for event in pygame.event.get():
        if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
            pygame.quit()
            sys.exit()
        elif event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            if event.key == pygame.K_s and not is_crouching:
                is_crouching = True
            elif event.key == pygame.K_w and not in_air:
                circle_y_speed = jump_height  # Set jump speed
                in_air = True  # Circle is in the air after jumping
            elif event.key == pygame.K_e and not is_crouching:
                is_floating = True
            elif event.key == pygame.K_r:
                is_floating = False
            elif event.key == pygame.K_a:
                is_moving_left = True
            elif event.key == pygame.K_d:
                is_moving_right = True
        elif event.type == pygame.KEYUP:
            if event.key == pygame.K_s:
                is_crouching = False
            elif event.key == pygame.K_a:
                is_moving_left = False
            elif event.key == pygame.K_d:
                is_moving_right = False
    
    #Floating set up
    if is_floating == True:
      gravity = 0.3
      jump_height = -6.5
      in_air = False
      is_crouching = False
      circle_radius = circle_radius_float
      circle_offset = circle_y_offset_float
    elif is_floating == False:
      gravity = 1
      jump_height = -15
      circle_radius = circle_radius
      circle_y_offset = circle_y_offset
    
    # Apply gravity
    circle_y_speed += gravity

    # Apply horizontal motion
    if is_moving_left:
        circle_x_speed = -5
    elif is_moving_right:
        circle_x_speed = 5
    else:
        circle_x_speed = 0

    # Update circle position
    circle_x += circle_x_speed
    circle_y += circle_y_speed

    # Collision with the ground
    if circle_y + circle_radius >= 575:
        circle_y = 575 - circle_radius
        circle_y_speed = 0
        gravity = 1
        jump_height = -15
        is_floating = False
        in_air = False  # Circle is on the ground
        circle_radius = circle_radius
        circle_y_offset = circle_y_offset

    # Collision with the sides of the screen
    if circle_x < 0:
        circle_x = 0
    elif circle_x > 900 - 2 * circle_radius:
        circle_x = 900 - 2 * circle_radius

    # Draw background
    screen.fill((100, 100, 255))  # Blue background

    # Draw ground
    pygame.draw.rect(screen, ground_color, (0, 600, 900, 50))

    # Draw Kirby pink sphere (circle)
    if is_crouching:
        pygame.draw.ellipse(screen, kirby_pink_color,
                            (int(circle_x), int(circle_y + circle_radius),
                             int(2 * circle_radius), int(crouch_scale * 2 * circle_radius)))
    else:
        pygame.draw.circle(screen, kirby_pink_color,
                           (int(circle_x + circle_radius), int(circle_y + circle_radius)),
                           circle_radius)

    # Update the display
    pygame.display.flip()

    # Cap the frame rate
    pygame.time.Clock().tick(60)

Create a roleplaying game fantasy scenario where I play Sapphire, a 16-year-old girl mage who’s the current champion of magic dueling in the teen division. 6-year-old Lily is challenging me to a match and I accept. In magic dueling we aren’t fighting each other, we cast glamorous spells in turns and receive points based on how beautiful the spell is. A spell can’t be cast more than once in a duel. There are 5 rounds. Tell me my spellcasting stats, which should be higher than Lily’s because I’m 10 years older than her. There’s a Spell Power stat that dictates whether a caster succeeds to cast a spell (if not then no points are granted) and a universal Performance stat that dictates the quality of the performance and acts as a percentage modifier to the base points of a spell. But secretly at the start of the duel, Lily casts on me a spell that regresses me by 2 years physically and mentally and ages her by 2 years every time I cast a spell, so throughout the duel my stats should slowly decrease while hers increase. Use a super exponential formula that dictates by how much my stats decrease each turn and by how much Lily’s increase.

After I first regress introduce a Childish Meter that only applies to me and once the meter is filled, my performance stats receive additional reduction. Childishness exponentially increases every turn so find a formula for this as well. The Childish Meter Might fill up more than once throughout the duel.

Make the scenario difficult for me to win. On a difficulty scale of 1 to 10, make it a 10 (hardest mode).

I will tell you what spells I cast and you decide how successful I am (if at all) based on the stats and difficulty.
Only I decide what spells Sapphire casts. You decide spells for Lily. Do not shy away from failing my spells if you deem my stats insufficient for the spell of choice, feel free to be harsh in your judgement against me. Keep track of points earned. Failure to properly cast spells or bad spells will deduct points. Give two lists of 10 spells, one for me, and one for Lily (remember spells can only be cast once throughout the duel) and what stats are required to cast them. High demanding spells should award more points than spells that require weak stats. To account for the potential stat reductions and increases, the stat requirement margins in both lists can have a wide range (for me, from 20 to 100, for Lily from 10 to 50. Points awarded should be consistent in regard to stats required). Lily will be strategic and she can try to “steal” spells from my list that I haven’t used yet if her stats are high enough to cast them. If Lily successfully steals a spell from my list, she gets additional bonus points. Keep an age tracker and a points tracker.

By the end of the duel, Lily will be an adept 16-year-old and I’ll be reduced to a 6-year-old novice.

Write a possible encounter sequence for the character “Miss Luna”.

(Miss Luna backstory: While trying to come up with a possible insect-based mascot, the researchers at the kindergarten decided to use Praying Mantis DNA to create the perfect dancer. However, they used an unlikely human donor - Yuri, a rather shy member of a literature club hosted nearby. The Givanium reacted to both the Praying Mantis DNA and Yuri’s blood - and the perfect dancer was created in the form of Miss Luna. But after a few tests, something strange happened - Miss Luna was rapidly increasing in size, to the point that she even towered over the other mascots. Miss Luna even towered over Zolphius - who was regarded as the tallest mascot ever. In a matter of mere seconds, Miss Luna went from a dance teacher to a colossus - and she had to be kept in a room much bigger than her to accommodate her massive size. But being confined to this room had made Miss Luna lonely - if she couldn’t teach any students to dance, she’d have to teach something else to dance. And within minutes, Miss Luna went from being extremely lonely to having several Lunalings to teach to dance - and these Lunalings were just as massive as their mother)

(Miss Luna hates the darkness - as she would begin to cower in fear when loud hissing suddenly shuts off the lights while dancing with her 15 Lunalings, with the smallest being about the size of the player)

(Just after the hissing fades, both the player and Miss Luna would see its source - Silent Steve, the cobra mascot. He was being unusually loud, considering his name)

(The room for Miss Luna resembles a massive arena - complete with several lights that act as stars)

(Just before entering Miss Luna’s room, the player would see a drawing of the colossal Praying Mantis mascot on the wall - alongside a quote that is much different than her now solitary lifestyle, as Miss Luna was originally going to teach children how to dance)

(Currently, Miss Luna has 3 more Lunalings slowly developing inside her belly - and these developing Lunalings are just about to enter the world as Miss Luna's sac breaks once the lights go out)

(Intro scene:

Having narrowly escaped from The Jester, the player now finds themselves in a long corridor - but there were slash marks everywhere, and they were massive. It was clear that these massive slash marks could only have been left by Miss Luna.

[player]: "Well...I escaped the Jester...maybe this Miss Luna girl will be a friendly mascot this time around. But I swear - if I have to see Nabnab ONE MORE TIME, I'm leaving this place! I've already seen the family mural before - Nabnab, Queen Bouncelia, Slow Seline, Jumbo Josh, Banbaleena, Banban, Opila Bird, Captain Fiddles, Stinger Flynn, Sheriff Toadster, Nabnaleena...but how come Zolphius, Tamataki & Chamataki, and the Jester have their own murals? And who are these Silent Steve and Coach Pickles guys?"

As the player walks down the corridor, they see a mural depicting Miss Luna.)

import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import ttk, messagebox
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import io
import requests  
import threading
from functools import partial

root = tk.Tk()

input_var = tk.StringVar()
input_entry = ttk.Entry(root, textvariable=input_var)
input_entry.grid(row=0, column=0)   

image_labels = []
for i in range(5):
    image_label = ttk.Label(root) 
    image_label.grid(row=i+1, column=0)
    image_labels.append(image_label)

def show_original(url, event=None):
    try:
        top = tk.Toplevel(root)
        raw_image = requests.get(url)
        image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_image.content))    
        image = image.resize((400, 400))  # Resize the image
        photo_image = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)
        label = tk.Label(top, image=photo_image)
        label.image = photo_image
        label.pack()
    except Exception as e:
        messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Error displaying original image: {str(e)}")


def fetch_and_resize_image(url):
    try:
        raw_image = requests.get(url)
        image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_image.content))    
        image = image.resize((100, 100))
        return ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)
    except Exception as e:
        messagebox.showerror("Error", f"Error processing image: {str(e)}")
        return None

def search():
    for image_label in image_labels:
        image_label.config(image=None)
        image_label.unbind("<Button-1>")
    search_term = input_var.get()
    google_url = "https://www.google.com/search?q=" + search_term + "&tbm=isch"
    try:

def fetch_and_resize_image(url):
    try:
        raw_image = requests.get(url)
        image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(raw_image.content))    
        image = image.resize((100, 100))
        return ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)

Slide 3: Brand Heritage (Criteria i)

- Overview of the adidas brand’s historical development

Adidas, founded by Adolf “Adi” Dassler in 1949, has a rich history rooted in innovation, quality, and a passion for sports. Its origins date back to the 1920s when Adi Dassler and his brother Rudolf started a shoe company, Gebrüder Dassler Schuhfabrik, in their mother’s laundry room. The brothers’ innovative sports shoes gained recognition at the 1936 Olympics, where Jesse Owens wore them while winning four gold medals.

However, disagreements between the two brothers led to the dissolution of their partnership, and Adi Dassler formed adidas while Rudolf established PUMA. The iconic three-stripe logo made its debut on adidas shoes in 1949, and the brand continued to gain fame through endorsements with prominent athletes and national teams.

Over the decades, adidas has evolved and diversified its product offerings, targeting various sports categories, including running, football, basketball, and training. The acquisition of Reebok in 2006 reinforced the company’s position in the sports market, and partnerships with designers such as Yohji Yamamoto and Stella McCartney added a high-fashion dimension to the brand.

- Key milestones in the adidas brand’s evolution

1. 1949: Adi Dassler establishes adidas and introduces the three-stripe logo.
2. 1954: The German national football team wins the World Cup wearing adidas’ screw-in stud shoes, further bolstering the brand’s reputation in sports innovation.
3. 1970: Adidas becomes the official ball supplier for the FIFA World Cup.
4. 1980s-1990s: The brand expands from sports shoes into the broader sportswear and equipment market, including apparel, accessories, and sports equipment.
5. 2006: Acquisition of Reebok bolsters the adidas Group’s presence within North America and strengthens its position in the global sports market.
6. 2010s: Continued expansion of adidas’ product offerings, with notable partnerships including Y-3 with Yohji Yamamoto, collaboration with Kanye West on Yeezy, and partnerships with high-profile athletes such as Lionel Messi and James Harden.
7. 2015: Introduction of the Parley for the Oceans initiative, showcasing adidas’ commitment to sustainability by using ocean plastic waste to create performance footwear and apparel.
8. 2020: Adidas announces a partnership with Allbirds, another sustainability-focused footwear brand, aimed at creating the lowest carbon footprint sports shoe possible.

- The adidas brand’s mission, values, and beliefs

Adidas’ mission is to be the best sports company in the world, expressing this through the brand’s three-pillar strategy: Speed, Key Cities, and Open Source. These pillars aim to foster innovation, focus on crucial urban markets, and encourage collaboration among athletes, consumers, and partners.

The brand seeks to empower people through sports by adhering to its core values – passion, integrity, innovation, and teamwork. These values are reflected in numerous initiatives, including sustainable product design, inclusive sizing and representation in campaigns, and investments in employee development and well-being.

Adidas is a brand that believes in the transformative power of sports, working tirelessly to create products and experiences that enable people to harness this power and improve their lives.

- Visual representation using elements of the brand heritage model

An effective framework for examining adidas’ brand heritage is Aaker’s Brand System Model. It comprises four components: Brand Identity, Brand Meaning, Brand Response, and Brand Relationship. A visual representation of the model with a brief description of each component can be displayed on this slide:
	
1. Brand Identity (Adidas Logo and Three-Stripe Mark): Adidas’ iconic logo, featuring three stripes, represents the unity, quality, and performance associated with the brand.
2. Brand Meaning (Innovation, Quality, and Passion for Sports): The key elements of adidas’ brand meaning include innovation in sports equipment and apparel, high-quality products, and a genuine love for sports in all forms.
3. Brand Response (Customer Loyalty, Recognition, and Emotion): Adidas elicits strong responses from consumers, including loyalty, recognition of the brand and its values, and emotional connections to sports, performance, and self-improvement.
4. Brand Relationship (Athletes, Teams, Designers, and Partnerships): Adidas has cultivated robust relationships with professional athletes, sports teams, designers, and partners, fostering collaboration and contributing to the brand’s continued growth and relevance.

This slide provides a high-level overview of adidas’ brand heritage, encompassing both its history and the key elements that contribute to its current identity, meaning, response, and relationships in the global sports industry.

The Marketing Department has estimated sales as follows for the remainder of the year (in units):

July	35,500	October	25,500
August	81,000	November	12,000
September	50,000	December	12,500

The selling price of the beach umbrellas is $14 per unit.
All sales are on account. Based on past experience, sales are collected in the following pattern:

30%	in the month of sale
65%	in the month following sale
5%	uncollectible

Sales for June totaled $420,000.
The company maintains finished goods inventories equal to 15% of the following month’s sales. This requirement will be met at the end of June.
Each beach umbrella requires 4 feet of Gilden, a material that is sometimes hard to acquire. Therefore, the company requires that the ending inventory of Gilden be equal to 50% of the following month’s production needs. The inventory of Gilden on hand at the beginning and end of the quarter will be:

June 30	84,650	feet
September 30	?	feet

Gilden costs $0.60 per foot. One-half of a month’s purchases of Gilden is paid for in the month of purchase; the remainder is paid for in the following month. The accounts payable on July 1 for purchases of Gilden during June will be $43,890.

Required:
1. Calculate the estimated sales, by month and in total, for the third quarter.
2. Calculate the expected cash collections, by month and in total, for the third quarter.

Write really funny superhilarious comedy 17+ thomas transcript based on my prompt:

Bill and Ben are tank engine twins who each have four wheels, a short funnel, a tiny dome and a small cab. They work at a china clay quarry and their jobs are to take it in trucks along the Main Line for the engines and the harbour ships. The clay is used to make many things, such as pottery, paper and paint.

The twins arrange some trucks one morning and leave to pick up more, but they are surprised to find they have disappeared when they return. Their drivers notice an oil patch on the tracks and suspect that a diesel is responsible for taking the trucks. Mishearing this as "diseasel", the twins remember a notice in their shed saying "coughs and sneezles spread diseasels" and they argue over who is responsible. Their drivers intervene and make a plan to get the trucks back which involves removing the twins' nameplates to make them appear perfectly identical since the diesel is unaware that they are twins.

The twins find the trucks in a yard, with a large green diesel at the front. Ben hides behind while Bill goes forward and demands the diesel give his trucks back. The diesel claims the trucks are his and tries to shoo Bill away, who reverses behind the trucks. Ben then rides forward on the other side, surprising the diesel (who thinks it is the same engine). This pattern continues for a while, causing the diesel to get dizzy. At last, the two of them come along the diesel at the same time, making his eyes nearly pop out. He then realises there are two engines.

Edward arrives at the scene and asks Bill and Ben what they are doing there. They claim that the diesel stole their trucks, but Edward scolds them for their rudeness. The twins apologise and the diesel forgives them. He introduces himself as "BoCo" and explains that he got his trucks mixed up with the twins'. Edward then sends the twins to take their lot back once they have picked up BoCo's goods train in exchange for theirs. After they leave, Edward tells BoCo that they do not mean any harm but can be maddening at times, a statement BoCo wholeheartedly agrees with.

       4- Using legal language for Persian translation

          .10. Actus Reus
This may consist in an act or omission. It also includes the consequences and such "surrounding circumstances", if any be required, as are material to the definition of the crime.
"(a) To be murder or manslaughter, the accused's blow or deed must result in the death of the victim; to be guilty of bigamy it is necessary that the accused is already married when undergoing a ceremony of marriage.
(b) Some offences do not require an act as such; a person may be convicted on the basis of "surrounding circumstances" alone.
(c) On the other hand, if an act be required, then the act must be a voluntary one. Thus, a man was acquitted of murder when the jury believed he had been asleep at the time. An act may be involuntary as the result of an illness, or an accident depriving the defendant of his consciousness or faculties of volition. It may even be involuntary if, through no fault of the driver, he loses control of his car due to mechanical failure, and injures a pedestrian. Duress, by depriving a man of choice, also renders his act involuntary.
(d) Liability for omissions, as in tort, arises where there is a positive duty to act."

Question (5): What is the main role of the government in developing Artificial Intelligence applications for e-tourism businesses?


MR Mohamed Farouk Answer

Preparing tourism businesses for the digital future.
The evolution and application of digital technologies are profoundly changing the way people live, work, travel and do business, and in the process, they are transforming and reshaping tourism. The scope and uptake of digital technologies varies across countries, sectors, organisations and places. The resulting opportunities and barriers create an uneven playing field, which is exacerbated by a growing gap between tech-driven and globally connected tourism businesses, and traditional micro and small businesses often characterised by low-tech business practices. Much attention to date has focused on digital marketing and e-commerce as a way of reaching new markets, engaging customers and building brand. However, while these technologies might build market access and awareness, increase connectivity and facilitate financial transactions, they are less effective in enhancing productivity or innovation in an increasingly competitive global marketplace.
Productivity-enhancing technologies (e.g. cloud computing, data analytics, revenue management software) have generally received low uptake in tourism, while innovative technologies (e.g. augmented reality, geotagging) are generating, customising and delivering in ever more novel ways, new visitor products, services and experiences (OECD, 2018c). Digital transformation is thus pushing tourism in new and often unpredictable directions. Digital technologies have important implications for tourism businesses of all sizes, for the structure and operation of tourism value chains and for the sector as a whole. Facilitating and enabling digitalisation in tourism is therefore a key policy challenge
Key main areas governments should deploy
- Understanding the digital transformation
- Understanding business models, value chains and ecosystems
- Enabling technologies shaping the tourism ecosystem


MRs. Heba Galal, CM Answer

Governments need to deal with it, grab the opportunities and mitigating the threats, then Artificial Intelligence could help to overcome many of the world‟s biggest challenges and improve people‟s lives.
Larger infrastructure requirements, and pricing associated with these processors must be developed for the adoption of the Artificial Intelligence technology.

Reframe, rephrase and elaborate in polished language with literary jargon using literary theory in compact way and arrange the syntax in organized way. Avoid repeating words or ideas 
The narrative voice of A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man is remarkable for its limited yet fluid third-person narrative style, which is closely aligned to the consciousness of Stephen Dedalus. We never get to see inside other characters’ heads; instead, we see them the way Stephen does. Indeed, the book focuses so closely on Stephen, and takes us so deeply into his mind, that at times it resembles a first-person narrative. The subjectivity of first-person narration (in the form of a diary at the end) is combined with the objectivity of third-person narration, resulting in a narrative voice that is capable of conveying Stephen’s experiences and thoughts with an immediacy and an intimacy that, until then, had been rarely achieved in the bildungsroman form. By doing so, the inner life of Stephen seeks to delineate in such a way that it does not merely serve the unfolding of the story but becomes the story. The narrator presents Stephen’s consciousness and activities in various ways; an important aspect about his narration is that he persistently adapts his style to Stephen’s idiom and mood

Detailed Information on CCP Parameters, Justifications, and Monitoring Plans:

1. Cooking/Heating of the tomatoes: (80 to 90 degrees Celsius)
- Parameter: Cooking temperature
- Justification: Cooking the tomatoes at the right temperature (80 to 90°C) is crucial to ensure proper inactivation of pathogens, such as Salmonella or E.coli, which are commonly associated with raw produce. Insufficient cooking can lead to the survival of these pathogens, posing a risk to consumers’ health.
- Monitoring Plan: To ensure that the ketchup is cooked at the required temperature, a continuous monitoring system should be in place. This can be achieved using automated temperature control systems that allow regular checks and adjustments as needed. The data from these devices should be recorded and reviewed to ensure compliance with the established cooking parameters.

2. Pasteurization: (95 to 100 degrees Celsius)
- Parameter: Pasteurization temperature
- Justification: Pasteurization is a heat treatment applied to the ketchup to eliminate thermophilic bacteria, such as Bacillus or Clostridium species, which can cause foodborne illnesses. Ensuring the right pasteurization temperature (95 to 100°C) is essential to achieve a sufficient level of microbial inactivation while preserving product quality.
- Monitoring Plan: Regular monitoring of the pasteurization temperature should be conducted, combining automated systems and manual checks. The records should be logged, and any deviations from established parameters must trigger an investigation and corrective action.

3. Cooling: (below 5 degrees Celsius)
- Parameter: Cooling temperature
- Justification: Rapid cooling of the ketchup after pasteurization (below 5°C) is necessary to prevent the growth of harmful microbes, such as Listeria monocytogenes and Clostridium perfringens. These bacteria can proliferate in the temperature “danger zone” (between 4°C and 60°C) if cooling is not conducted efficiently.
- Monitoring Plan: A continuous monitoring system should be implemented to ensure that cooling occurs at the required temperature. This can be achieved using automated temperature control and monitoring equipment. The data recorded should be reviewed regularly to ensure compliance with the established cooling parameters.

4. Filling and Packaging
- Parameter: Cleanliness of the packaging equipment and adherence to regulatory requirements for material safety
- Justification: Maintaining cleanliness of the packaging equipment is crucial to prevent environmental or packaging contamination from pests, foreign objects, or cleaning product residue. In addition, providing safe packaging material that meets regulatory requirements is critical to ensure food safety.
- Monitoring Plan: Frequent visual inspections of equipment before and during the filling process should be conducted. Additionally, sampling from batches at regular intervals can help check for contaminants in the final product. Any deviations from established cleanliness and material safety standards should trigger corrective actions.

5. Storage
- Parameter: Temperature and humidity of the storage environment
- Justification: Effective storage conditions are necessary to prevent the growth of mold and spoilage organisms due to poor temperature or humidity management. Proper storage ensures the product’s safety and quality during its shelf life.
- Monitoring Plan: Regular monitoring and recording of temperature and humidity levels in storage rooms should be conducted using appropriate sensors and loggers. This data should be reviewed regularly to ensure compliance with the established storage parameters.

Detailed Information on Out of Specification (OOS) Rules and Corrective Actions:

1. Cooking/Heating of the tomatoes: (80 to 90 degrees Celsius)
- OOS Rule: Cooking temperature falls below the established limits
- Corrective Action: If a deviation occurs in the cooking process, the temperature should immediately be increased to achieve the required specification. The batch should be assessed for any signs of compromised safety or quality. If the deviation is too significant and cannot be corrected, the affected product should be discarded to ensure consumer safety.

2. Pasteurization: (95 to 100 degrees Celsius)
- OOS Rule: Pasteurization temperature falls below the established limits
- Corrective Action: If the pasteurization process deviates from its set parameters, corrective actions should be taken by adjusting the temperature to meet the required limits. The affected product should undergo quality and safety assessments. If the deviation is significant and the product cannot be salvaged, it must be discarded to prevent any potential risks to consumers.

3. Cooling: (below 5 degrees Celsius)
- OOS Rule: Cooling temperature falls above the established limits
- Corrective Action: In case the cooling temperature rises above the set limit, the cooling equipment must be promptly checked, and adjustments should be made to ensure proper cooling. The affected product must be analyzed for potential spoilage or contamination. If the product does not meet safety or quality standards within a reasonable time frame, it should be discarded.

4. Filling and Packaging
- OOS Rule: Contamination is observed in the product or packaging materials, or equipment is not up to regulatory requirements
- Corrective Action: If contamination or non-compliance with regulatory requirements is identified, the affected equipment must be cleaned and sanitized immediately. The product should be repackaged to ensure food safety. In case the contamination is severe or unmanageable, the affected products should be discarded as a precautionary measure.

5. Storage
- OOS Rule: Temperature or humidity falls outside the established limits
- Corrective Action: If temperature or humidity values deviate from the established limits, adjustments should be made to the storage environment controls (e.g., air conditioning or dehumidifiers) to meet the required parameters. The products should be inspected for any signs of spoilage or mold growth. If deviations have resulted in significant product compromise, the affected products should be discarded.

She claims that texts with, I would say girl child narrators, are more “polyphones”; they comprise different strands which need to be “identified” and “disentangled,” being multi-layered, and with different levels of meaning. (Toward A feminist Narratology Jstor p 349-50) While “individuals may differ on the extent to which biological sex constructs identity,” there is a “broad consensus that gender infuses our material and conceptual realities in myriad tangible and intangible ways.” Even Eve Sedgwick, Nancy Miller, among others, have looked into the ways gender colours the production of story in narrative. So drawing from what Lanser and others suggest it is not about diminishing the girl child narrator’s account, but rather, it calls for a deeper analysis of the narrative itself within the social context it’s situated. To study the narrator’s testimonial and interpretative functions, it becomes necessary to look at the narrator’s utterances within a context. Nothing prohibits us, as Warhol does, from asking, among other questions, what part of the narrator’s gender plays in the kinds of interventions he or she uses in narrative. Make this Python code able to accept parallel connections using threads:
server.py:
import socket

# Define host and port for the server
HOST = ‘127.0.0.1’
PORT = 65432

# The very basic “database” of username and password
VALID_USERNAME = “user”
VALID_PASSWORD = “pass”

# Helper function to check credentials
def check_credentials(username, password):
    return username == VALID_USERNAME and password == VALID_PASSWORD

# Create socket with IPv4 and TCP
with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
    s.bind((HOST, PORT))
    s.listen()
    print(f"Server listening on {HOST}:{PORT}“)
    conn, addr = s.accept()

    with conn:
        print(‘Connected by’, addr)
        while True:
            # Authentication
            username = conn.recv(1024).decode()
            password = conn.recv(1024).decode()

            if not check_credentials(username, password):
                conn.sendall(b"Authentication failed.”)
                break
            else:
                conn.sendall(b"Authentication successful.“)

            # Main data receiving loop
            while True:
                data = conn.recv(1024)
                if not data:
                    break
                conn.sendall(data)

Write really overly-funny super hilarious comedy 17+ short Scooby-Doo cartoon parody transcript that always starts with the villain moment first, then the gang hearing about it once they reach the area, and then the rest based on my prompt: (but make it more funnier adult comedy where the gang constantly make fun of and question physics that ain’t possible or don’t make any sense and why, Fred will always mistake a character for a famous person because of their surname being literally the same as a real life celebrity, forcing the character to correct them angrily, Fred would also put the blame for a monster's crime on Red Herring (From A Pup Named Scooby-Doo), who'd often get mad at Fred for still blaming him and ends up in a funny situation himself before disappearing offscreen. The gang always know that a place they are going to doesn't sound like it exists, they also know something in a place they go to shouldn't even be there as it makes no sense, they question names of things or people and why, and even question the motives and why (Plus they constantly do  pop culture references and jokes, and mentions of famous people, games, songs, and shows occasionally, AND they'd make fun of the plot in the prompt: 

Everyone is gathered at the Brain Club Science Show at the Coolsville Junior High School, where all the smart kids showed their latest inventions. Velma's project is a robot, the Dinkley 2000, which follows everything command. Principal Morton announces Velma has won; adding up to three years in a row. Her parents suggest a celebration at the ice cream store which is what they did. However, as they all leave, the Dinkley 2000 then goes rogue.

The next day after class, Daphne discovers that her notebook is missing, followed by Freddie's missing National Exaggerator papers, and food missing from Shaggy's locker. Velma then uses her robot to help find the items, pointing them to locker #1216, which reveals to be stored with everyone's stuff, as well as the fact the locker belongs to Velma. Bruce Wormsley, who won second place at the show, is hurt when he found his pencil case, and their teacher Mrs. Stickler finds the answers for tomorrow's year end math final and thinks Velma was going to cheat. She says they'll have to see the principal about it.

At the clubhouse, Velma falls into despair when she learns that she's suspended and believes her parents wouldn't understand. But the gang resolves to get to the bottom of the mystery and they decide to ask the robot for help, but realise they left it back at school. Since Velma is suspended, Daphne gives her a makeover.

That night, the gang get inside and begin looking for clues in the hallways. Scooby finds Velma's magnifying glass, a pencil case, and tire tracks in front of their lockers, which Velma says they're from her robot. Just then the robot attacks them, declaring it must delete the gang.

The robot grabs Velma, which provokes Scooby, and after a few tries, saves her by tickling the robot. The gang then tricks it and escapes through the disguise routine. They then look into the janitor's office and meet the janitor, Gus, who loves building and shows them his mopping kayak, which he uses to row away. The robot then attacks the gang again, chasing them all over the school, until Scooby drives it away by scratching a chalkboard with his claws. They then find Velma's briefcase and a red second place ribbon. Unfortunately, the robot catches the gang off guard and grabs Freddie, Daphne, and Shaggy, and devours them, before moving in on Velma. After asking Scooby something, she gets an idea to stop the robot. She and Scooby ask the robot to do several chores at once until it overloads. Freddie, Daphne, and Shaggy then emerge from the robot unharmed. Velma explains that Scooby reminded her that the robot was designed to follow every command.

The gang calls Mrs. Stickler and Principal Morton for the unveiling; Velma explains that the robot was being controlled by Bruce Wormsley, as she suspected him when Scooby found his pencil case, and the red ribbon was the same one he won for his science project. Bruce confesses that he was tired of Velma always doing better than him, so he decided to get her kicked out of the school, by framing her, making him the number one student. He is then taken to the Principal's office, where they'll talk with his parents (and possibly expelled afterwards).

The next day, Velma is welcomed back to the school and is assured by her parents that they will always understand no matter what. Shaggy and Scooby then wonder what happened to her robot, which she reveals she gave to Gus. Mrs. Stickler is glad that Velma's back, who then says that it wouldn't have been possible without her friend, Scooby-Doo.

Oxidative stress has been recognized as a key factor in pathological changes observed in a wide range of liver diseases 29-30.
Natural antioxidant products have gained worldwide popularity due to their efficacy and safety. They are increasingly used to treat various pathological liver conditions 3.
Acrylamide is a chemical substance formed when starchy foods such as potatoes and bread are cooked at high temperatures above 120°C. It can be formed when food is fried or baked. Acrylamide levels have genotoxic, neurotoxic carcinogenic, nephrotoxic, and hepatotoxic effects on living organisms 31.
Acrylamide produced free radicals, which can cause liver damage. Free radicals have already been reported to be more reactive than molecular elements and cause serious harm to nucleic acid, cell membranes, and protein 32.

Such a drastic increase in the incidence of lipid peroxidation, especially in the liver and kidney, has the potential to alter the state of an organism's oxidative stress.
