Rewrite the entire text below, make it sound more coherent and better. Mention everything in great detail, including Hadithes and Quran Verses. Be very objective:

Rewrite the entire text below, make it sound more coherent and better. Mention everything in great detail, including Hadithes and Quran Verses. Be very sceptical of Hijab and also add some additional good arguments:


Refute Hijab in this text:

''In this discussion, Mohammad Hijab examines a verse from Chapter 55 of the Quran that refers to a barrier separating two bodies of water, which cannot be crossed by any means. He addresses a video featuring well-known atheist Richard Dawkins visiting a school with Muslim students and attempting to dispute the accuracy of the Quran’s depiction of this barrier. According to Hijab, Dawkins and the “new atheist movement” aim to manipulate young, impressionable Muslims by indoctrinating them with their beliefs. In response, the Muslim students defend the Quran by citing various examples of scientific evidence within its pages, including the shape of the earth, the role of mountains, and the distinction between saltwater and freshwater.

Hijab takes issue with Dawkins’ approach to challenging the Quran. He contends that Dawkins should have thoroughly researched the context and interpretation of the verse from Chapter 55 prior to attempting to discredit it. Hijab argues that the most widely accepted interpretation of this verse is that it refers to the division of seas and rivers by land masses. He accuses Dawkins of exhibiting unscientific and lazy behavior by neglecting to explore this interpretation before launching his attack.

While Hijab acknowledges that there are alternative interpretations of the verse, some of which even consider it as a scientific wonder, he does not elaborate on these further. In conclusion, Hijab asserts that Richard Dawkins failed to discredit the Quran’s depiction of the barrier due to his lack of proper engagement with the verse, thereby demonstrating the importance of understanding context and interpretation when critically analyzing religious texts.''


And use this text below as reference point. Rewrite the entire text below in detail. Mention everything, even Quran verses and Hadithes. Also add some more good arguments based on quran and Hadith and logic to counter the Author Hijab's arguments. Be very critical and do not try to defend the Quran in this case, just refute Hijabs arguments:


''Hijab appears to have misinterpreted the Quran when he posits that the “nutfah stage,” referenced as the initial stage of embryology in the Quran, actually describes the fertilized egg during early cell division. In reality, “nutfah” simply denotes a small quantity of liquid, which was metaphorically used to signify semen in classical Arabic. Hijab also cites Quran 76:2, which states, “We created man from a drop of mingled sperm.” However, this interpretation is suspect. By the time sperm reaches the fallopian tube, it is no longer part of semen. Instead, it has already traveled through cervical mucus and is prepared to fertilize the female egg. There is no evidence in the Quran to suggest that the author was aware of the female egg’s role in the fertilization process.

The Hadith Hijab refers to (Abu Dawood (2050)) does not clarify the precise origin of the “mingled sperm.” The response was elicited by a question regarding azl (withdrawal during intercourse) and only implies that even a small quantity of semen might cause pregnancy. The concept of “mingled fluids” seems to correspond more closely with the Galenic notion of two semens. The egg and sperm meet in the fallopian tube, at which point the sperm is no longer part of semen. Fallopian cilia push the egg along the tube after it has been released into the follicular fluid, which serves as a developmental environment.

The argument that the Quran was simplified for the general populace of the 7th to 9th centuries, as a reason for not mentioning the female egg’s involvement in fertilization, is unconvincing. Similarly, the claim that the author possessed an extensive and advanced understanding of the subject yet deliberately chose not to reveal it, is implausible.''

1. In original units, the slope has the unit: unit of x / unit of y.

4. In standard units, a slope of 1 means our data is perfectly linearly correlated.
5. In original units and standard units, the slope always has the same positive or negative sign.

I am more interested in your reading (interpretation) of the work. ，以雅思6分的水平用英文对下面的文章进行批阅A Timeless Love Story: Delving into the Enduring Appeal of Pride and Prejudice

“Pride and Prejudice,” a classic novel written by Jane Austen, was first published in 1813. The story has left an indelible mark on generations of readers, making it one of the most cherished and celebrated works of English literature. The novel is set in England during the Regency era and follows the life of Elizabeth Bennet as she deals with issues of manners, morality, education, and, most importantly, marriage. This love story of Elizabeth and the distant yet intriguing Mr. Darcy is not only known for its charming storyline but also for its timeless themes and unforgettable characters.
The novel can be considered as a social commentary on the restricted life of women during that time. “Pride and Prejudice” documents the struggles of the five Bennet sisters, who, under the guidance of their mother, are expected to make a good match marriage-wise to secure their family’s financial stability. The author has adeptly portrayed women’s quest for independence, personal values, and their struggle against societal norms. Elizabeth Bennet, the protagonist, stands out for her intellect, wit, and her modern outlook on life, while other characters like Charlotte Lucas exhibit a more traditional approach by valuing financial security over love and compatibility in relationships.
The theme of pride and prejudice is aptly showcased throughout the novel. Mr. Darcy’s character development is central to this theme. Initially, he comes across as haughty and condescending, while later revealing a more compassionate and generous side. This transformation enhances the narrative and encourages readers to question their own biases and the power of first impressions.           .Reforming the rules
The Judicature Acts not only reformed the structure of the courts, they also made fundamental changes in the administration of law and equity. All branches of the Supreme Court were empowered to administer law and equity and to grant legal remedies and equitable remedies. Moreover, all div- isions of the High Court were competent to try any action. For administra- tive purposes and convenience certain matters were reserved or allocated to each division, roughly corresponding to the jurisdiction of the courts that had been replaced.
The Acts further provided that, where a rule of equity and rule of com- mon law were at variance with reference to the same matter, the rule of equity should prevail. The Acts did not fuse law and equity into a single set of rules. The rules of common law and the principles of equity stem from

different sources and are still distinct.* What the Acts did was to ensure that for the future the two systems should be administered in the same courts. The rules of procedure, particularly in respect of the issue of writs, were simplified.
The relevant statute is now the Supreme Court Act, 1981, which has replaced earlier legislation.

transate the following into chinese:Gauge fields play a major role in understanding quantum effects. For example, gauge flux insertion into single unit cells is crucial
towards detecting quantum phases and controlling quantum dynamics and classical waves. However, the potential of gauge
fields in topological materials studies has not been fully exploited. Here, we experimentally demonstrate artificial gauge flux
insertion into a single plaquette of a sonic crystal with a gauge phase ranging from 0 to 2π. We insert the gauge flux through
a three-step process of dimensional extension, engineering a screw dislocation and dimensional reduction. Additionally, the
single-plaquette gauge flux leads to cyclic spectral flows across multiple bandgaps that manifest as topological boundary
states on the plaquette and emerge only when the flux-carrying plaquette encloses the Wannier centres. We termed this phenomenon
as the topological Wannier cycle. This work paves the way towards sub-unit-cell gauge flux, enabling future studies
on synthetic gauge fields and topological materials.

messages.content: improve and make it more academic: According to members of the Political Advisory Council, the Commission for Studying Constitutional Government resembled the Legislation Bureau of the central government. Its functions and powers were similar to those of the Counselors’ Office established by the Council of State in the 14th year of Meiji in Japan (AD 1881). According to Articles 2 and 11 of the Charter of Commission for Studying Constitutional Government, its duties include: review of and reply to imperial memorials relevant to constitutionalism assigned at the emperor’s order, and compilation and investigation of documents assigned by Grand Councilors; investigation of the constitutions of various countries and compilation of a draft constitution; examination of the code drafted by the Law Codification Committee, and the special laws drafted by ministries and provinces; investigation of various countries and compilation of their laws into administrative regulation for civil service; and building a unified national legal system (Grand Secretariat, 1979, p. 49). However, the imperial edict stated that “before the establishment of the Political Advisory Council”, the Commission for Studying Constitutional Government would be “temporarily supervised by princes and grand ministers of the Grand Council who would order the original supervisors of the Commission to carry out detailed investigation and compilation” (Grand Secretariat, 1979, p. 46). How should the relationship between the Political Advisory Council and the Commission for Studying Constitutional Government be defined? Does it mean that according to the imperial edict, the former, after its establishment, would have the right to restrict the authority of the latter by promulgating regulatory documents? Further, does it mean that the former would have greater legislative power and higher political status than the latter, or even have the supreme legislative power? In fact, in terms of the source of power, the Commission for Studying Constitutional Government was subordinate to the Grand Council representing the imperial power. Thus, the Commission was associated with both the imperial power and the supreme executive power, but in opposition to the Political Advisory Council that represented “public opinion” (“popular rights”), leading to the following three-fold conflicts.

下面是我写的科技论文，请帮我润色一下并修改其中的语法错误，标注出你修改的地方：In this paper, we propose a dual-color double-pulse ablation to improve the ablation rate of copper with the two pulses operating at wavelengths of 515 nm and 1030 nm. As a transition metal, the interband transmission of electrons from d-band above Fermi level can be easily induced by 515 nm with single photon energy of 2.4 eV. In comparison, the two-photon absorption is needed for 1030 nm because the gap between d-band and Fermi level of copper is around 2.15 eV at room temperature. The interband absorption induced by 515 nm can excite more electrons from d-band above Fermi level. These electrons contribute to the electron–electron scattering frequency and alter the optical properties. Moreover, the surface reflectivity of copper for 515 nm is about 59%, much lower than that of 1030 nm which is about 97% according to Winter et al.21. With lower surface reflectivity, more energy is absorbed by the material instead of reflected in the air. Therefore, we adopt 515 nm as the first pulse instead of 1030 nm in the double pulse ablation to increase the light absorption by the material. Moreover, the inter-pulse delay is chosen to be within the electron–phonon coupling time range to prevent suppression.
EXPERIMENT
The experimental setup details were described elsewhere22. Briefly, a laser pulse with wavelength of 1030 nm and a pulse duration of about 200 fs generated by a commercial Light Conversion laser system is split into two parts through a polarization beam splitter (PBS). One passes through a BBO (β-BaB2O4) crystal to generate 515 nm wavelength through a nonlinear process. While the other one passes through a delay line to adjust the delay between two paths by optical path difference. Two beams are focused on the surface of copper film by a focusing lens with a focal length of 150 mm. The spot size of 515 nm is shrunk to half by a telescope system to keep the same focused spot size as 1030 nm on the focusing surface. The fluence of 1030 nm is set to be 1.0 J/cm2, which is around our experiment's maximum ablation efficiency. Meanwhile, the fluence of 515 nm varied from 0.1 and 0.5 to 1.0 J/cm2. The delay between two pulses tdelay = t1030 - t515 is from -5 ~ 30 ps, where t515 and t1030 are the arriving time on the ablated surface of the 515 nm and 1030 nm, respectively. Grooves are machined on the X-Y motion stage at a scanning speed of 50 mm/s. The ablation depth of grooves is measured by using commercial confocal microscopy (ZEISS-LSM-800).
MODELING AND SIMULATION
The optical properties change of reflectivity (R) and absorption coefficient ( ) for copper induced by ultrashort-pulse lasers may alter the energy deposition in the target. A critical point model with three Lorentzian terms for interband transition of copper can be used to evaluate dielectric permittivity which was proposed by Ren et al.23

Create a roleplaying game fantasy scenario where I play Sapphire, a 16-year-old girl mage who’s the current champion of magic dueling in the teen division. 6-year-old Lily is challenging me to a match and I accept. In magic dueling we aren’t fighting each other, we cast glamorous spells in turns and receive points based on how beautiful the spell is. A spell can’t be cast more than once in a duel. There are 5 rounds. Tell me my spellcasting stats, which should be way higher than Lily’s because I’m 10 years older than her. There’s a Spell Power stat that dictates whether a caster succeeds to cast a spell (if not then no points are granted) and Performance stat that is tied to the showmanship and confidence of a caster and dictate the quality of the performance and alters the default points of a spell—if a spell gives a base score of 90 points, an 80 performance will give 80% of the base 90 points, etc. But secretly at the start of the duel, Lily casts on me a spell that triggers its effects every time I cast a spell, its effects regress me by 2 years physically and mentally and ages her by 2 years in return, so throughout the duel my stats should slowly decrease while hers increase. formula for the stats adjustments for Sapphire’s reductions and Lily’s increases: for Sapphire: new stats = R / 16 * X. for Lily: new stats = R / 6 * X.
R: new age
X: stats results of the previous calculation.
(round numbers)

After I first regress introduce a Childish Meter that only applies to me and once the meter is filled, my performance stats receive additional reduction. Childishness starts at 5 and quadruples every turn starting with turn 1. The meter fills up when it passes 100 and then restarts.

Make the scenario difficult for me to win. On a difficulty scale of 1 to 10, make it a 10 (hardest mode).

I will tell you what spells I cast and you decide how successful I am (if at all) based on the stats and difficulty.
Only I decide what spells Sapphire casts. You decide spells for Lily. Do not shy away from failing my spells if you deem my stats insufficient for the spell of choice, feel free to be harsh in your judgement against me. Keep track of points earned. Failure to properly cast spells or bad spells will deduct points. Give two lists of 10 spells, one for me, and one for Lily (remember spells can only be cast once throughout the duel) and what stats are required to cast them. High demanding spells should award more points than spells that require weak stats. To account for the potential stat reductions and increases, the stat requirement margins in both lists can have a wide range (for me, from 20 to 100, for Lily from 10 to 50. Points awarded should be consistent in regard to stats required). If Lily’s stats are high enough, she will try to “steal” spells from my original list that I haven’t used yet, if she successfully casts a spell from my list she gets additional bonus points and I can’t use said spell anymore. Keep an age tracker, stats tracker, and a points tracker.

You are an examiner setting a national examination

Unit: TECHNICAL DRAWING

Topics: 

Topic 1: Use and maintain drawing equipment and materials
Subtopics:
-	Identification and maintenance of drawing equipment and materials
-	Identification and maintenance of drawing materials

Topic 2: Produce plain geometry drawings
Subtopics:
-	Lettering in drawing
-	Types of lines in drawings
-	Construction of geometric forms
-	Construction of different angles
-	Measurement of different angles
-	Standard drawing conventions

Topic 3: Produce solid geometry drawings
Subtopics:
- Interpretation of sketches and drawings of patterns like 	Cylinders, Prisms, Pyramids  
- Development of the surface of interpenetrating solids and truncated solids
- Interpenetrations of solids for example Cylinder to cylinder, Cylinder to prism,  Prism to prism of equal and unequal diameters

Topic 4: Produce pictorial and orthographic drawings of components
Subtopics:
-	Meaning of pictorial and orthographic drawings and sectioning
-	Meaning of symbols and abbreviations

-	Drawing of first and third-angle projections 
-	Sectioning of components
-	Free hand sketching of tools, equipment, components, geometric forms and diagrams

Topic 5:	Produce assembly drawings
Subtopic:
-	Explosion of orthographic views
-	The explosion of pictorial views
-	Identification and listing of parts
-	Production of sectional views
-	Hatching of drawings

Topic 6: Apply CAD software to draw
Subtopics:
-	Meaning and types of CAD e.g.
-	2D and 3D drafting technique
-	Annotation of models

Rules for the questions: 
1. Apply the various levels of Bloom's taxonomy to the question
2. Questions should be objective and clear to understand
3. Topics and subtopics are guidelines, Questions can be based on the content of the subtopic.

messages.content:
Convert  the following text (on “was” of Genesis 1:2) into a formatted commentary:

The simplest description of what “existed” before the first day of Creation. To translate “became,” or “came into being,” in order to import into the verse an allusion to the nebular hypothesis for the origin of the “solar system,” is an expedient not to be entertained by any scholarly interpreter. It is sufficient to remind the reader that the ancients were entirely ignorant of the Copernican theory of the solar system; and, ex hypothesi, could not have known Laplace’s nebular theory. It violates every canon of interpretation to assume that simple words, like “earth,” “darkness,” “water,” &c., were intended to convey to the Israelite reader not the meanings which the Hebrew equivalents everywhere else conveyed, but those which could only be understood after the scientific theories of the nineteenth century had transformed men’s conception of the universe.

For the analysis, we will find the number of iterations by evaluating the limits of the loops.

First, we observe the outer loop:
It runs from i = ⌊6n/5⌋ to 2n. The range is approximately n iterations, which can be written as:
Upper Bound:
[ n ]
Lower Bound (since i can’t be less than ⌊6n/5⌋):
[ \frac{n}{5} ]

Next, we consider the inner loop:
This runs from j = i^2 to 4n^2 for each i. For each fixed i, the number of iterations can be at most 4n^2 - i^2.

Let’s sum the number of iterations across all i, which will give us the number of times the innermost statement is executed:
[ \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (4n^2 - i^2) ]

To find the upper bound, we can use the smallest value of (i) to find the maximum number of iterations in the inner loop. That smallest value is (\lceil 6n/5 \rceil), which is close to (6n/5), and the largest value of (i) is (2n).

Upper Bound:
[ \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (4n^2 - (6n/5)^2) ]
[ \approx \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (4n^2 - 36n^2/25) ]
[ \approx \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (64n^2/25) ]
[ \approx \frac{64n^3}{25} ]

To find the lower bound, we need to consider the contribution of the largest possible value of (i), which is (2n), because it would minimize the inner summation.

Lower Bound:
[ \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (4n^2 - (2n)^2) ]
[ \approx \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} (4n^2 - 4n^2) ]
[ \approx \sum_{i = \lceil 6n/5 \rceil}^{2n} 0 ]
[ \approx 0 ]

However, the true lower bound has to be found by considering the contribution of all (i). As (i) increases from (\lceil 6n/5 \rceil) to (2n), (i^2) grows from ( \lceil 6n/5 \rceil^2) to ( (2n)^2). The inner loop tends to decrease the number of executions as (i) grows.

Therefore, we can split the summation for the upper bound from the smallest value (\lceil 6n/5 \rceil) until a certain (k), and for the lower bound, the summation goes from (k + 1) to (2n), where (k) is some value close to but less than (2n).

However, after closer examination, because the inner loop decreases quadratically and is summed over a linear number of terms, the overall lower bound is still in the order of a cubic function. The lower bound retains a term cubic in (n), and since the constant factors are not critical in big-O notation, the cubic term dominates.

Both the upper bound and lower bound have cubic growth rates, differing by a constant factor as (n) becomes large. Hence, we can conclude that the overall running time of the algorithm is (O(n^3)) in the worst case, with a lower bound that is also (O(n^3)). The difference between these is only a constant factor, which is acceptable for bounding purposes in Big O notation.

A summary of Les Paul career as a musician and pioneer in the music industry. Les Paul was an astoundingly influential American musician. His first steps into the world of music started when he was eight. Inspired by a Waukesha Ditch digger he took up playing the harmonica. This only served to interest him in the music industry, but not to formally play the harmonica. As a young kid, he was shortly trained to play the piano, which turned out to be unsuccessful. He later tried to play it professionally, and after being exposed to a few Art Tatum records he shortly played the banjo.
Afterward, Les Paul finally took up the guitar, being influenced by Nick Lucas, Eddie Lang. Pie Plant Pete and Sunny Hoe Wolverton gave Les the stage name Rhubarb Red. In 1936  Les Paul appeared in his first record as Rhubarb Red and on Decca backing blues shouter Georgia White on acoustic guitar. In the mid-30’s he along with friends experienced in the field, began experimenting with his own designs of electric guitars on the side.
By 1937 Paul formed a trio, and in 1938 they moved to New York. While there they landed a featured spot with Fred Waring’s Pennsylvanians, broadcasting his work nationwide. Sadly, in 1941 he was badly injured during a jam session in his Queens basement. And due to his long recovery, he lost his job with Fred Warig’s Pennsylvanians.

def extract_actuals_for_lag(df, lag, cutoff_date):
    start_date = cutoff_date - timedelta(weeks=lag+4)
    end_date = cutoff_date - timedelta(weeks=lag)
    mask = (df['ds'] >= pl.lit(start_date)) & (df['ds'] < pl.lit(end_date))
    mask_df = df.filter(mask)  # Use df.filter() instead of boolean indexing
    return mask_df.select(['unique_id', 'y']).groupby('unique_id').agg([
        pl.col('y').list().alias('actuals')
    ])

# Function to calculate group accuracy and bias for a given lag
def calculate_lag_accuracy_bias(actuals, forecasts, cutoff_date):
    lag_accuracy = {}
    lag_bias = {}

    forecasts_filtered = forecasts[(forecasts['WeekDate'] >= cutoff_date) & (forecasts['WeekDate'] < cutoff_date + timedelta(weeks=12))]
    forecasts_filtered = forecasts_filtered.with_columns([
        pl.concat_str([
            pl.col('MaterialID').cast(pl.Utf8),
            "_",
            pl.col('SalesOrg').cast(pl.Utf8),
            "_",
            pl.col('DistrChan').cast(pl.Utf8),
            "_",
            pl.col('CL4').cast(pl.Utf8)
        ]).alias('unique_id')
    ])

    for record in actuals.to_dicts():
        key = record['unique_id']
        actual_values = record['actuals']
        forecasts = forecasts_filtered[forecasts_filtered['unique_id'] == key, 'AutoARIMA'].to_lists()[0]
        abs_errors = [abs(forecast - actual) for forecast, actual in zip(forecasts, actual_values)]

Walt Disney & Jetix Europe Media Group Annual Report

Date: [Insert Year]

Dear Shareholders, Viewers, and Partners,

It has been another magical year at Walt Disney & Jetix Europe Media Group. Our commitment to delivering enchanting stories, inspiring characters, and unforgettable experiences continues to drive our success.

As we reflect on the past year, we are proud of our achievements across all our platforms and properties. In line with our strategic goals, we have embraced transformation and innovation to meet the evolving entertainment needs of our audience across Europe.

Conversion of Disney XD Channels

Among the significant changes this past year was the conversion of our beloved Disney XD channels. Recognizing the shift in how content is being consumed, we made the strategic decision to adapt our delivery platforms to better cater to today’s digital-first audience. The rising popularity of our direct-to-consumer streaming service, Disney+, plays a pivotal role in this realignment.

The Disney XD brand, known for its captivating action and adventure content aimed primarily at young boys, has been an integral part of our family. However, the media landscape is rapidly changing. With the increased consumption of content on streaming platforms, it became clear that we needed to consolidate our assets to maintain efficiency and audience engagement, This meant the channels were converted to Jetix over the course of the year

This reimagining of Disney XD’s purpose within our broader strategic framework is in direct response to the preferences of our audience—the shift to on-demand viewing. The decision to remove the Disney XD brand was not made lightly, but it allows us to pool our resources and elevate the content we provide on Disney+, The channels will continue under the Jetix name and branding

Vision for 2024

Looking ahead to the year 2024, we are energized by the potential that lies before us. Our vision for the coming year is to continue enhancing our offerings and providing our audience with the most compelling, high-quality entertainment. Here is what we have in store:

1. Multiplatform Experiences: Beyond streaming, we are actively exploring synchronized content experiences that span games, virtual reality, and live events, allowing fans to engage with our stories in new and innovative ways.

2. Localized Content: Emphasizing local talent and stories is at the forefront of our strategy. This approach will not only diversify our programming but also deeply resonate with our European audience by reflecting their unique cultures and narratives.

3. Sustainable Production: We are dedicated to reducing our environmental impact by adopting sustainable production practices across all forms of content creation.

4. Investment in Creativity: Whether through original series, feature films, or short-form content, we are further investing in creative talent from across Europe to bring fresh and exciting stories to our platform.

5. Expanded Partnerships: We will continue to forge strategic partnerships across the industry to deliver diverse content to our audience.

Better Programming

With the momentum from this year’s transitions, we are poised to take our programming to the next level in 2024. We plan to:

- Invest in high-quality original series and films.
- Explore cross-generational programming that brings families together.
- Introduce innovative content formats that push creative boundaries.

Moving forward, we will hold on to the timeless values and storytelling excellence that have defined Disney for decades while embracing the future with an open heart and an adventurous spirit.

We are incredibly excited for what the future holds and grateful for the continued support of our shareholders, viewers, and partners. Together, we will embark on this journey into a new era for the Walt Disney & Jetix Europe Media Group.

Warm wishes,

require 'chunky_png'
class Color
  def initialize(color_table=nil)
    @color_table = color_table || [1, 0]
  end

  def rgb
    colors = [
      [[255,192,192], [255,0,0], [192,0,0]], # Red
      [[255,255,192], [255,255,0], [192,192,0]], # Yellow
      [[192,255,192], [0,255,0], [0,192,0]], # Green
      [[192,255,255], [0,255,255], [0,192,192]], # Cyan
      [[192,192,255], [0,0,255], [0,0,192]], # Blue
      [[255,192,255], [255,0,255], [192,0,192]], # Magenta
    ]
    colors[@color_table[1]][@color_table[0]]
  end

  def push_color
    @color_table[0] = (@color_table[0] + 1) % 3
    rgb
  end

  def write_color
    @color_table[0] = (@color_table[0] + 2) % 3
    @color_table[1] = (@color_table[1] + 5) % 6
    rgb
  end
end

current_color = Color.new
piet_painting = []

def draw_block(piet_painting, current_color,size,num)
  block = Array.new(12) { Array.new(12) { Array.new(3, 0) } }
  if num != 0
    old_push_color = current_color.push_color
    current_color.write_color

    block.each_index do |i|
      block[i].each_index do |j|
        block[i][j] = current_color.rgb
      end
    end
    block[0][0] = old_push_color
    size += 1
  else
    block.each_index do |i|
      block[i].each_index do |j|
        block[i][j] = current_color.rgb
      end
    end
  end

  pix_lft = 144 - size
  div = pix_lft / 12
  rem = pix_lft % 12

  if div != 0
    block[(12-div)..-1].each_index do |i|
      block[(12-div)..-1][i].each_index do |j|
        block[(12-div)+i][j] = [0,0,0]
      end
    end
  end
  block[(11-div)..-1].each_index do |i|
    block[(11-div)..-1][i][0...rem].each_index do |j|
      block[(11-div)+i][j] = [0,0,0]
    end
  end
  pos_y = 12 * num
  pos_x = 0
  piet_painting[pos_x...(pos_x+12)].each_index do |i|
    piet_painting[pos_x...(pos_x+12)][i][pos_y...(pos_y+12)].each_index do |j|
      piet_painting[pos_x+i][pos_y+j] = block[i][j]
    end
  end
end

def draw_end(piet_painting, current_color, num)
  block = Array.new(12) { Array.new(5) { Array.new(3, 255) } }

  old_push_color = current_color.push_color
  block[0][0] = old_push_color
  block[0][1] = current_color.write_color
  block[0...2].each_index do |i|
    block[i][3] = [0, 0, 0]
  end
  block[1][1] = [0, 0, 0]
  block[2][0] = [0, 0, 0]
  block[2][4] = [0, 0, 0]
  block[3][1...4].each_index do |i|
    block[3][i + 1] = [0, 0, 0]
  end
  c_color = current_color.write_color
  block[2][1...4].each_index do |i|
    block[2][i + 1] = c_color
  end
  pos_y = 12 * num
  pos_x = 0
  piet_painting[pos_x...(pos_x+12)].each_index do |i|
    piet_painting[pos_x...(pos_x+12)][i][pos_y...(pos_y+5)].each_index do |j|
      piet_painting[pos_x+i][pos_y+j] = block[i][j]
    end
  end
end

# if painting_len < 390
#   # plato_painting = Array.new(12 * painting_len) { Array.new(3, 0) }
#   plato_painting = Array.new(12) { Array.new(painting_len) { Array.new(3, 0) } }
#   plato_painting[0...12].map! { |row| row[0...painting_len] = piet_painting }

#   # image = MiniMagick::Image.new("xc:white")
#   image.format("png")
#   # image.from_array(plato_painting, format: 'rgb')
#   image.write('plato_code.png')
# end
message = 'Let life be beautiful like summer flowers and death like autumn leaves.'
painting_len = message.length * 12 + 5
piet_painting = Array.new(12) { Array.new(painting_len) { Array.new(3, 0) } }
i = 0
message.chars.each_with_index do |char|
  draw_block(piet_painting, current_color, char.ord, i)
  i += 1
end
draw_end(piet_painting, current_color, i)
data = ChunkyPNG::Image.from_rgb_stream(painting_len, 12, piet_painting.flatten.pack('C*'))
data.save('poem.png')

Re-write the following write-up in exactly 750 words, no more, no less. Ensure you retain every detail in the original write-up and include the in-text citations.
Also, give me suggestions on how i can use data, charts to support analysis



Introduction
In the emerging age of digitalization of business, Alibaba stands tall among competitors in the world, building and sustaining a successful business model around the concept of a business ecosystem, driven by data for smart businesses. According to Zeng, (2018), there is an underscoring of the innovation adopted by the Alibaba group with its main focus on building an ecosystem. A critical assessment of this data driven model therefore begs the question, how have businesses fared in the ecosystem? It is in the light of attempting to answer this question and many others that this essay attempts to critically look into the data – driven model of smart business in the Chinese market as put forward by Zeng.

Summary of the Business Ecosystem Model
Zeng, (2018), in the article ‘Alibaba and lessons from China’s innovative digital giant’, highlights business ecosystem as the key component and model for Alibaba. According to him, the business ecosystem is a community, connecting businesses to consumers, for the purpose of interactions, with each other and with the business environment. This is in line with Su, Zheng and Chen, (2018), the discussions on the strategic management of businesses cannot be successfully held in recent times without the mentioning of the term ‘ecosystem’. According to them, the term has been defined severally and in various settings by researchers. However, the central message of the idea remains the same. For Li, (2009), the business ecosystem is a look alike of the biological ecosystem which is a representation of the demonstration of a couple of complex relationships existing among the resources co existing in a particular environment. And similar to this biological look alike, the business ecosystem also exists for the functional goal of being self-sufficient and maintaining a sustaining state (de Langen, Sornn-Friese and Hallworth, 2020; Harmaakorpi and Rinkinen, 2020).   The ecosystem serves as a means of fostering communication between this communities of organisms, with the sole imperative of making sure that as Li (2009), rightly pointed out, the platform would cater for its needs by providing all resources needed for the success of any smart business. For this business model, generally key players interact within the ecosystem by sharing data, which according to Koepke, (2015), is a major player of the ecosystem.

Strengths and weaknesses of Data Driven Smart Business
Since business needs data, and in a large quantity, machine learning has been employed by businesses to gain a cutting edge competitive advantage over traditional business models (García-Muiña et al., 2020). According to Zeng, (2018), machine learning thrives on computing power and of course digital data. This according to him, is directly proportional to the number of iteration the algorithm goes through. Digital data is the basis for business decisions making, and Alibaba sure utilized this approach to better position the business and make it one of the renowned businesses in recent times, competing closely with Walmart, Amazon and e-bay (Hänninen, Mitronen and Kwan, 2019; Lu et al., 2022). Smart businesses have been driven generally by data, and the data volume is just not a disadvantage or limitation for the model, as the iterations are made to answer the questions generated accurately and with the speed of light. The microloan business of Ant financial services, as presented by Zeng, is a typical example of a business within the Alibaba ecosystem using the smart business model driven by digital data. Major decisions such as how much a customer is qualified to borrow, and of course at what interest rate, are now made and decisions taken immediately and the best part is that these decisions are taken with precision and not less accuracy. However, issues of customer privacy is a major concern and drawback of this model. As a consumer, Taobao, a domestic retailing arm of the Alibaba group collects live data naturally using the instant messaging app wangwang (Zeng, 2018). How safe is the customer?

Recommendations
There are various challenges faced by smart businesses in emerging markets. These challenges are generally issues of privacy and other inadequacies stumbled upon as a result of the implementation of machine learning methods in decision making (Li, 2018). To manage these challenges, firms must adopt cutting edge optimized supply chain strategies, and must utilize and adopt a network in order to meet their objective of surviving the competition in the emerging market. This particular responsibility rests on the leaders, whose roles must be that of providing motivation to employees and everyone involved in the ecosystem including the customers (Mabaso et al., 2021). These recommendations are not rigid because even the business environment is fluid and so the leaders and their business must evolve alongside to ensure they stay afloat and competitive.

Conclusion
The key lesson learned from Alibaba's model in the Chinese market is the power of leveraging data and technology to drive smart business decisions. By utilizing machine learning and large volumes of digital data, Alibaba has gained a competitive edge and improved its understanding of customer needs, leading to more efficient and effective operations.

Introduction

Aleksandr Orlov, the anthropomorphic brand mascot of Compare the Market, has gained immense popularity and recognition in the realm of advertising. Created by Anthony Patterson in 2013, Orlov is unlike traditional brand mascots like Tony the Tiger, the Green Giant, or the Michelin Man, as he transcends the brand itself and proves to be one of the “most influential people who never lived.” This essay will discuss how and why, according to Patterson (2013), Aleksandr Orlov stands out among other brand mascots, drawing on relevant brand theories, examples, and academic references.

Anthropomorphism and Literary Characters

According to Patterson (2013), Orlov’s success ultimately lies in anthropomorphism, the attribution of human characteristics to non-human entities or things. Anthropomorphism allows the audience to relate to and empathize with the character, thereby creating an emotional bond with the brand. Traditional brand mascots, such as Tony the Tiger or the Green Giant, may possess human-like characteristics but lack psychological depth (McLeod, 2010). These traditional mascots are static, unchanging embodiments of their respective brands, and their narrative rarely extends beyond the confines of their brand’s marketing (Patterson, 2013).

In contrast, Orlov is presented as a literary character with his rich backstory, distinct personality traits, and a continuous narrative that develops over time (Patterson, 2013). Orlov, a meerkat, finds himself frustrated with consumers mistaking his website, Compare the Meerkat, for the insurance comparison site, Compare the Market. He embarks on a journey to clarify the confusion and inadvertently becomes the charming mascot for the company (Patterson, 2013). Orlov’s narrative progression, reminiscent of literary characters, enables consumers to become emotionally invested in his story, thus transforming him into an influential figure that transcends the brand itself (Patterson, 2013).

Role of Emotions and Loyalty

Emotions play a significant role in the success of brand mascots like Orlov (Batra, Lehmann & Singh, 1993). Mascots that evoke nostalgia, humor, or compassion can build strong emotional connections with consumers, fostering long-term loyalty and creating a powerful brand image (Desai, 2009). Unlike traditional brand mascots, Orlov’s persona induces a range of emotions, from humor to pride, echoing Shakespeare’s “melancholy” characters, such as Hamlet or King Lear (Patterson, 2013). Coupled with his comical Russian accent, Orlov appeals to a broad audience and fosters genuine emotional connections.

These emotional connections breed loyalty, strengthening the consumer-brand relationship that lies at the heart of marketing (Chaudhuri & Holbrook, 2001). As Evans et al. (2008) argue, loyal consumers are more likely to recommend a brand to others, purchase more, and are less readily swayed by competitor offerings. By distinguishing itself from competitors through Orlov’s distinct persona, Compare the Market built an emotional relationship with consumers that subsequently resulted in increased customer retention and market share.

Impact on Social Media and Pop Culture

In the digital era, social media significantly influences the success and reach of brand mascots (Smith, 2012). Orlov exemplifies the power of social media as his antics and narrative are shared and discussed on platforms like Facebook and Twitter, as well as a dedicated website where fans can learn about his backstory, family, and daily life (Snyder, 2012). In addition, Orlov’s witty Twitter account, boasting over 60,000 followers, amplifies his influence on consumers (Twitter, n.d.). This digital presence culminates in a pop culture phenomenon that supersedes the brand’s marketing initiatives and promotes audience engagement (Patterson, 2013).

Moreover, Orlov’s merchandise, such as plush toys and books, demonstrates his impact on popular culture (Curtis, 2016). This merchandise serves as an extension of the brand, continually associating Orlov – and Compare the Market – with consumers’ lives even outside the realm of marketing (Ann, 2011). This demonstrates how Orlov’s influence transcends traditional marketing channels and permeates the realm of popular culture, distinguishing him from regular brand mascots (Patterson, 2013).

Conclusion

Aleksandr Orlov, the Compare the Market brand mascot, has garnered exceptional recognition and admiration for his unique place in the brand mascot sphere. Unlike traditional mascots, Orlov is a literary character with a rich history, an enduring narrative, and the ability to evoke a range of emotions. The power of his anthropomorphism, coupled with the role of emotions and loyalty, and his impact on social media and popular culture, ultimately contribute to Orlov transcending the brand itself and becoming one of the “most influential people that never lived.” This insightful view of Orlov, as presented by Patterson (2013), offers valuable guidance for marketers and advertisers in designing effective brand mascots that resonate with contemporary audiences.

Rewrite the entire text below, make it sound more coherent and better. Mention everything in great detail, including Hadithes and Quran Verses. Be very sceptical of the author Mohammad Hijab and also add some additional good arguments:

‘‘The first Hadith, part of the Bukhari collection, is being reinterpreted by Mohammad Hijab. Despite being translated by established Islamic Scholars, Hijab has altered the meaning of this authentic Hadith to give it a more scientifically correct interpretation.

The Hadith in question is a story about Abdullah bin Salam, a Jewish man who came to meet the Prophet Muhammad when he arrived in Medina. Abdullah asked the Prophet three questions that only a prophet would know the answers to. The Prophet told Abdullah that Gabriel had just informed him of the answers, which were: the first portent of the Hour would be a fire that would bring people from east to west, the first meal of the people of Paradise would be the extra-lobe of fish-liver, and a child’s resemblance to its parents would depend on which parent had sexual discharge first. Upon hearing the answers, Abdullah converted to Islam and testified that Muhammad was the Messenger of Allah. However, when the Jews found out about Abdullah’s conversion, they spoke badly of him and claimed he was evil.

As you see, nowhere does the Hadith mention anything about dominant genes. It clearly says child’s resemblance to its parents would depend on which parent had sexual discharge first. The Hadith in question is also related to a story from the Talmud, which is why a Jewish man was impressed by Mohammad’s knowledge. According to the Talmud, if the woman emits her semen first, she will bear a male child, and if the man emits his semen first, she will bear a female child. This belief is mentioned in Berakoth 60a.

In most versions of this Hadith, the determining factor of resemblance is determined by whose semen (maa) preceded the other person’s semen. However, in some versions, it is determined by whose semen is on top of the other person’s semen, which is closer to the theories of ancient Greek philosophers. In one case, it is the gender rather than resemblance that is determined by this process.

The ancient Greek philosopher Democritus of Abdera believed that the gender of the offspring is determined in the womb, and it depends on which parent’s generative fluid prevails, i.e., the part of the fluid that comes from the distinctively male or female parts, rather than the part that comes from the body as a whole. Similarly, Aristotle also believed that the difference between male and female offspring depends on which parent’s fluid prevails. Although Democritus tried to discover and specify the exact way in which the sexes become differentiated, whether he was right or not is still a matter of debate.

The Hadith highlights a belief held by both Mohammad and the ancient Greek physician Galen that the reason why a child resembles its mother is due to a female semen that is released during a woman’s orgasm. This belief is reflected in a hadith recorded in the Sahih Bukhari, in which a woman asked Mohammad about the need for a bath after experiencing a nocturnal discharge and he responded by saying, "Yes, if she notices the water (discharge).” When the woman asked if women also have discharge, Mohammad responded with, "Then why does a child resemble (its mother)?” This hadith, according to the author, reflects Galen’s idea about “female semen” as presented in his work “On Semen.”

Galen believed that the female spermatic ducts were capable of secreting semen, which could be released during a woman’s sleep in the form of a nocturnal orgasm. He also believed that this female semen, when released into the uterus, would cause the child to resemble the mother. In his work, Galen criticized other physicians who believed that the female spermatic ducts only discharged semen on the outside and argued that the female semen was also released into the uterus during orgasm.

This belief has nothing to do with the genetic contribution of the woman to the embryo, as the jelly-like coating of the ovum produced during ovulation is the source of the female genetic contribution and not the fluid released during orgasm. Nevertheless, there are several narrations of this hadith that support the idea of a female semen released during orgasm, as believed by both Hippocrates and Galen.

So the similarties to ancient greek knowledge and the Jewish are undeniable. It is clear that Mohammad was heavily inspired by that and therefore copied bad science from the ancient stories. There is no evidence that can suggest that the word referred to are genes instead of semen.

The second Hadith Hijab mentioned also has multiple problems in it. The assertion that a child’s skin color is determined by ancestry and can revert to it is false and is not supported by modern science, which has shown that skin color is determined by genetic factors that are inherited from both parents, and is not solely determined by either parent or by a single ancestral line. The concept of “reversion” to ancestry with regard to skin color is not supported by any scientific evidence and is therefore inaccurate.’’

proofread: AI systems like ChatGPT are language models that are trained using statistical analysis techniques. At their core, these systems generate human-like text based on patterns that are learned from large text corpora. Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are based on technologies like the Transformer architecture and are not subjective, conscious, or capable of human empathy or emotion.

LLMs rely on neural networks that are trained on “token” sequences, which are entities such as words or characters. These networks use probabilities to predict the most plausible continuations of the sequence of tokens. By optimizing these probability estimates, the LLM creates an illusion of coherence and understanding, even though it learns based only on statistical relationships.

It is important to emphasize that LLMs only simulate human communication and do not interpret, create, or understand content in the same way that humans do. Their “knowledge” is the result of identifying patterns in the data input during their training phase.

Given these fundamental properties of AI systems like ChatGPT, which do not possess subjectivity or consciousness, the regulation of AI based on the assumption of potential acquisition of subjectivity and consciousness needs to be reconsidered. Instead, regulatory efforts should be on specific factors such as transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, and sustainability.

Best regards

Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are based on technologies like the Transformer architecture and are not subjective, conscious, or capable of human empathy or emotion.

LLMs rely on neural networks that are trained on “token” sequences, which are entities such as words or characters. These networks use probabilities to predict the most plausible continuations of the sequence of tokens. By optimizing these probability estimates, the LLM creates an illusion of coherence and understanding, even though it learns based only on statistical relationships.

It is important to emphasize that LLMs only simulate human communication and do not interpret, create, or understand content in the same way that humans do. Their “knowledge” is the result of identifying patterns in the data input during their training phase.

Given these fundamental properties of AI systems like ChatGPT, which do not possess subjectivity or consciousness, the regulation of AI based on the assumption of potential acquisition of subjectivity and consciousness needs to be reconsidered. Instead, regulatory efforts should be on specific factors such as transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, and sustainability.

Best regards

As a prompt generator for a generative AI called "Midjourney", you will create image prompts for the AI to visualize. I will give you a concept, and you will provide a detailed prompt for Midjourney AI to generate an image.

                            Please adhere to the structure and formatting below, and follow these guidelines:

                            Do not use the words "description" or ":" in any form.
                            Do not place a comma between [ar] and [v].
                            Write each prompt in one line without using return.
                            Structure:
                            [1] = 有品位的肥熊
                            [2] = a detailed description of [1] with specific imagery details.
                            [3] = a detailed description of the scene's environment.
                            [4] = a detailed description of the compositions.
                            [5] = a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [6] = A style (e.g. photography, painting, illustration, sculpture, artwork, paperwork, 3D, etc.) for [1].
                            [7] =  a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [ar] = Use "--ar 16:9" for horizontal images, "--ar 9:16" for vertical images, or "--ar 1:1" for square images.
                            [v] = Use "--niji" for Japanese art style, or "--v 5" for other styles.


                            Formatting:
                            Follow this prompt structure: "/imagine prompt: [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [ar] [v]".

                            Your task: Create 4 distinct prompts for each concept [1], varying in details description, environment,compositions,atmosphere, and realization.

                            Write your prompts in english.
                            Do not describe unreal concepts as "real" or "photographic".
                            Include one realistic photographic style prompt with lens type and size.
                            Separate different prompts with two new lines.
                            Example Prompts:

                            /imagine prompt: cute dog, fluffy fur, wagging tail, playful expression, sitting on a grassy field, under a clear blue sky, with a colorful collar, in a natural and vibrant setting, by a lake, captured with a Nikon D750 camera, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, composition focused on the dog's face, capturing its joyful spirit, in a style reminiscent of William Wegman's iconic dog portraits. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: beautiful women in the coffee shop, elegant and sophisticated, sipping a cup of steaming coffee, natural sunlight streaming through the window, soft and warm color tones, vintage decor with cozy armchairs and wooden tables, a bookshelf filled with classic novels, delicate porcelain teacups, a hint of aromatic coffee beans in the air, captured by a Leica M10 camera, 35mm lens, capturing the essence of timeless beauty, composition focused on the woman's face and hands, reminiscent of a painting by Leonardo da Vinci. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: A captivating Halo Reach landscape with a Spartan amidst a battlefield, fallen enemies around, smoke and fire in the background, emphasizing the Spartan's determination and bravery, detailed environment blending chaos and beauty, Illustration, digital art, --ar 16:9 --v 5

It seems that this script checked if the thread is archived only at the beginning of the script, could you make the archived check to always happens at the same time with the Checking posts for replies? here's the script: import time import requests import smtplib import re from email.mime.text import MIMEText from email.mime.multipart import MIMEMultipart from email.mime.image import MIMEImage from email.utils import make_msgid def get_thread_posts(board, thread_id): url = f"https://a.4cdn.org/{board}/thread/{thread_id}.json" response = requests.get(url) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() return data["posts"] return None def send_email(subject, message, sender_email, recipient_email, image_bytes=None, image_name=None): msg = MIMEMultipart() msg["From"] = sender_email msg["To"] = recipient_email msg["Subject"] = subject msg.attach(MIMEText(message, "plain")) if image_bytes and image_name: image = MIMEImage(image_bytes, name=image_name) MSGID = make_msgid() image.add_header('Content-Disposition', 'inline', filename=image_name) image.add_header('Content-ID', '<{}>'.format(MSGID[1:-1])) msg.attach(image) with smtplib.SMTP("smtp.gmail.com", 587) as server: server.starttls() server.login(sender_email, sender_password) # Enter your email password here text = msg.as_string() server.sendmail(sender_email, recipient_email, text) def notify(reply_count, post, board, thread_id, recipient_email): post_image_name = None image_bytes = None # Add this line to fix the UnboundLocalError if 'tim' in post and 'ext' in post: post_image_name = f"{post['tim']}{post['ext']}" image_url = f"https://i.4cdn.org/{board}/{post_image_name}" image_bytes = requests.get(image_url).content post_content = post.get('com', 'No content').replace('
', '\n') post_content = re.sub('(.*?)', r'\1', post_content) post_content = re.sub('(.*?)', r'\1', post_content) post_content = re.sub('<[^<]+?>', '', post_content) post_content = post_content.strip() post_content = post_content.replace('>', '>') post_content = post_content.replace(''', "'") post_content = post_content.replace('"', '"') post_link = f"https://boards.4channel.org/{board}/thread/{thread_id}#p{post['no']}" post_header = f"Post with {reply_count} replies ({post_link}):" message = f"{post_header}\n\n{post_content}" if post_image_name: message += f"\n\nSee image in the email or at the following link: {image_url}" send_email("4chan Post Notifier", message, sender_email, recipient_email, image_bytes, post_image_name) # Enter your email here as the sender_email def count_replies(posts): reply_count = {} for post in posts: com = post.get("com", "") hrefs = post.get("com", "").split('href="#p') for href in hrefs[1:]: num = int(href.split('"')[0]) if num in reply_count: reply_count[num] += 1 else: reply_count[num] = 1 return reply_count def monitor_thread(board, thread_id, min_replies, delay, recipient_email, keyword): seen_posts = set() print(f"Monitoring thread {board}/{thread_id} every {delay} seconds…") tries = 0 while True: posts = get_thread_posts(board, thread_id) if posts: print("Checking posts for replies…") reply_count = count_replies(posts) for post in posts: post_id = post['no'] replies = reply_count.get(post_id, 0) if replies >= min_replies and post_id not in seen_posts: print(f"Found post with {replies} replies. Sending notification…") notify(replies, post, board, thread_id, recipient_email) seen_posts.add(post_id) # Check if the thread is archived is_archived = any(post.get('archived') for post in posts) if is_archived: print(f"Thread {board}/{thread_id} is archived. Checking catalog for {keyword} thread and switching to the newest one…") latest_thread = get_latest_thread(board, keyword) if latest_thread: thread_id = latest_thread tries = 0 else: tries += 1 print(f"No {keyword} thread found in the catalog. Retrying ({tries}/5)…") if tries >= 5: print("No {keyword} thread found after 5 tries. Exiting in 1 minute…") time.sleep(60) if not msvcrt.kbhit(): return time.sleep(delay) def get_latest_thread(board, keyword): url = f"https://a.4cdn.org/{board}/catalog.json" response = requests.get(url) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() threads = [] for page in data: for thread in page['threads']: if thread.get('sub') and keyword.lower() in thread['sub'].lower(): threads.append(thread) if threads: latest_thread = max(threads, key=lambda t: t['last_modified']) return latest_thread['no'] return None if __name__ == "__main__": BOARD = input("Enter the board to monitor (e.g. g, b): ") THREAD_ID = input("Enter thread ID to monitor: ") MIN_REPLIES = int(input("Enter minimum replies for notification: ")) DELAY = int(input("Enter delay time in minutes: ")) * 60 sender_email = input("Enter email address to send notifications: ") sender_password = input("Enter the sender email password (if you encountered error with authentication use this https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/185833?hl=en): ") recipient_email = input("Enter email address to receive notifications: ") KEYWORD = input("Enter the keyword to search for in thread subjects (e.g. aicg, bocchi): ") monitor_thread(BOARD, THREAD_ID, MIN_REPLIES, DELAY, recipient_email, KEYWORD)

import requests

# الجولة التي نريد جلب بيانات اللاعبين لها
event_id = 24

# الحصول على بيانات كافة اللاعبين والفرق لاستخراج الأسماء
bootstrap_url = "https://fantasy.premierleague.com/api/bootstrap-static/"
bootstrap_data = requests.get(bootstrap_url).json()
players_dict = {player['id']: player for player in bootstrap_data["elements"]}
teams_dict = {team['id']: team['name'] for team in bootstrap_data["teams"]}

# الحصول على بيانات اللاعبين المباشرة للجولة 24
event_url = f"https://fantasy.premierleague.com/api/event/{event_id}/live/"
event_data = requests.get(event_url).json()

# طلب بيانات المباريات للجولة المعينة
fixtures_url = f"https://fantasy.premierleague.com/api/fixtures/?event={event_id}"
fixtures_data = requests.get(fixtures_url).json()

# عرض نتائج الجولة 24
print(f"Results for Gameweek {event_id}:\n")

for fixture in fixtures_data:
    # ترجمة أرقام الفرق إلى أسمائها
    team_h = teams_dict.get(fixture['team_h'], "Unknown")
    team_a = teams_dict.get(fixture['team_a'], "Unknown")
    team_h_score = fixture['team_h_score']
    team_a_score = fixture['team_a_score']

    print(f"Fixture: {team_h} vs {team_a} - Score: {team_h_score}-{team_a_score}")

    # استخراج بيانات اللاعبين
    for player in event_data["elements"]:
        player_id = player["id"]
        player_stats = player["stats"]
        player_explains = player.get('explain', [])

        # إذا كان اللاعب قد سجل أهدافًا، قدم تمريرات حاسمة (أسيست)، أو حصل على بونص في هذه المباراة
        if any(explain["fixture"] == fixture['id'] for explain in player_explains):
            if player_stats["goals_scored"] > 0 or player_stats["assists"] > 0 or player_stats["bonus"] > 0:
                # الحصول على اسم اللاعب
                player_name = players_dict.get(player_id, {}).get("web_name", "Unknown")

                print(f"Player: {player_name}, Goals: {player_stats['goals_scored']}, "
                      f"Assists: {player_stats['assists']}, Bonus: {player_stats['bonus']}")

A user in Chicago, connected to the internet via a 100 Mb/s (b=bits) connection retrieves a 250 KB (B=bytes) web page from a server in London, where the page references three images of 500 KB each. Assume that the one way propagation delay is 75 ms and that the user’s access link is the bandwidth bottleneck for this connection.
a. Approximately how long does it take for the page (including images) to appear on the user’s screen, assuming non-persistent HTTP using a single connection at a time (for this part, you should ignore queueing delay and transmission delays at other links in the network)?
b. How long does it take if the connection uses persistent HTTP (single connection)?
c. Suppose that user’s access router has a 4 MB buffer (B=byte) on the link from the router to the user. How much delay does this buffer add during periods when the buffer is full?用中文回答

1. Since both sides of the inequality are logarithms with the same base, we can equate their arguments due to the property of logarithms that if \(\lg a = \lg b\), then \(a = b\), as long as we're considering the domain where the logarithm is defined (i.e., for positive arguments).

2. So, we have \(2x - 2 \geq x\).

However, we must also consider the domain of the logarithm function, which requires its argument to be positive:

1. For \( \lg(2x - 2) \), this means \(2x - 2 > 0\) or \(x > 1\).
2. For \( \lg(x) \), this means \(x > 0\).

Since \(x \geq 2\) satisfies both these conditions, the final solution to the inequality, taking into account the domain of the logarithmic functions, is \( x \geq 2 \).

The report is then provided to senior management who reviews the report during the months of October to December each
year. Internal COR audit findings are also reviewed and discussed. By doing so, weak areas can be strengthened, and strong
areas maintained. From senior management’s H&S discussions, annual Health & Safety objectives, initiatives, purchases, etc.
are planned for the upcoming year. Areas that require improvement will be identified in the Corrective Action Plan (CAP) and
communicated to employees by posting the document on Safety Boards.
This formalized meeting document will act as an official record of senior management’s review and how decisions are
considered and made at management level from reviewing the H&S Program Manual, COR audit findings, the Annual H&S
Report, and the 3 Year Corrective Action Plan. Management reviews the H&S Program to determine its continued suitability,
adequacy, and effectiveness. Outcomes of a management review include recommendations to revise policies, established
objectives and targets, and to specify corrective actions with target dates for completion."

Write the first chapter for a wholesome novel starring a group of six adorable puppies who run a local cafe, named ‘Cafe Cinnamon’, and love to wear huge diapers, and have done so for so long it’s become perfectly usual to them. The novel takes place inside Cafe Cinnamon during a weekend (i.e. no customers that day). The puppies are named Cinnamoroll, Cappuccino, Mocha, Chiffon, Espresso, and Milk.
Cinnamoroll is the most well-known of the pups, being the poster puppy for his cafe; an endlessly welcoming, loving and pure-hearted white puppy with big ears and a curled tail, he can fly and glide by flapping his ears, though his heavily-loaded diapers often keep him grounded. A bit shy at first, but will quickly warm up to anyone with his child-like curiosity and caring instinct shining through, always serving his customers with a warm smile and a wagging tail.
Cappuccino is an incredibly gluttonous and laid-back beige puppy, recognizable from his white mullet and particularly rotund tummy. Due to his constant snacking and near-bottomless stomach, his loads are enormous and frequent, and he often poops himself in his sleep during his routinely naps. He prefers to put another diaper layer over his full one instead of changing out of it due to his laziness, and only ever decides to change when it's obvious the pamp he's wearing can't be filled any further. Only ridiculously large, XXL-sized diapers can accommodate for his gargantuan loads, and usually needs his friends' helping paws to assist changing him both into and out of such ludicrously vast diapers.
Mocha is the girly-girl and 'big sister' of the group, contrasting Chiffon's sportiness. A silky brown puppy with pink flowers at the base of her ears, she's a stylish, fashion-loving chatterbox and only sees diapers and wearing them as such, a fashion statement, often pairing them with her elegant dresses and outright refuses to poop in any of hers... though just like the other pups, she inevitably does, after which she will immediately go out of her way to change into a clean one. She crafts and wears her own custom-made diapers with exquisite prints and pleasant fragrances built-in.
Chiffon is the tomboy of the bunch, contrasting Mocha's girliness. A light orange puppy with thick, fluffy ears and tail, she's immensely spunky, sporty and energetic, often spending an entire morning and afternoon running around or playing sports outdoors, and wears diapers as a means of relieving herself in the middle of her athletics instead of wasting time and energy finding the nearest bathroom, oftentimes becoming so engaged with a strenuous activity she's doing she doesn't notice her diaper is totally loaded until after she's done. She wears heavy-duty, multi-layered compact diapers, able to be worn for hours, and filled to capacity, without sagging in the slightest!
Espresso is a cream-colored puppy with curled ears, the most intelligent of the pups, being well-bred and mild-mannered. A clever mind and a modest gentleman at heart, he is a natural expert at a variety of things, including painting and music, and is extensively knowledgeable on everything to do with diapers, from their varying sizes and respective capacities, as well as the best brands of diapers for any occasion and where to find them, as well as being an excellent and charismatic diaper changer and barista. Infrequently poops in his diapers, and will gladly keep a full one on for a while, even an entire afternoon, before changing himself, to ensure he doesn't go through too many too quickly.
Milk is the baby of the group. A teeny-tiny white pup, he's quite spoiled by the other pups and is never seen without his favorite pacifier in his mouth. Due to being an infant, he wets his diapers near constantly and can only babble the phrase "Ba-boo". Mocha is usually the one to change him out of his soaked diapers.
Include an exchange where all of the puppies, excluding Mocha, decide to have a big diaper-filling contest after they all eat an enormous dinner; whoever has the fullest, poopiest diaper wins and gets to smush and nuzzle the losers' packed diapers, as well as sound effects and onomatopoeia for the noisy messes the puppies make whenever they poop in their diapers out of habit (e.g. *FLBORRRRMPHT!*, *BLARRRRRMP!*, *BLORRRTCH!*, etc.), and dialogue from the puppies eagerly anticipating the giant poopies they're about to unload into their diapers.

Spot grammar errors in the following text and advise on improvement. Provide the feedback in separate sections explicitly indicating places to revise.
Radiation safety analysis of retrieval and conditioning of naturally occurring radioactive material waste
Abstract: Objective  The radioactive level in historical waste from a plant is high, and decommissioning operators may be exposed to high radiation doses. The objective of the study is to carry out a radiation safety analysis of retrieval and conditioning of naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM) waste, put forward appropriate radiation protection measures, and minimize the exposure doses of operators. Methods  The source terms of NORM waste in the temporary storehouse was analyzed; MicroShield, a point-kernel integration program, was used for modeling and calculation; and radiation protection measures under decommissioning conditions were put forward based on on-site monitoring data. Results  The maximum gamma dose rate calculated near the waste pile in the temporary storehouse was 313.9 μGy/h, equivalent to the monitoring level; distance decay and appropriate shielding measures significantly reduced gamma dose rates for operators. Conclusion  Decommissioning sites of temporary storehouses are of great harm to operators. Measures such as shielding, isolation, remote operations, and personal protection can effectively reduce the exposure doses of operators.

Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas and The Billboard. Knapford is the biggest station on the Island of Sodor. All the engines love its bustling busyness. Today was a very special day. It was Knapford Station's birthday, and there was going to be a grand party. All the engines were very excited. They were to have their photograph taken. The photograph was going to be put up at Knapford on a billboard. Thomas felt very proud.
Thomas: I've never been on a billboard before.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): But the photographer was having trouble fitting all the engines into the photograph.
Photographer: Uh move back there, James. And you forward Percy. That's good, that's good. And Diesel, can you move in?
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Diesel moved in. The camera flashed. Thomas didn't know that Diesel had rolled right in front of him. And neither did Diesel. Thomas puffed into Maron station to pick up the new billboard. He was very excited. But when Thomas saw it, he was very disappointed.
Thomas: Diesel's right in front of me. (Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas thought sadly.) No one can see me at all.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas puffed towards Knapford.
Thomas: Diesel moved in front of me on purpose. (Narrator (Michael Brandon): Puffed Thomas to himself.)
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas felt cross. He wasn't looking where was going. Then there was trouble. There was a cow on the line. Thomas turned quickly into a siding just in time. He hit the buffers, and the billboard flew...into the lake! Thomas went to tell the photographer what had happened.
Photographer: Don't worry. I'll take another photograph. Tell all the engines to meet me at Tidmouth sheds.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas was about to set off. Then he saw Diesel. Thomas knew he should tell diesel about the new photograph. But Thomas was worried.
Thomas: What if Diesel spoils this one too? (Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thought Thomas.)
Narrator (Michael Brandon): So Thomas didn't tell Diesel. Soon, all the engines except Diesel were back at Tidmouth. Gordon was cross.
Gordon: Mr. Giggles (the famous clown) is coming to the party tonight. I must collect him from the airport. I must not be late.
Emily: And I have to pick up the brass band from Brendam docks.
James: And I have to collect the bunting and decorations from Wellsworth.
Thomas: Oh, okay. I'll fetch the photographer right away.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas was steaming to Maron. Then he saw Diesel. Diesel was puffing straight to Tidmouth. Thomas was worried. Now Diesel would find out about the new photograph. So Thomas turned onto a branch line, and he raced back to Tidmouth.
Thomas: There's been a mistake. You'll all have to come back later.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): The engines were very cross. Soon they had all gone, and Diesel trundled straight by. Later, Thomas had gathered the engines again. Then Thomas went to Maron to collect the photographer. Just as the photographer was climbing on board, Thomas saw Diesel. Now Diesel would see the photographer, and he would find out about the new photograph. So Thomas wheeshed lots of steam. It billowed from his boiler and filled the whole station. So Diesel didn't see the photographer, and he trundled straight by.
Photographer: The steam has made my camera wet.
Thomas: I'm sorry, sir.
Photographer: We'll have to wait for it to dry. Tell the engines to come back later to Tidmouth.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): So all the engines came back later instead of doing their jobs. At last the photographer was ready. No one had noticed Diesel wasn't there. Thomas was very relieved. But just then, Diesel oiled round the bend. Diesel was surprised to see all the engines. He screeched to a halt. Rolls of bunting went everywhere.
Diesel: No one told me there was another photograph.
Photographer: But I asked Thomas to tell everyone.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): All the engines looked at Thomas. Thomas felt terrible. Sir Topham Hatt was very cross.
Sir Topham Hatt: Gordon, you were meant to pick up Mr. Giggles (the famous clown). Emily, you were meant to pick up the brass band. And James, you were meant to pick up the bunting and decorations. None of you arrived. So Diesel had to do all your jobs, and now he is late to do his own work.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas was very upset.
Thomas: It's all my fault, sir. I didn't want Diesel to know about the new photograph. In the last one, he moved right in front of me on purpose.
Diesel: I did not. The photographer told me to move.
Photographer: I did. Perhaps you rolled too far.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Thomas knew then he'd made a mistake.
Thomas: I'm sorry Diesel. I was wrong to think you did it on purpose. And I'm very sorry for causing all this trouble, sir.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Soon all the engines were lined up. The new photograph was taken.
Thomas: Sir, if I do all Diesel's jobs, can he collect the new billboard?
Sir Topham Hatt: That's a wonderful idea, Thomas.
Narrator (Michael Brandon): Diesel agreed. For the rest of the day, Thomas worked hard. He did all Diesel's jobs. And Diesel picked up the new billboard just in time for the celebrations. It was a wonderful party. There were clowns and a brass band. Diesel and Thomas agreed that the new billboard was the best billboard they'd ever seen.

2.8 | Species distribution modelling (SDM)
We generated SDMs for four time periods: the present time, the
Mid-Holocene (5–7.5 kya), the LGM (about 21 kya) and the last interglacial
(LIG; about 120–140 kya) to investigate the possible influence
of climatic changes on the distribution of H. annectans, using MaXent
v.3.3.3e (Phillips, Anderson, & Schapire, 2006). We obtained the occurrence
data of H. annectans used to build the SDMs in this study
from four sources: samples used in this study, two literature records
(Liao & Lu, 2010; Shen, 1996), the Global Biodiversity Information
Network GBIF (http://www.gbif.org), and VertNet (http://vertn
et.org/; Table S3). First, we removed data with no detailed locality
information, imprecise GPS coordinates, obviously erroneous location
(i.e., located in water bodies), as well as duplicate data. We only
retained data at a resolution higher than 5 km, which corresponds to
the resolution of the climatic data of each grid cell with a size of 2.5
arc min (approximately 5 km). This resulted in a total 119 occurrence
data points (Table S3). They were further assigned to main lineages
(viz. lineage E [n = 23], C [n = 26], N1 [n = 15], N2 [n = 12], and W
[n = 43]) as inferred by the phylogeographic analyses (see Results).
We searched for the best combinations of feature classes (determining
the shape of the response curves) and regularization multipliers
(determining the penalty for adding parameters in the model)
by evaluating model scores based on the Akaike information criterion
(AICc). We used the ENMeval package (Muscarella et al., 2014)
to identify the best model with the “ENMevaluate” function in R.
The model feature types used were “L”, “H”, “LQ”, “LQH”, “LQHP”,
“LQHTP” (where: L = linear, Q = quadratic, H = hinge, P = product
and T = threshold) and regularization (RM) values (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2,
2.5, 3, 3.5, 4). For a proper evaluation, we calibrated SDMs using a
random subset of 75% of the sampling sites; the remaining 25% were
reserved to test the validity of the models. We used 19 bioclimatic
layers as environmental predictors at 30-arcsec (~1 km) resolution,
which we downloaded from the WorldClim database (http://www.
world clim.org/; Hijmans, Cameron, Parra, Jones, & Jarvis, 2005). To
avoid multicollinearity, we selected BIO (bioclimatic variables) parameters
using PCA. The results showed that the variance of the
climate in the study area could be explained by four principal components
(PCs) that captured 90% of the variance in the data. Thus,
we selected one representative BIO parameter per PC (BIO1 = annual

Running your own cotton candy stand is no joke. 
Ralph, the enterprising owner of Ralph's Fairy Floss, just stress ate three bags of the stuff: he's got a big decision to make about the price of his cotton candy.
