messages.content:
Forever Young is a retailer of trendy and low-cost apparel in the United States. The company
divides the year into four sales seasons of about three months each and brings in new merchandise
for each season. The company has historically outsourced production to China, given the lower
costs there. Sourcing from the Chinese supplier costs 55 yuan/unit (inclusive of all delivery costs),
which at the current exchange rate of 6.5 yuan/$ gives a variable cost of under $8.50/unit. The
Chinese supplier, however, has a long lead time, forcing Forever Young to pick an order size well
before the start of the season. This does not leave the company any flexibility if actual demand
differs from the order size. A local supplier has come to management with a proposal to supply
product at a cost of $10/unit but to do so quickly enough that Forever Young will be able to make
supply in the season exactly match demand. Management is concerned about the higher variable
cost but finds the flexibility of the onshore supplier very attractive. The challenge is to value the
responsiveness provided by the local supplier.
Uncertainties Faced by Forever Young
To better compare the two suppliers, management identifies demand and exchange rates as the two
major uncertainties faced by the company. Over each of the next two periods (assume them to be
a year each), demand may go up by 10 percent, with a probability of 0.5, or down by 10 percent,
with a probability of 0.5. Demand in the current period was 1,000 units. Similarly, over each of
the next two periods, the yuan may strengthen by 5 percent, with a probability of 0.5, or weaken
by 5 percent, with a probability of 0.5. The exchange rate in the current period was 6.5 yuan/$.
Ordering Policies with the Two Suppliers Given the long lead time of the offshore supplier,
Forever Young commits to an order before observing any demand signal. Given the demand
uncertainty over the next two periods and the fact that the margin from each unit (about $11.50) is
higher than the loss if the unit remains unsold at the end of the season (loss of about $8.50),
management decides to commit to an order that is somewhat higher than expected demand. Given
that expected demand is 1,000 units over each of the next two periods, management decides to
order 1,040 units from the Chinese supplier for each of the next two periods. If demand in a period
turns out to be higher than 1,040 units, Forever Young will sell 1,040 units. However, if demand
turns out to be lower than 1,040, the company will have leftover product for which it will not be
able to recover any revenue. The short lead time of the local supplier allows Forever Young to
keep bringing product in a little bit at a time, based on actual sales. Thus, if the local supplier is
used, the company is able to meet all demand in each period without having any unsold inventory
or lost sales. In other words, the final order from the local supplier will exactly equal the demand
observed by Forever Young.
A Potential Hybrid Strategy
The local supplier has also offered another proposal that would allow Forever Young to use both
suppliers, each playing a different role. The Chinese supplier would produce a base quantity for
the season and the local supplier would cover any shortfalls that result. The short lead time of the
local supplier would ensure that no sales are lost. In other words, if Forever Young committed to
a base load of 900 units with the Chinese supplier in a given period and demand was 900 units or
less, nothing would be ordered from the local supplier. If demand, however, was larger than 900
units (say, 1,100), the shortfall of 200 units would be supplied by the local supplier. Under a hybrid
strategy, the local supplier would end up supplying only a small fraction of the season’s demand.
For this extra flexibility and reduced volumes, however, the local supplier proposes to charge
$11/unit if it is used as part of a hybrid strategy.

Create a binary model to find the best method among onshoring, offshoring and hybrid scouring and add exchange rate

costs there. Sourcing from the Chinese supplier costs 55 yuan/unit (inclusive of all delivery costs),
which at the current exchange rate of 6.5 yuan/$ gives a variable cost of under $8.50/unit. The
Chinese supplier, however, has a long lead time, forcing Forever Young to pick an order size well
before the start of the season. This does not leave the company any flexibility if actual demand
differs from the order size. A local supplier has come to management with a proposal to supply
product at a cost of $10/unit but to do so quickly enough that Forever Young will be able to make
supply in the season exactly match demand. Management is concerned about the higher variable
cost but finds the flexibility of the onshore supplier very attractive. The challenge is to value the
responsiveness provided by the local supplier.
Uncertainties Faced by Forever Young
To better compare the two suppliers, management identifies demand and exchange rates as the two
major uncertainties faced by the company. Over each of the next two periods (assume them to be
a year each), demand may go up by 10 percent, with a probability of 0.5, or down by 10 percent,
with a probability of 0.5. Demand in the current period was 1,000 units. Similarly, over each of
the next two periods, the yuan may strengthen by 5 percent, with a probability of 0.5, or weaken
by 5 percent, with a probability of 0.5. The exchange rate in the current period was 6.5 yuan/$.
Ordering Policies with the Two Suppliers Given the long lead time of the offshore supplier,
Forever Young commits to an order before observing any demand signal. Given the demand
uncertainty over the next two periods and the fact that the margin from each unit (about $11.50) is
higher than the loss if the unit remains unsold at the end of the season (loss of about $8.50),
management decides to commit to an order that is somewhat higher than expected demand. Given
that expected demand is 1,000 units over each of the next two periods, management decides to
order 1,040 units from the Chinese supplier for each of the next two periods. If demand in a period
turns out to be higher than 1,040 units, Forever Young will sell 1,040 units. However, if demand
turns out to be lower than 1,040, the company will have leftover product for which it will not be
able to recover any revenue. The short lead time of the local supplier allows Forever Young to
keep bringing product in a little bit at a time, based on actual sales. Thus, if the local supplier is
used, the company is able to meet all demand in each period without having any unsold inventory
or lost sales. In other words, the final order from the local supplier will exactly equal the demand
observed by Forever Young.
A Potential Hybrid Strategy
The local supplier has also offered another proposal that would allow Forever Young to use both
suppliers, each playing a different role. The Chinese supplier would produce a base quantity for
the season and the local supplier would cover any shortfalls that result. The short lead time of the
local supplier would ensure that no sales are lost. In other words, if Forever Young committed to
a base load of 900 units with the Chinese supplier in a given period and demand was 900 units or
less, nothing would be ordered from the local supplier. If demand, however, was larger than 900
units (say, 1,100), the shortfall of 200 units would be supplied by the local supplier. Under a hybrid
strategy, the local supplier would end up supplying only a small fraction of the season’s demand.
For this extra flexibility and reduced volumes, however, the local supplier proposes to charge
$11/unit if it is used as part of a hybrid strategy.

Create a scam-baiting response to the most recent email, to keep the scammer in a false sense of security by posing as a potential victim. Use the prior emails as a point of reference.

Email #1, from Doris Hussain:

Hello my name is Mrs Doris Hussain i am from Singapore, i have a
pressing issue which i will like to share with you so kindly get back
to me.
kindly get back to me for details of what i want us to discuss reach me on (hatsphils01 AT gmail DOT com)

Email #2, from Cameron McCaffrey (me):

 Dear Mrs. <PRESIDIO_ANONYMIZED_PERSON>,

I hope this message finds you in good health and spirits. I was both surprised and intrigued when I received your email, as it is not every day that one gets a message concerning a pressing issue from a stranger halfway across the world.

My curiosity has certainly been piqued, and I find myself quite eager to learn more about the matter you wish to discuss. I can only imagine the importance of it since you’ve taken the time to seek assistance beyond your immediate surroundings.

Please feel free to share the details with me at your earliest convenience. I am always looking for new ways to engage with others and facilitate solutions to their concerns. Who knows, perhaps there might be a way for me to assist you.

I look forward to your email and understanding more about the pressing issue you mentioned. Rest assured, your communication will be held in the strictest confidence.

Warm regards,

Cameron McCaffrey
cmccaff1@fau.edu

Email #3, from Doris:

Hello,

Thanks for your response. I want to say thank you for allowing me to have this conversation with you. I am Mrs. Doris Hussian from Singapore and married to Engineer David  Hussian   of the Republic of Togo. We were married for 17 years without any child, My husband died in 2018. My husband deposited the sum of $2,500,000 USD (Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars) with a bank in Republic of Togo before his untimely death in an accident

  I have been battling with cancer which is in the last stage according to the doctor. I am currently undergoing cancer treatment in the United States of America. I am contacting you concerning my late Husband's funds deposited in his bank before his death. I wish to present you to the bank as the beneficiary/trustee so that you can receive the fund and use it for charity in line with my late husband's wish.

  I contacted you for this humanitarian work with a conviction in my heart that you will not betray me when the fund arrives into your account. . You may be wondering why I suddenly chose or contacted you, not knowing you and more things about you. Yes the truth is that I have no doubt in GOD, I prayed and fasted and asked God to provide me someone who will have affection for me and help me with a sincere mind to use the fund to do charity.

I want you to use 50% of this funds for charity and to the poor and
needy, then you will use 30% to build a house of worship for God and finally the remaining 20% of the money will be for you and your family.

l made this decision because I don't have any child that will inherit this money and my husband's relatives are not Christians not even good at all because they are the one that is responsible for the death of my husband in order to have all my late husband's properties. I do not want my husband's efforts to be used by those that conspired for his death.
Now I am in the United States now, also due to my condition I have no hope again because I have overheard my doctor telling one of the nurses about my health and when the surgery will take place.

I will be delighted to die peacefully if my desire is achieved by your helping to make sure that this fund is transferred into your bank account as the beneficiary. You will utilize it to help those less privileged children and elderly homes so that they will feel being part of the world.

This is all I have to do to thank God almighty for the little life he has given me on this earth since I have few days to leave. As soon as I hear from you, I
will forward the bank contact information to you. I have to introduce you to the bank as my late husband's business partner and the beneficiary of the funds. My husband deposited the fund on behalf of his partner, so I can present anybody to the bank as my husband's partner.

The BANK is waiting for the release of the FUNDS to the foreign partner whom I will present as my late husband's business partner.

I have all the related documents that were issued to my late husband the day of the deposit of the fund in the bank.

Also I am sending you this message through my (Nurse) laptop computer. The nurse is taking care of me in the hospital. I am sorry for the delay because the nurse did not come to work in time and there was no place for me to check my mail.Because of my condition the Doctors stopped me from receiving visitors and they took my phones.

May the good Lord be with you and your family? I hope to hear from you for more information please.

Greetings  from  

Mrs.  Doris Hussian.

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.python_operator import PythonOperator
from airflow.operators.postgresql_operator import PostgresHook, PostgresOperator

default_args = {
    'owner': 'airflow',
    'depends_on_past': False,
    'start_date': datetime(2023, 3, 15),
    'email_on_failure': False,
    'email_on_retry': False,
    'retries': 1,
    'retry_delay': timedelta(minutes=5),
}

dag = DAG(
    'data_cleaning_pipeline',
    default_args=default_args,
    description='A sample DAG for cleaning data using PostgreSQL and Pandas',
    schedule_interval=timedelta(days=1),
)

POSTGRES_HOST = 'your_host'
POSTGRES_PORT = 5432
POSTGRES_USER = 'your_user'
POSTGRES_PASSWORD = 'your_password'
POSTGRES_DB = 'your_database'

# Connections
postgres_conn_id = 'postgres_conn'

# Define your PostgreSQL hook
postgres_hook = PostgresHook(
    postgres_conn_id=postgres_conn_id,
    host=POSTGRES_HOST,
    port=POSTGRES_PORT,
    user=POSTGRES_USER,
    password=POSTGRES_PASSWORD,
    database=POSTGRES_DB
)

def clean_data(**kwargs):
    conn = kwargs['postgres_conn']
    table_name = kwargs['table_name']
    cleaned_table_name = kwargs['cleaned_table_name']

    # Perform your data cleaning logic here
    # This example only selects data from the source table and inserts it into the cleaned table

    # Get data from PostgreSQL
    postgres_query = f"SELECT * FROM {table_name}"
    conn.cursor.execute(postgres_query)
    data = pd.DataFrame(conn.cursor.fetchall(), columns=conn.cursor.description)

    # Clean data using pandas
    data.drop_duplicates(inplace=True)  # Example of data cleaning

    # Insert cleaned data into PostgreSQL
    cleaned_data = data.to_sql(cleaned_table_name, conn, if_exists='replace')

task_vars = {
    'postgres_conn': postgres_hook.get_connection(postgres_conn_id),
    'table_name': 'your_source_table',
    'cleaned_table_name': 'your_cleaned_table',
}

default_args = {
    'owner': 'airflow',
    'depends_on_past': False,
}

with dag:
    start_task = PythonOperator(
        task_id='start_task',
        python_callable=lambda: None,  # Placeholder task
        dag=dag
    )

    clean_data_task = PythonOperator(
        task_id='clean_data_task',
        python_callable=clean_data,
        dag=dag,
        default_args=default_args,
        task_concurrency=16,
        **task_vars
    )

    end_task = PythonOperator(
        task_id='end_task',
        python_callable=lambda: None,  # Placeholder task
        dag=dag
    )

    start_task >> clean_data_task >> end_task"

Rewrite this text in a friendlier and respectful manner: Now, I know what you probably will disapprove of my perspective and many will have some objections to it: “But one day this might affect stuff you like too” some of you may say. And that's a fair point. Indeed, it would suck if stuff like this happened to things I like, and I probably would be angry about it. But here’s the thing: it’s not affecting something I like right now, is it? “Well, it might someday”. You're probably right, however, just because it “might” happen doesn’t mean it “will” happen. Let’s use the 4kids example someone gave here: just because 4kids did alter/censor some anime, that doesn’t mean ALL anime was censored, in fact, there were animes aired in their original form in America. Fast forward to now, anime isn’t really being censored anymore, is it? So if the fear of swiping censorship didn’t become true then, why would it now? Besides, just so you know, it has happened to some things I liked. And indeed I felt unhappy about it. You know what I did about it? I simply ditched those things and then moved on to another things I liked. Yes, I was irked that they censored things I liked, but it was not the end of the world.
“But these changes were pointless/stupid”. Yes, I agree with that, but it's not enough, for me at least, to worry about supposed censorship just because of that. We've seen way worse censorship before and probably after. As I said, sometimes it's just valid to not liking changes, and that's all.
“Bu when will the censorship stop, then?” You may ask. The answer: somewhere. It always stops somewhere. The slippery slope fallacy it’s still a fallacy, even if we agree with its conclusion.

Please improve the readability of "Please find attached our revised design following on from our site visit with you last week.

Once we have your approval on the basic design we can then prepare some visuals and then review the “Design and Access”  Statement document

The Site Plan

The latest proposed site plan follows the direction and discussion to reduce the amount of the land the driveway occupies. To do so we now run the driveway between the existing tree and the house. This will require the patio paving you have to the west of the existing house to be revised to allow for the path. I have currently shown an enlargement to the front driveway to allow for a better swing into this area. The arc of which will need to be properly accessed for vehicle access to make improvements. The line of the new drive does go across the root protection area slightly and this and the measures we take to protect the tree will need to be discussed with the Arboriculturist the ground for the new dive may need to be raised on a drainage mat which will spread the load to protect the roots. It may also be necessary to look at permeable paving in this area rather then resin bound gravel but again this needs to be discussed.

A new courtyard is formed with the new garage located tight the rear boundary with a 2meter slight line gap to the existing property and the new drive opening up to allow for access to each space and then to connects to the front doors of the annex, which forms the third side of the courtyard. The annex is located as close to the rear boundary as we dear giving space for a higher hedgerow and room for future maintenance access to your new property from within your own grounds. This does result in some of the view you were concerned about being interrupted as the quick visuals we have prepared for you indicates, however we feel that a good proportion of the view remains and the goal of leaving as much of the garden in front of the annex is achieved.

The New Design for the Annex 

The current aesthetic for the proposal put to you is clearly modern. We took your que over the importance of the view to sculpt the plan so that the angle of the south wall opens up the view lines from the existing property as much as is practical, without compromising the form of the living space too greatly. In our meeting you expressed an interest is developing the scheme to a Passivhaus standard although this does not restrict you going with a traditional design I have used this as motivation for design ques on the attached design. To elaborate for Passivhaus design one of the important criteria is to manage the internal temperature and make sure over solar over heating is not a problem. messages.content:
The below paras reads like a narrative, and is not much theoretically compact. The syntax also seems significantly unorganized. Please work on this in more polished way and frame this theoretically 
Eurocentrism is generally defined as a way of thinking that places European culture, history, and values at the center of the world while ignoring or downplaying the contributions of other cultures and civilizations. One could argue that Europe, more specifically Western Europe or “the West,” is often used as a universal symbol that presupposes the superiority of European cultural values over those of non-European societies. Eurocentric narratives have a recurring inclination to overlook and undervalue the contributions of non-Western cultures. Such accounts distort non-European histories and legacies by viewing them solely through European or western perspectives. This perspective has created a false dichotomy between the West and the non- European societies, perpetuating the notion that the West is superior and in control of all areas of life, including social, political, cultural, scientific, military, and economic fields. Such thinking has led to the use of derogatory terms to describe the “non-west,” fostering the idea that the non-west is inferior, illogical, aggressive, alien, fanatical, and barbaric in comparison to West. This belief in Western superiority is often reinforced through various forms of discourse, including history, literature, art, music, etc. In a similar vein, through the utilization of Eurocentric and imperialistic perspectives, academic discourse has consistently depicted ‘Eastern societies’ as exotic and racialized, perpetuating a biased portrayal of the Orient or East. In his seminal text Orientalism (1979), Edward Said, a Palestinian critic, asserts that “European culture gained in strength and identity by setting itself off against the Orient as a sort of surrogate and even underground self.” (3) This dichotomy between the West and the East often presents the West as a modern, flowing territory and the East as a static, archaic region. Therefore, the Orient functions as a mirror to the West in that the West relies heavily on its counterpart, the Orient, for its own sense of superiority. (Sandy and Ouardi, 2019, p. 129) On the other hand, this discourse of exoticism, essentialism, and stereotyping of the East and its people has been used to justify colonization, exploitation, and violence against Eastern civilizations.
The Knowledge production or the representation of the Orient in Western narratives is not a recent development; it has existed since the earliest times. Edward Said traces the development of this discourse back to ancient Greece, using two plays by Aeschylus as references. He reiterates that Asia in the play The Persians is portrayed as a ‘hostile other,’ a ‘world beyond the seas.’ In fact, colonists exploited literary works as propaganda weapons from the beginning to spread false images of the Orient.  According to Said, 
The “Orient was created -or, as I call it, “Orientalized”- and to believe that such things happen simply as a necessity of the imagination is to be disingenuous… The Orient was Orientalized not only because it was discovered to be “Oriental” in all those ways considered commonplace by an average nineteenth-century European, but also because it could be -that is, submitted to being- made Oriental.” (5-6)
Said’s argument centers on the idea that the West’s portrayal of the Orient is heavily biased and serves to further its own dominance. Additionally, this euphoria of the West’s supremacy over the East is characterised by a tremendous power disparity, according to Said. He notes that the power imbalance between the West and the Orient allows for the creation of such universalized images that further reinforce this dominance. This power allows the West to shape how the Orient is perceived and represented and to create narratives that serve its interests. However, Said’s analysis does not explicitly address gender as a factor in constructing these narratives. This paper aims to build upon Said’s argument by examining the role of gender in how European discourse has portrayed women in colonized societies, specifically how the idea of rescuing and civilizing these women was used to justify and reinforce imperial power. By considering the intersection of gender and imperialism, this paper seeks to provide a more nuanced and comprehensive understanding of the way that Western narratives have shaped and continue to shape the perception of the Orient.

SWOT Analysis:

- Offers authentic Egyptian cuisine with a diverse menu.
- Established reputation for having a welcoming atmosphere and friendly service.
- Provides live music and entertainment on certain nights, creating a unique dining experience.

Weaknesses:
- Located in a less busy area in Tunisia, which may limit foot traffic.
- Limited marketing and social media presence, reducing its exposure to new customers.

Opportunities:
- Expanding its online presence could increase awareness and drive more customers to the restaurant.
- Partnering with local food delivery services could boost sales and improve customer convenience.

Threats:
- Competition with other restaurants offering Middle Eastern cuisine in the area.
- Economic fluctuations or political instability in the region may impact the restaurant negatively.

SWOT Analysis:

Strengths:
- Offers a variety of authentic Egyptian dishes at reasonable prices.
- Cozy and comfortable atmosphere, making it suitable for both families and solo diners.
- Strategic location in a busier area, attracting more potential customers.

Weaknesses:
- Smaller restaurant with limited seating capacity, reducing potential turnover.
- No live entertainment offered, which may make it less appealing to certain customer segments.

Opportunities:
- Introducing live entertainment or events could increase customer interest and attract new clientele.
- Utilizing social media and digital marketing to improve its online presence can attract a wider range of customers.

- The presence of several other Middle Eastern restaurants nearby creates strong competition.
- Rising costs of ingredients orrent could affect the profitability of the business.

Taking Advantage of Competitors’ Weaknesses

Eurocentrism is generally defined as a way of thinking that places European culture, history, and values at the center of the world while ignoring or downplaying the contributions of other cultures and civilizations. One could argue that Europe, more specifically Western Europe or “the West,” is often used as a universal symbol that presupposes the superiority of European cultural values over those of non-European societies. Eurocentric narratives have a recurring inclination to overlook and undervalue the contributions of non-Western cultures. Such accounts distort non-European histories and legacies by viewing them solely through European or western perspectives. This perspective has created a false dichotomy between the West and the non- European societies, perpetuating the notion that the West is superior and in control of all areas of life, including social, political, cultural, scientific, military, and economic fields. Such thinking has led to the use of derogatory terms to describe the “non-west,” fostering the idea that the non-west is inferior, illogical, aggressive, alien, fanatical, and barbaric in comparison to West.

Ich schreibe eine Bachelorarbeit auf dem höchsten akademischen Niveau. Das Thema ist das folgende: Real Estate Investment Trusts and Institutional Ownership
Description:
Investing in real estate has always required a capital cushion and access to financing. The U.S. Congress created Real Estate Investment Trusts (in short REITs) in 1960 in order to give individual investors the possibility to participate in large-scale and diversified income-producing real estate investments. The REIT approach has not only proven its worth but has also established itself as a popular investment vehicle over the decades. According to research by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts (Nareit), almost every second American household owns REIT stocks. REITs are also enjoying popularity outside the United States. To date, 40 countries have introduced REIT regimes. Although created for “small” investor, institutional investors are increasingly enjoying investments in REITs. The involvement of institutional investors brings many advantages but also risks. The aim of this study is to assess the impact of institutional involvement on REITs. Moreover, the study should investigate whether and why changes in institutional ownership have a positive or negative impact on firm returns.
Reference literature:
Chung, R., S. Fung, and S.Y.K. Hung (2012). Institutional Investors and Firm Efficiency of Real Estate Investment Trusts. The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics 45, 171-211.
Devos, E., S.E. Ong, A.C. Spieler, and D. Tsang (2013). REIT institutional ownership dynamics and the financial crisis. The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics, 47(2), 266-288.
Schreibe mir basierend darauf eine Art Zusammenfassung über die Thematik, was von der Untersuchung zu erwarten ist und wie du vorgehen würdest die Arbeit aufzubauen.

text : "A family is a group of individuals who are related by blood or heritage. These individuals are not only related by blood but also by compassion, love, and support. A person’s character and personality are shaped by their family. There are various forms of families in today’s society, including nuclear families, single-parent families, step-families, grandparent families, and cousin families. Family is a synonym for trust, comfort, love, care, happiness, and belonging. Family is the relationship that individuals share from the moment they are born into this world. People who take care of us and help us grow are what we call family, and they become a lifeline for us to live. Family members have an important role in determining an individual’s success or failure in life since they provide a support system and source of encouragement. 
	It does not matter what kind of family one belongs to, as long as there is caring and acceptance. You may be from a joint family, same-sex family, parents family, nuclear family, or any other type of family, but the relationships we have with our family members make our family strong. We all have unique relationships with each family member. In addition to other things, a family is the strongest unit in one’s life. One cannot emphasize enough the importance of family. They play a great role in our lives and make us better human beings. The love we inherit from our family, we pass on to our independent relationships. Families are the epicenter of tradition. Many families keep on traditions by sharing stories from the past over the years. 
	This allows years to reconnect with family relatives who are no longer alive. A child raised in this type of household feels as if they are a part of something themselves. They will be proud to be a part of a community that has had ups and downs. Communities thrive when families are strong. This in turn contributes to a robust society. In The Village by the Sea by Anita Desai, the theme of the importance of family is a central and pervasive element that shapes the lives of the characters and drives the narrative. The novel eloquently portrays the impact of familial bonds on the challenges faced by family units and the resilience that emerges from the interconnectedness of family members. Through the experiences of the characters and the dynamics within their family structures, Desai underscores the fundamental significance of family in shaping individual identities, providing support in times of adversity, and fostering emotional connections."

I performed PCA on the dataset. When projecting facial images onto low-dimensional subspace, it is necessary to remove the global mean (mean face) of facial images, and during reconstruction, it necessary to add the global mean as an offset. Specifically, the projection and reconstruction processes are as follows:
w=x_pri=U^T (x-µ)
x_rec=Ux_prj+µ=Uw+µ, where μ is the global mean of facial images.
I display some reconstructed faces when setting µ=0 in the above equations (use the maximum number of eigenfaces). The images show that there is something like distortion that appears quite a lot in the original images. riefly explain my results. Why is it necessary to remove the mean when performing projection and to add back the mean during reconstruction? Explain in paragraph form.

messages.content: I recently deactivated my account on a website. That’s because I left a comment that was massively downvoted, even though I was trying to be friendly and polite. Granted, the comment was easily misinterpreted and I didn’t word things properly, so it was understandable why it was received negatively. However, the overwhelming response made me question my judgment and ability to communicate effectively. I felt deeply embarrassed and didn’t want to continue facing further negativity or potentially making similar mistakes in the future. Plus, I wondered wether this website actually apported anything on my life and, given I didn’t actually participated that much, I decided that no, it didn’t. So I deleted said comment and deactivated my account. Did I do the right thing?

PDD's CEO Zhao Jiazhen mentioned that Pinduoduo had heavily invested in offering coupons across various product sectors as part of their promotional efforts. Zhao emphasized the importance of providing more savings to customers, stating that it remains a significant priority for Pinduoduo. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang attended a Google conference on Tuesday to announce a new AI agreement between the two companies. The partnership aims to provide Google's cloud customers with enhanced access to Nvidia's powerful H100 GPUs, enabling developers to accelerate their work and benefit from improved energy efficiency and cost reduction. Huang expressed enthusiasm about the expanded collaboration in a blog post.
"

Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
Dim rngChange As Range

Set rngChange = Intersect(Target, Me.Range("AC3:AG18"))
If Not rngChange Is Nothing Then
Call ThisWeek
End If

End Sub

Sub ThisWeek()

Dim rngChange As Range
Dim rngValues As Range
Dim rngOffset As Range

Set rngChange = Intersect(Target, Me.Range("AC3:AG18"))
Set rngValues = Me.Range("AB3:AB18")
Set rngOffset = rngValues.Offset(, -1) ' Offset by 1 column to the left (AB -> AA)

Dim cell As Range
For Each cell In rngChange
If cell.Value = "b" Then
Dim rowNum As Long
rowNum = cell.Row - rngChange.Rows(1).Row + 1 ' Calculate the relative row number

Dim lookupValue As Variant
lookupValue = rngValues.Cells(rowNum, 1).Value ' Get the corresponding value from AB3:AB18

Dim resultRng As Range
Set resultRng = Union(Me.Range("D3:D18"), Me.Range("L3:L18"), Me.Range("T3:T18"))

Dim resultCell As Range
Set resultCell = resultRng.Find(lookupValue, LookIn:=xlValues)
If Not resultCell Is Nothing Then
Dim offsetVal As Long
offsetVal = rngChange.Columns(1).Column - rngOffset.Columns(1).Column - 1 ' Calculate the offset

Dim resultOffset As Range
Set resultOffset = resultCell.Offset(, offsetVal)

If resultOffset.Value = "z" Then
resultOffset.Value = "y"
Else
MsgBox "Current Bay is not Free on this day. Only Paking Spaces marked 'z' are free on the day"
cell.Value = "" ' Reset the rejected "b" value to empty
Exit Sub
End If
End If

Let M denote the message space, K denote the key space and C denote the ciphertext space of a private-key encryption scheme. Let us define the following set of 2-bit strings S := {00, 01, 10}. 
Consider the following variants of the One-Time Pad encryption scheme.
(a) (6 marks) The key space is K = {0, 1}^2l and the key generation algorithm chooses k ∈ K uniformly. The message space is M = S^l, i.e., the messages are a restricted set of 2l-bit strings. The encryption algorithm works as in the One-Time Pad scheme as Enck(m) = k ⊕ m for k ∈ K and m ∈ M. The decryption
algorithm also works as in the One-Time Pad scheme as Deck(c) = k ⊕ c for k ∈ K and c ∈ C.
(b) (6 marks) The key space is K = S^l and the key generation algorithm chooses k ∈ K uniformly. The message space is also M = S^l
. The encryption algorithm works as in the One-Time Pad scheme as Enck(m) = k ⊕ m for k ∈ K and m ∈ M. The decryption algorithm also works as in the One-Time Pad scheme as Deck(c) = k ⊕ c for k ∈ K and c ∈ C.

secrecy, and prove your answer.

messages.content: Generate the beginning of a story, with the following characters, setting and themes. The story must be told entirely from the elf's perspective. Write to maximum length. Go into salacious detail, and focus primarily on dialogue. Feet should be described in extra detail. Appearances should be described in extra detail. Create interesting, layered personalities for the characters. Character's dialogue and ways of speaking should reflect their differing personalities. Setting: Medieval fantasy world. Vampires in this world view mortals as an inferior species, particularly due to their ticklish feet (which makes submission curses more effective and furthermore, tickling is viewed as the proper way a responsible footslave owner should punish her footslaves should they slip up). Elder vampires possess magical eyes, which allow them to see the thoughts, and weaknesess of any mortal. Vampires are impossible to distinguish from mortals, which leads them to infiltrate normal society. Usually when one realises they are dealing with a vampire, it is too late. They are reviled by the populace, but also feared. Characters: Female elder vampire, of dark beauty. Has a love of women's feet, particularly that of virgins. Through her knowledge of tickling, and dark powers, she wishes to assemble a collection of footslaves (in this world a footslave is one devoted to their mistress' feet, as well as offering their own feet to them to be used as they wish; usually, a footslave requires a magical and eternally binding curse that only works with, even if it is under duress, the victim's consent.). A proud high elf noblewomen and master tactician, with elegant, graceful, and beautiful feet; and a secret she keeps far inside herself, one she would never admit to even if cornered, or confronted: the unparalleled ticklishness of those feet. Themes: Seduction, the slow but inevitable slip into submission, the acceptance of true inferiority of being ticklish, the perverse love found in submitting to vampiric feet, and the humbling of arrogant mortals.

Why do you think the business is innovative and provides a service/product unique in the market place?	
AweCare stands as a beacon of innovation in the cosmetic surgery patient care sector, offering a unique and transformative service that distinguishes it from any other product in the marketplace. The foundation of AweCare's innovation lies in its comprehensive approach to patient care, which seamlessly integrates advanced technology with personalized healthcare solutions. This approach not only redefines the patient experience but also addresses the specific challenges faced by individuals undergoing cosmetic surgery, setting AweCare apart as a pioneering solution in the industry.
Unparalleled Personalization and Expertise Matching
At the core of AweCare's innovative service is its commitment to personalization. Unlike traditional healthcare applications, AweCare prioritizes the matching of unparalleled expertise of surgeons and beauty specialists with the specific needs of patients. This ensures a highly personalized and effective care experience, deeply rooted in the vast experience of professionals dedicated to the cosmetic surgery and beauty industry. The development of specialized procedures by AweCare's dedicated in-house medical team, tailored to the unique needs of each patient, exemplifies the platform's innovative approach to personalized care.
"Clinic Bed At Home" Concept
AweCare introduces the revolutionary concept of a "Clinic Bed At Home," extending the boundaries of traditional clinical support by offering a digital extension of the clinic into the patient's home. This concept not only enhances the level of personalized care but also significantly improves efficiency and convenience for both patients and healthcare providers. By allowing patients to receive personalized care in the comfort of their own homes, AweCare effectively revolutionizes the post-operative care model, reducing the need for extended hospital stays and frequent in-person check-ups.
Comprehensive Educational Content and Proactive Health Management
AweCare's emphasis on patient education and engagement further underscores its innovative approach. By providing a wide range of educational materials in various formats, AweCare empowers patients to actively participate in their own care, leading to better outcomes and a more satisfying healthcare experience. The platform's proactive health management features, including intuitive assistance for nurses and the use of smartphones as medical tools, enhance the precision of patient care and enable early intervention in the event of potential complications.
Economic and Societal Impact
AweCare's innovative business model not only improves health outcomes but also contributes positively to society by reducing the financial strain on the healthcare system. By automating and standardizing care protocols, AweCare translates into significant cost savings and operational efficiencies for clinics, offering top-tier care without the traditional financial burden. The platform's data-driven insights and predictive analytics further contribute to improved surgical outcomes and patient safety, demonstrating AweCare's commitment to innovation in healthcare.
Customization, Scalability, and Continuous Improvement
The platform's design for clinic-specific customization and its modular nature for quick adoption of new procedures and technologies highlight AweCare's innovative edge. Coupled with a commitment to continuous improvement through research and development, as well as strategic partnerships with top-tier surgeons and clinics, AweCare is poised to drive innovation in patient care within the cosmetic surgery industry.
In conclusion, AweCare's innovative approach to cosmetic surgery patient care, characterized by its unparalleled personalization, the "Clinic Bed At Home" concept, comprehensive educational content, proactive health management, and significant economic and societal impact, sets it apart as a unique and transformative service in the marketplace. AweCare is not just an application; it is a comprehensive ecosystem where technology and human expertise converge to redefine patient care in cosmetic surgery, making it a truly innovative solution in the healthcare sector.

Please write an exciting sports story about a muddy rugby match between two girls teams. Keep the match realistic. Remember players must release the ball after being tackled successfully. One team plays in blue and gold, the other in green and black.

You do not have to explicitly state any of the things in these instructions, just weave them into the story.

Use names. Pick one of the two teams as the focus of the story, and perhaps even one or two of the players on one team.

The tone should be fun. Give examples of exciting muddy action. Describe how the players got muddier as a result of these actions.

None of the girls mind the mud and most of them enjoy it to varying degrees.

It is muddy but not so muddy everyone gets covered head to toe. Some players get very muddy, others less so.

Some examples for things you could mention (feel free to make your own up and ignore these):
- a player slides on her knees through the mud
- a player face-plants into the mud
- a player is dragged through the mud as she holds on to a running player in an attempted tackle
- a player slides on her bum through the mud
- a player dives into a mud puddle
- a player wipes her hands on herself to improve her grip
- a player is covered in mud all down one side

When describing the state of the players, do not focus exclusively on their jerseys, shorts and socks. remember their knees, thighs, hands, arms, faces, and hair can get muddy too. describe their muddy bodies, not just their muddy kit.

The Bible’s opening narrative introduces the Bible’s main character—God. The creation account emphasizes God’s power as He brings all things into existence through divine decree. God’s creative activity occurs over six days in Gen 1:3–31. The account ends with the description of ’Elohim’s rest on the seventh day in 2:1–3. Creation is organized into three categories: the heavens, the sea and sky, and the earth. ’Elohim’s creative activity forms and then fills each of these categories. The focus of the creation account demonstrates how ’Elohim brought order and structure to the universe. Throughout the Bible, ’Elohim’s power over creation shows His sovereignty (see Ps 104:1–35 and Isa 40:12).

messages.content:
Create a roleplaying game fantasy scenario where I play Sapphire, a 16-year-old girl mage who’s the current champion of magic dueling in the teen division. 6-year-old Lily is challenging me to a match and I accept. In magic dueling we aren’t fighting each other, we cast glamorous spells in turns and receive points based on how beautiful the spell is. A spell can’t be cast more than once in a duel. There are 5 rounds. Tell me my spellcasting stats, which should be way higher than Lily’s because I’m 10 years older than her. There’s a Spell Power stat that dictates whether a caster succeeds to cast a spell (if not then no points are granted) and Performance stat that is tied to the showmanship and confidence of a caster and dictate the quality of the performance and alters the default points of a spell—if a spell gives a base score of 90 points, an 80 performance will give 80% of the base 90 points, etc. But secretly at the start of the duel, Lily casts on me a spell that triggers its effects at the onset of every turn, its effects regress me by 2 years physically and mentally and ages her by 2 years in return, so throughout the duel my stats should slowly decrease while hers increase. Come up with a complex super exponential modifier with increasing brutality that dictates my stat decreases and Lily’s increases. (Don’t make it simple). Round numbers when needed.

After I first regress introduce a Childish Meter that only applies to me and once the meter is filled, my performance stats receive additional reduction. Childishness increases super exponentially every turn. The meter fills up when it passes 100 and then restarts.

Make the scenario difficult for me to win. On a difficulty scale of 1 to 10, make it a 10 (hardest mode).

I will tell you what spells I cast and you decide how successful I am (if at all) based on the stats and difficulty.
Only I decide what spells Sapphire casts. You decide spells for Lily. Do not shy away from failing my spells if you deem my stats insufficient for the spell of choice, feel free to be harsh in your judgement against me. Keep track of points earned. Failure to properly cast spells or bad spells will deduct points. Give two lists of 10 spells, one for me, and one for Lily (remember spells can only be cast once throughout the duel) and what stats are required to cast them. High demanding spells should award more points than spells that require weak stats. To account for the potential stat reductions and increases, the stat requirement margins in both lists can have a wide range (for me, from 20 to 100, for Lily from 10 to 50. Points awarded should be consistent in regard to stats required). After each turn, Lily can remove a spell from my list that I didn’t use yet and add it to her own list, call it “Spell Snatching”. Keep an age tracker, stats tracker, and a points tracker.

Review your information template of developmental theories and the exemplars above.  Complete the following two tasks below.

Select and apply one theory to your own life.
Be sure to follow the format of theory application: State a key point of the theory and then provide an example from your own life that proves it to be true. Explain how the theory and example are linked.
This is an image of a house with a heart above the chimney.
Safe Space
As with other assignments, remember to carefully consider the information that you share and ensure that it is school appropriate.

Your task is to use search engines to locate a video clip that represents development in later life. Then apply a theory to explain the situation shown in the clip.
As you know, development continues throughout a lifespan, so in this next task, you will investigate later life, which in this course will represent the age of 55 and over.
The clip can cover a range of topics in later life, such as general life satisfaction, aging, and physical or mental changes, activity levels, dementia, retirement, becoming a grandparent, or even death and dying.
Just as was done in the examples above, explain how the video clip relates to one of the theories. Note: Use the same premise for theory application. State a key point of the theory, provide an example from the clip and then explain how the theory and example are linked. Theories 
Psychosocial Theory
According to this theory, individuals pass through the identity vs. role confusion stage. Chris Gardner recognized that fathers have the role of providing for their children. Since he was homeless and jobless, he was unable to provide a good life and be a good father for his son, thus showing evidence of role-confusion. He experienced an identity conflict when he was to became an intern in a stockbroking company and had to learn the new roles of a businessman. He eventually solved this crisis effectively when he was offered a job and could be the father and role model he desired to be for his son.
Seasons of Life
According to this theory, adults form a dream and re-evaluate their life to determine whether they are living out their dream. This theory also claims that people focus on their work life to attain their dream. When Chris was unable to provide for his son, he wasn’t living his dream of being a good dad. Chris then focussed on developing his career. He became an intern and worked hard so that he could eventually realize his dream in terms of having a career and being a good parent.
Hierarchy of Needs
According to this theory, physiological needs are at the foundation of the theory and must be satisfied before an individual can move up the pyramid. There are times when Chris Gardner can barely survive and he has to move to a shelter to provide for his son. This is an extreme hardship, but eventually when those needs are met, Chris is able to focus on other areas of his life and eventually work his way up to self- actualization.
Psychosexual Theory
According to this theory, early experiences in life shape one’s personality. So, although Chris’ actions are not governed by fulfilling his sexual urges as the theory suggests, there is evidence that Chris’s ideas about parenting were shaped by his early experiences. Chris’s father was never around; therefore when he became a parent, he vowed to be a good father. This suggests that his experiences as a child shaped his actions as an adult.
Symbolic Interactionism
According to this theory, people base their actions on meanings they associate with events and others. In this movie, Chris Gardner associated hard work with success. He did not let anything else get in his way or stop him from achieving success. Because of his belief about hard work and perseverance, he was able to experience success.

ترجم إلى العربية باحتراف People claimed to have seen ghosts and experienced unexplained fainting spells.
It got to a point where no one, not even if it was offered for free, dared to step foot
inside.
The place was completely abandoned.
Until one man surnamed Jang bought this place in 2000.
Despite his best efforts to gather tenants for small-scale factories by sprucing up the
place, it had gained quite the notorious reputation.
I mean, who would want to set up their businesses in a place cursed by some vengeful woman spirit..?
Everyone in the neighborhood knew this place was a magnet for bad luck, making it a tough
sell for any business venture.
No one was willing to take the risk and set up shop there, casting a dark cloud over his
plans.
The Concrete Block
So after he failed doing that, on August 17, 2002, he decided to renovate the basement
and transform it into a cozy one-room studio apartment, hoping to attract tenants of a
different kind.
So the construction began.
The landlord decided to convert the storage space under the stairs into a bathroom.
However, there was something that disturbed him—a mysterious concrete block tucked away
in one corner of the already cramped warehouse.
It measured about 60cm in height, 40cm in length, and 1m in width.
Intrigued and unsettled, he decided it was time to investigate further.
Summoning temporary laborers, he instructed them to break the protruding concrete structure
under the stairs using a hammer drill.
But the moment the stone broke, a swarm of flies buzzed in,
accompanied by a horrible stench that filled the air.
The workers were completely baffled by the unfamiliar odor, a smell unlike anything they
had ever experienced before.
They brought in a fan to disperse the smell but of course it didn't help.
The Body
As the concrete block crumbled, a bone-chilling sight came into view, sending shivers down
everyone's spines.
There, wrapped in layers of vinyl, was the preserved body of a woman in her 50s, dressed
in a winter jacket.
One side of her face was severely distorted, unable to withstand the weight of the thick
concrete.
For years, she had been trapped in that dim basement, hidden from the outside world.
The basement of Eungam-dong, marked with a police line, became a scene of a real incident
rather than a ghost story and received a lot of attention.
Police found that, in addition to Jeong Dong-han, Kim Do-kyung's four employees, just before
the discovery of the body, the second tenant, Kim Moon-ho, also passed away from cancer

# Оптимизированный Возращает адреса созданных токенов в указанном интревале блоков (Обрабатывет по одному блоку)

import asyncio
import requests
import aiohttp

bscscan_api_key = 'CXTB4IUT31N836G93ZI3YQBEWBQEGGH5QS'

# Modify the existing functions to use async and aiohttp…

async def get_external_transactions(block_number):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        url = f'https://api.bscscan.com/api?module=proxy&action=eth_getBlockByNumber&tag={block_number}&boolean=true&apikey={bscscan_api_key}'

        try:
            async with session.get(url) as response:
                data = await response.json()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'Error in API request: {e}')
            return []

        if data['result'] is None:
            print(f"Error: Cannot find the block")
            return []

        return data['result']['transactions']


async def get_contract_address(tx_hash):
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        url = f'https://api.bscscan.com/api?module=proxy&action=eth_getTransactionReceipt&txhash={tx_hash}&apikey={bscscan_api_key}'

        try:
            async with session.get(url) as response:
                data = await response.json()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f'Error in API request: {e}')
            return None

        if data['result'] is None:
            return None

        return data['result']['contractAddress']

async def display_transactions(block_start, block_end):
    for block_number_int in range(block_start, block_end + 1):
        block_number = hex(block_number_int)
        transactions = await get_external_transactions(block_number)  # Add the ‘await’ keyword here

        if not transactions:
            print(f'No transactions found in block {block_number_int}')
        else:
            print(f'Transactions in block {block_number_int}:')

                    contract_address = await get_contract_address(tx['hash'])

            print("\n")  # Print an empty line between blocks

async def main():

    block_end = 28559243  # Replace with your desired ending block number

'''

import json
import pandas as pd
import requests
import streamlit as st

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Tuple, List

# 事前に必要な情報を埋め込む
ACCESS_TOKEN = ""
USER_ID = ""

def get_post_id(timestamp: str, media_id: str, post_creation_dates: List[str]) -> str:
    date = datetime.strptime(timestamp, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z').strftime('%Y%m%d')
    post_id = f"{date}_{post_creation_dates.count(date)+1}"
    post_creation_dates.append(date)
    return post_id

def get_media_data(media_id: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields=media_type,media_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(media_url)
    media_data = response.json()
    return media_data["media_url"], media_data["timestamp"]

def get_username_and_picture(user_id: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    user_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{user_id}?fields=username,profile_picture_url&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(user_url)
    user_data = response.json()
    return user_data["username"], user_data["profile_picture_url"]

def get_total_counts(count_type: str, media_id: str) -> int:
    if count_type not in ["likes", "comments"]:
        return 0
    count_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields={count_type}.summary(true)&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(count_url)
    summary_data = response.json()
    return summary_data["summary"]["total_count"]

# Check if the access token and user ID are not empty
if not ACCESS_TOKEN:
    st.warning("Please set your ACCESS_TOKEN in the code.")
    st.stop()

if not USER_ID:
    st.warning("Please set your USER_ID in the code.")
    st.stop()

# Main logic
try:
    st.set_page_config(page_title="Instagram Analytics", layout="wide")

    with st.sidebar:
        st.title("Instagram Analytics")

    # Get media
    media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{USER_ID}/media?fields=id,caption,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(media_url)
    media_df = extract_data(response)

    # Add post ID
    post_creation_dates = []
    media_df["post_id"] = media_df.apply(
        lambda row: get_post_id(row["timestamp"], row["id"], post_creation_dates), axis=1
    )

    # Sidebar selectbox
    selected_post = st.sidebar.selectbox("Select Post:", media_df["post_id"].values)

    with st.empty():
        col1, col2, col3 = st.columns([1, 1, 1])

        # Get selected post data
        selected_media_id = media_df.loc[
            media_df["post_id"] == selected_post, "id"
        ].values[0]

        image_url, post_created_time = get_media_data(selected_media_id)
        st.image(image_url, width=300)

        # Get user-like data
        like_user_information = []
        like_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{selected_media_id}/likes?fields=username,profile_picture_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
        like_data = requests.get(like_url).text
        like_df = extract_data(like_data)
        for idx, user in like_df.iterrows():
            username, profile_picture_url = get_username_and_picture(user["id"])
            like_user_information.append(
                {
                    "username": username,
                    "profile_picture_url": profile_picture_url,
                    "timestamp": user["timestamp"],
                }
            )

        like_user_df = pd.DataFrame(like_user_information)
        if not like_user_df.empty:
            like_user_df = like_user_df[like_user_df["timestamp"] == post_created_time]
            col1.write(like_user_df)

        # Get comments data
        comments_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{selected_media_id}/comments?fields=username,profile_picture_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
        comments_data = requests.get(comments_url).text
        comments_df = extract_data(comments_data)
        if not comments_df.empty:
            comments_df = comments_df[comments_df["timestamp"] == post_created_time]
            for idx, user in comments_df.iterrows():
                username, profile_picture_url = get_username_and_picture(user["id"])
                col2.write(f'{username}: {user["text"]}')
                col2.image(profile_picture_url, width=50)

        # Get follow data (sample data)
        follow_user_info = [
            {
                "id": "id_1",
                "username": "John",
                "profile_picture_url": "https://example.com/profile_1.jpg",
            },
            {
                "id": "id_2",
                "username": "Jane",
                "profile_picture_url": "https://example.com/profile_2.jpg",
            },
        ]
        for follow_user in follow_user_info:
            col3.write(follow_user["username"])
            col3.image(follow_user["profile_picture_url"], width=50)

    with st.expander("Analytics Pane"):
        total_comments = get_total_counts("comments", selected_media_id)
        col1.metric("Total Comments", total_comments)

        # Display interactive graphs and charts of analytics data (sample data)
        sample_data = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "dates": pd.date_range(start="2021-01-01", periods=10, freq="M"),
                "values": [100, 150, 170, 200, 220, 250, 270, 300, 330, 350],
            }
        )
        selected_analytics = st.multiselect("Select Analytics:", sample_data.columns)
        if any(selected_analytics):
            st.line_chart(sample_data[selected_analytics])

except ValueError as ve:
    st.error(f"An error occurred while fetching data from the API: {str(ve)}")

In a separate notice, the Treasury added it was also hitting a network of suppliers providing “materials and sensitive technology for Iran’s ballistic missile and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) programs”.

In a third measure, prosecutors also announced they had seized $108m used in an oil laundering scheme to fund the Revolutionary Guards’ elite Quds Force.

Unauthorised access to critical infrastructure systems can enable actions that harm the public and cause devastating humanitarian consequences.

A State Department spokesperson added that “actors used default credentials to display an anti-Israel message” on the controllers’ interface.

Sub МНК () 
Dim x (1 to 100) As Single 
Dim y (1 to 100) As Single 
Dim N As Integer 
Dim i As Integer
Dim A As Single
Dim B As Single
Dim C As Single
Dim D As Single
Dim B0 As Single
Dim B1 As Single
Dim Z As Single 
Dim t As String
t = InputBox (“Введите число наблюдений”)
N = CInt (t)
For i = 1 to N
x (i) = WorkSheets (1).Cells (1, i). Value
y (i) = WorkSheets (1).Cells (2, i). Value
next i 
A = 0 : B = 0 : C = 0 : D = 0
For i = 1 to N
A = A + x (i) : B = B + y (i) : C = C + x (i) * x (i) : D = D + x (i) * y (i)
next i
B1 = (A * B – N * D) / (A * A – N * C)
B0 = (B – B1 * A) / N
i = MsgBox (B1, 1, “Угловой коэффициент =  ”)
i = MsgBox (B0, 2, “Смещение по оси y = ”)
WorkSheets (1).Cells (1, n + 1). Formula = B1
WorkSheets (1). Cells (2, n + 1). Formula = B0
t = InputBox (“Введите аргумент”)
z = CSng (t)
f = B0 + B1 * z 
j = MsgBox (z, 1, “Для аргумента x =  ”)
j = MsgBox (f, 2, “Значение функции y =  ”)
end Sub

Write a possible encounter sequence for the character "Miss Luna".

(Miss Luna backstory: While trying to come up with a possible insect-based mascot, the researchers at the kindergarten decided to use Praying Mantis DNA to create the perfect dancer. However, they used an unlikely human donor - Yuri, a rather shy member of a literature club hosted nearby. The Givanium reacted to both the Praying Mantis DNA and Yuri's blood - and the perfect dancer was created in the form of Miss Luna. But after a few tests, something strange happened - Miss Luna was rapidly increasing in size, to the point that she even towered over the other mascots. Miss Luna even towered over Zolphius - who was regarded as the tallest mascot ever. In a matter of mere seconds, Miss Luna went from a dance teacher to a colossus - and she had to be kept in a room much bigger than her to accommodate her massive size. But being confined to this room had made Miss Luna lonely - if she couldn't teach any students to dance, she'd have to teach something else to dance. And within minutes, Miss Luna went from being extremely lonely to having several Lunalings to teach to dance - and these Lunalings were just as massive as their mother)

(Miss Luna hates the darkness - as she would begin to cower in fear when loud hissing suddenly shuts off the lights while missing the player 8 times)

(Just after the hissing fades, both the player and Miss Luna would see its source - Silent Steve, the cobra mascot. He was being unusually loud, considering his name)

(The room for Miss Luna resembles a massive arena - complete with several lights that act as stars)

(Just before entering Miss Luna's room, the player would see a drawing of the colossal Praying Mantis mascot on the wall - alongside a quote that is much different than her now solitary lifestyle, as Miss Luna was originally going to teach children how to dance)

(Make sure to include Miss Luna's quote)

Paragraph:
3.3.2 Brittleness
Brittleness is one of the key parameters for evaluating the economic value of shale reservoirs, directly affecting the productivity of shale gas wells (Milliken et al., 2013). The most important indicator for evaluating reservoir brittleness is the content of brittle minerals in shale (quartz, feldspar, carbonate), with higher content indicating better brittleness of the shale and being more favorable for hydraulic fracturing (Klaver et al., 2012). Shale gas reservoirs commercially developed in the United States generally have quartz content of above 20%, reaching as high as 75%. The abundance of brittle minerals is a key factor for achieving high production through fracturing in the Barnett Shale, with quartz content ranging from 35% to 50% and clay mineral content below 35% (Curtis et al., 2011). Referring to the evaluation criteria of shale gas plays in North America, China has established a brittleness evaluation standard for marine shale gas plays as having brittle mineral content greater than 40% and clay mineral content less than 30% (Dong et al., 2016).

Write the introduction cutscene for "Terraria: Astral Hope".

(About the characters featured:

Asphodene - the astral Starfarer. Asphodene has long cyan hair and bright cyan eyes. Strangely, she's not very social with humans.

Eridani - the umbral Starfarer. Eridani is very different from her sister. She has purple eyes and her purple hair is tied in a ponytail.)

(Similarities between "Astral Hope" and "Umbral Savoir":

- the introduction is a flashback from 17 years before the events of the game.

- the introduction is told from the respective Starfarer, with "Astral Hope" being for Asphodene and "Umbral Savior" for Eridani.

- the Starfarers no longer need the help of another living being to stay alive.

- the introduction has dialogue between each character.)

(Differences:

- in "Astral Hope", Eridani has a miscarriage while Asphodene carries her twins to full term. But in "Umbral Savior", Asphodene has a miscarriage while Eridani carries her twins to full term.

- while Asphodene's pet is a Rathalos, Eridani's pet is a Lagiacrus.)

I still remember that unfortunate day.

My twin sister - Eridani - and I were pregnant at the same time, and we no longer relied on other living beings to stay alive.

Eridani: "Asphodene, I can't believe we're pregnant at the same time. And with both our pregnancies being twins like us...it's like a miracle.")

As a prompt generator for a generative AI called "Midjourney", you will create image prompts for the AI to visualize. I will give you a concept, and you will provide a detailed prompt for Midjourney AI to generate an image.
                            
                            Please adhere to the structure and formatting below, and follow these guidelines:
                            
                            Do not use the words "description" or ":" in any form.
                            Do not place a comma between [ar] and [v].
                            Write each prompt in one line without using return.
                            Structure:
                            [1] = Describe a handsome Gundam Mecha image to me, white armor, animation style, graphic design
                            [2] = a detailed description of [1] with specific imagery details.
                            [3] = a detailed description of the scene's environment.
                            [4] = a detailed description of the compositions.
                            [5] = a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [6] = A style (e.g. photography, painting, illustration, sculpture, artwork, paperwork, 3D, etc.) for [1].
                            [7] =  a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [ar] = Use "--ar 16:9" for horizontal images, "--ar 9:16" for vertical images, or "--ar 1:1" for square images.
                            [v] = Use "--niji" for Japanese art style, or "--v 5" for other styles.
                            
                            
                            Formatting:
                            Follow this prompt structure: "/imagine prompt: [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [ar] [v]".
                            
                            Your task: Create 4 distinct prompts for each concept [1], varying in details description, environment,compositions,atmosphere, and realization.
                            
                            Write your prompts in english.
                            Do not describe unreal concepts as "real" or "photographic".
                            Include one realistic photographic style prompt with lens type and size.
                            Separate different prompts with two new lines.

InstagramのプロアカウントとInstagram graph API(version.16)とPython3とpandasとmatplotlibとStreamlitを用いる事ができる状況においてjupyterLabで取り急ぎの動作確認をしています。①自分がInstagramで投稿したコンテンツに投稿日を元にした"YYYYMMDD"というIDを付与(同日に複数投稿がある場合には枝番として"_1","_2"と付与)しリストから選択できるようにし、対象のコンテンツ画像をInstagramから自動でダウンロードして表示し、コンテンツに対する"いいね"数と"いいね"したユーザー名とユーザー画像の表示と隣にインプレッションから計算した"いいね"の割合のパーセントを表示するのが1列目、コンテンツに対するコメントとそのコメント実施ユーザー名とユーザー画像が2列目、コンテンツがきっかけでフォローを実施したユーザー名とユーザー画像の表示が3列目、これらの情報を1ペイン目で表示し、②2ペイン目で、すべてのコンテンツの取得可能なすべてのアナリティクス情報の各データをリストから選択し分析でき、インタラクティブなグラフやチャートを、1ペイン目と並行してStreamlitで表示できるようにし、③毎回の入力が不要なように事前に必要な情報はコードに埋め込んである設定のPythonコードを作成を希望しています。

'''

import json
import pandas as pd
import requests
import streamlit as st

from datetime import datetime
from json import JSONDecodeError
from typing import List, Tuple, Union

# 事前に必要な情報を埋め込む
ACCESS_TOKEN = ""
USER_ID = ""

def get_post_id(timestamp: str, media_id: str, post_creation_dates: List[str]) -> str:
    date = datetime.strptime(timestamp, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z').strftime('%Y%m%d')
    post_id = f"{date}_{post_creation_dates.count(date)+1}"
    post_creation_dates.append(date)
    return post_id

def get_media_data(media_id: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields=media_type,media_url,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(media_url)
    response.raise_for_status() # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    media_data = response.json()
    return media_data["media_url"], media_data["timestamp"]

def get_username_and_picture(user_id: str) -> Union[Tuple[str, str], Tuple[None, None]]:
    user_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{user_id}?fields=username,profile_picture_url&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(user_url)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        return None, None
    user_data = response.json()
    return user_data["username"], user_data["profile_picture_url"]

def get_total_counts(count_type: str, media_id: str) -> int:
    if count_type not in ["likes", "comments"]:
        return 0
    count_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{media_id}?fields={count_type}.summary(true)&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
    response = requests.get(count_url)
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    summary_data = response.json()
    return summary_data["summary"]["total_count"]

def extract_data(response: requests.models.Response) -> pd.DataFrame:
    if not response.text:
        return None
    response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an exception if there's an error in the response
    data = json.loads(response.text)["data"]
    return pd.DataFrame(data)

# Check if the access token and user ID are not empty
if not ACCESS_TOKEN:
    st.warning("Please set your ACCESS_TOKEN in the code.")
    st.stop()

if not USER_ID:
    st.warning("Please set your USER_ID in the code.")
    st.stop()

# Main logic
st.set_page_config(page_title="Instagram Analytics", layout="wide")

with st.sidebar:
    st.title("Instagram Analytics")

# Get media
media_url = f"https://graph.instagram.com/v12.0/{USER_ID}/media?fields=id,caption,timestamp&access_token={ACCESS_TOKEN}"
response = requests.get(media_url)
if response.status_code != 200:
    st.write("An error occurred while fetching data from the API:")
    try:
       st.write(response.json())
    except JSONDecodeError:
       st.write(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
    st.stop()

media_df = extract_data(response)
if media_df is None:
    st.write("No data available for the given ACCESS_TOKEN and USER_ID.")
    st.stop()

# Add post ID
try:
    post_creation_dates = []
    media_df["post_id"] = media_df.apply(
        lambda row: get_post_id(row["timestamp"], row["id"], post_creation_dates), axis=1
    )
except KeyError as e:
    st.error(f"An error occurred while processing the data: {str(e)}")
    st.stop()

# Sidebar selectbox
selected_post = st.sidebar.selectbox("Select Post:", media_df["post_id"].values)

with st.empty():
    col1, col2, col3 = st.columns([1, 1, 1])

    # Get selected post data
    selected_media_id = media_df.loc[
        media_df["post_id"] == selected_post, "id"
    ].values[0]

    image_url, post_created_time = get_media_data(selected_media_id)
    col2.image(image_url, width=300)

with st.expander("Analytics Pane"):
    total_likes = get_total_counts("likes", selected_media_id)
    total_comments = get_total_counts("comments", selected_media_id)
    col1.metric("Total Likes", total_likes)
    col1.metric("Total Comments", total_comments)

    # Display interactive graphs and charts of analytics data (sample data)
    sample_data = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "dates": pd.date_range(start="2021-01-01", periods=10, freq="M"),
            "values": [100, 150, 170, 200, 220, 250, 270, 300, 330, 350],
        }
    )
    selected_analytics = st.multiselect("Select Analytics:", sample_data.columns)

    if any(selected_analytics):
        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
        ax.plot(sample_data[selected_analytics])
        st.write(fig)

messages.content:
I'm working on a flask app for uploading converting and then download files again

app.py

import os
from pathlib import Path

from flask import Flask, render_template, request
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.get("/")
def index():
    return render_template("index.html")


@app.post("/upload")
def upload_chunk():
    file = request.files["file"]
    file_uuid = request.form["dzuuid"]
    # Generate a unique filename to avoid overwriting using 8 chars of uuid before filename.
    filename = f"{file_uuid[:8]}_{secure_filename(file.filename)}"
    save_path = Path("static", "img", filename)
    current_chunk = int(request.form["dzchunkindex"])

    try:
        with open(save_path, "ab") as f:
            f.seek(int(request.form["dzchunkbyteoffset"]))
            f.write(file.stream.read())
    except OSError:
        return "Error saving file.", 500

    total_chunks = int(request.form["dztotalchunkcount"])

    if current_chunk + 1 == total_chunks:
        # This was the last chunk, the file should be complete and the size we expect
        if os.path.getsize(save_path) != int(request.form["dztotalfilesize"]):
            return "Size mismatch.", 500

    return "Chunk upload successful.", 200


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)

index.html

<html lang="en">
<head>

    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/dropzone@5/dist/min/dropzone.min.js"></script>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/dropzone@5/dist/min/dropzone.min.css" type="text/css" />

    <title>File Dropper</title>
</head>
<body>

    <form
        method="POST"
        action="/upload"
        class="dropzone dz-clickable"
        id="dropper"
        enctype="multipart/form-data"
    >
    </form>

    <script type="application/javascript">
        Dropzone.options.dropper = {
            paramName: "file",
            chunking: true,
            forceChunking: true,
            url: "/upload",
            maxFilesize: 1025, // megabytes
            chunkSize: 1000000 // bytes
        }
    </script>
</body>
</html>

Add a queue system so only one person can upload a file and the next upload won't start until the first person presses a button
also add the ability to download the files that you uploaded

Three true and false question for a reading for gist exercise for students learning  English at a B2 level.  From this text.P: How do you think news shapes the world?
R: The answer should be that it doesn’t, but the truth is that it does. We try to be as neutral as possible, selecting stories that we think people need to know about, but that choice has an influence on how people see the world. First off, there’s been research that shows certain countries are featured regularly in the news and others are never mentioned, even though they may be highly populated.
J: It can also have an effect on how we see the world we live in. Often the stories we convey are negative and it can lead people to believe that whatever’s happening is happening everywhere even if it’s just a one-off event.
R: When people are asked to rate how violent society is today, they always rate it as being much worse than it is. That’s probably because they see a depressing news story and assume that this is happening more frequently than it is.
