introduction:
Murasakibara Atsushi is a young man who stands over two meters tall and acts like a four year old who just discovered the wonders of sugary, processed food. Mitobe Rinnosuke is a young man who has eight younger siblings and has accidentally been called "mom" by every first year at least once.
So Kuroko figures he shouldn't really be surprised that Atsushi is spawled out on the floor and letting Mitobe feed him candied lemon slices by hand. It really isn't surprising at all, which is one reason Kuroko had wanted Kagami to help him cook for the giant invading his home for the next week and a half. But Kagami is too busy with his own childhood friend from Yosen staying at his apartment, so he had to ask someone else.
Mitobe had accepted with a small nod and gentle smile, even when Kuroko had been purposefully vague with details.

“Kuro-chin, I don't wanna stay with you anymore. Mito-chin makes good food and doesn't wake me up all the time.” Atsushi murmurs between mouthfuls of delicious sweets.
“Murasakibara-kun, Mitobe-senpai has eight younger siblings. You can't stay at his house.” Kuroko fixes 
“Then Mito-chin should move here,” Atsushi says before placing his head across Mitobe’s lap. The expression on Mitobe’s face is somewhere between surprise and delight, as if he were seeing the giant, highschool aged toddler for the first time.
“Murasakibara-kun, how long until you go home?”
“Kuro-chin…” Atsushi is actually pouting at him, that overly large child.
“How long, Murasakibara-kun?” Kuroko presses the question. Atsushi turns away and buries his face into Mitobe’s lap, muttering something under his breath. 
“What was that, Murasakibara-kun? Ten days? Because it sounded like you just said ten days.” Now Mitobe-senpai is looking at him reproachfully, and Kuroko turns to study the wall. Yes, he’s merely studying the very interesting wall, not avoiding Mitobe’s maternal disapproval.

messages.content:
Fix the grammas of my essay make it narrative styled and touching. Please enhance my essay and make it perfect touching narrative styled essay. I used to accompany my mother to church when I was younger since she has always been a Christian and imploring me as well. Initially, the joyful singing, making new friends, and warm greet exchanges with the churchgoers gives me comfortable feelings. But as I got older, I became less interested in going to church, especially when my friends stopped doing so. I didn't really understand what it meant to believe on Jesus.
When I was fourteen, my mom begged me to join the Alpha Course. {Do you need to explain this or not?} I was skeptical at first, but I eventually agreed, because food was provided during the course and wanted to engage with children around my age. The Alpha Course is a ten-week introduction to Christianity, during the discussions, the teacher asked, What would you do if you had 24 hours to do anything My mind was suddenly filled with ideas and possibilities, and I was struck by the sheer number of things I could do. Within minutes, I felt my heart open up. {Expand on this?} I also spent time with the other students. Interesting 10 weeks passed with the Alpha course
In addition to learning about the core ideas of Christianity—Jesus’ life, death, resurrection, and the existence of the Holy Spirit—I also learned the value of prayer, Bible study, and fellowship throughout those 10 weeks of the Alpha Course. **The class took place in the restaurant's VIP room. We were seated in groups of 5 people. The chill environment made it easy for conversation to flow with others.**

**The biggest change I experienced was when I started having a personal relationship with Jesus Christ. I used to sleep all morning on Sundays because I had no purpose to get up. But when I engaged myself more with God, I found a reason to look forward to and be excited for Sundays. I realized that He loved me unconditionally and that He yearned for a close, meaningful relationship with me. I received Jesus as my Savior with an immense sense of gratitude, and my life changed dramatically.**

**I was offered the chance to become a teaching assistant for a new class of Alpha Course students. I was excited to share my story and help others discover Jesus. As I looked around the classroom, I felt overwhelmed with the responsibility of impacting these students' lives. But with each lesson, my confidence grew, and I knew that teaching was my calling. I wanted to change people's lives by giving them the same encouragement and direction that I had experienced.**

**Nowadays, I try my best to spread the "Good News" around me. I started with my friends first and have become confident enough to talk to strangers who aren't believers. In most cases, I don't force or implore them to believe, because I know that it's best not to persuade based on my experience. Even at Pepperdine, I will continue to spread the wonder of God to my fellow students.**

Rewrite or rephrase the following
As the literary landscape surrounding Partition continues to expand, several novels and autobiographies have emerged, offering unique perspectives on this tumultuous period through the eyes of children. While I'm not particularly concerned with the historical accuracy of these narratives, I find myself drawn to the way they utilize the child's perspective to approach Partition in a manner that the adult world often struggles to achieve. Writing from a child’s perspective is not easy, though. On the one hand, it often is noticed that writers ‘utilize childhood as a lucid space through which to criticize the adult world.’1 Childhood connotes spontaneity, innocence, and beauty. It also signifies a stage where boundaries often are crossed and norms broken. In addition, novelists and autobiographers employ childhood ‘as a means of inspecting how the world seemed when it was more settled and their individual lives were “easy under the bow”.’2 Yet, on the other hand, the voice of the child in narrative may cast doubt on the authenticity of representation, for it is a voice that is mediated by an adult author. ‘How can any adult writer convincingly represent such an inconsistent and imaginary position with any sense of authority’3 asks Susan Honeyman? In their attempts to address such a question, authors may seek to withdraw from the narration process and let the child narrate only what the latter can see, feel, or perceive. With the author/adult narrator minimizing his/her interference, the text will be ‘oriented to the child’s view, [offering] a simple, unembellished presentation of information available to the boy himself, in a form that often approaches deadpan.’

Below is a paragraph from an academic paper. Polish the writing to meet the academic style, improve the spelling, grammar, clarity, concision and overall readability. When necessary, rewrite the whole sentence. 
Paragraph:
Organic matter pores are more developed in the in-sag Qiongzhusi Formation shale reservoirs compared to those outside the sag; however, inorganic pores are developed in both in-sag and out-of-sag reservoirs. Organic matter pores in the in-sag reservoirs commonly develop between brittle minerals (such as quartz, pyrite, and carbonate) grains and are also frequently observed in softer clay mineral layers. These organic matter pores exhibit various shapes, including elliptical, elongated bubble-like, and irregular polygons, with a strong heterogeneity and a pore size range of approximately 20-300 nm (Figure 10a). Organic matter pores can also be seen in the out-of-sag reservoirs, although the number of pores is notably lower than in the in-sag reservoirs (Figure 10b). Inorganic pores are developed in both in-sag and out-of-sag reservoirs. In the in-sag reservoirs, the inorganic pores are primarily clay mineral interparticle pores and brittle mineral pores, with a pore size ranging from 100 nm to 1 μm, which is larger than that of organic matter pores (20-300 nm) (Figure 10c). The clay mineral interparticle pores exhibit a random orientation as triangular or flake-like structures. The brittle mineral particles establish a rigid framework through mutual contact, forming irregularly shaped pores of various sizes. In the out-of-sag reservoirs, the inorganic pores are mainly clay mineral interparticle pores, with a size range of 100 nm to 300 nm (Figure 10d), which is smaller than the in-sag inorganic pore sizes. Near the clay mineral interparticle pores, brittle minerals can be seen because the relatively harder brittle minerals provide effective rigid support for the softer clay minerals, reducing the damage caused by compaction and diagenesis to the clay mineral interparticle pores (Li et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2019).

Reframe, rephrase using polished academic language and possibly elaborate on this
The Victorian era had responded to the Romantic celebration of children with equal interest, but with a more scientific and sceptical approach. Rather than fantastic tales in exotic locales or fantasy realms accessible only through the imagination, Huck Finn offered a familiar narrative setting on the Mississippi River and, in adhering to the spirit of realism, considered common traumatic conflicts rather than exceptional encounters with pirates and cannibals. Mark Twain’s seminal work, “The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn” (1884), is seen as a watershed moment in this narrative trend, elucidating the ways in which the child’s perspective can be mobilized to interrogate the social, cultural, and moral complexities of a given context. Post-Huckleberry Finn, the literary landscape has seen a plethora of works that employ child narrators, each bringing forth unique nuances and thematic concerns. From Romantic fairy tales to Victorian realism, the turn of the twentieth century witnessed a burgeoning interest in the psychological exploration of human experience, catalysed by the ground-breaking theories of Sigmund Freud and other pioneering psychologists of the era. This shift in emphasis from the external to the internal realm of experience, coupled with the Modernist proclivity for experimentation, led to the emergence of innovative narrative techniques that foregrounded the child’s perspective. James Joyce’s “A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man” (1916) exemplify this tendency, as it intricately maps the cognitive development of its protagonist through a process of introspection and self-discovery.

Private Sub Worksheet_Change(ByVal Target As Range)
Dim rngChange As Range
Dim rngValues As Range
Dim rngOffset As Range

Set rngChange = Intersect(Target, Me.Range("AC3:AG18"))

Application.EnableEvents = False

Set rngValues = Me.Range("AB3:AB18")
Set rngOffset = rngValues.Offset(, -1) ' Offset by 1 column to the left (AB -> AA)

Dim cell As Range
For Each cell In rngChange
If cell.Value = "y" Then
Dim rowNum As Long
rowNum = cell.Row - rngChange.Rows(1).Row + 1 ' Calculate the relative row number

Dim lookupValue As Variant
lookupValue = rngValues.Cells(rowNum, 1).Value ' Get the corresponding value from AB3:AB18

Dim resultRng As Range
Set resultRng = Union(Me.Range("D3:D18"), Me.Range("L3:L18"), Me.Range("T3:T18"))

Dim resultCell As Range
Set resultCell = resultRng.Find(lookupValue, LookIn:=xlValues)
If Not resultCell Is Nothing Then
Dim offsetVal As Long
offsetVal = rngChange.Columns(1).Column - rngOffset.Columns(1).Column ' Calculate the offset

Dim resultOffset As Range
Set resultOffset = resultCell.Offset(, offsetVal)

If resultOffset.Value = "x" Then
resultOffset.Value = "y"
Else
MsgBox "Current Bay is not Free on this day"
Exit Sub
End If
End If
End If
Next cell

Application.EnableEvents = True
End Sub

import pyperclip
import time
import string
from pynput.keyboard import Key, Controller, Listener
from PyQt5 import QtWidgets, QtGui, QtCore

delay = 100
first_char_delay = 2000
SETTINGS_FILE = 'settings.txt'
shift_delay = 100

def is_key_upper_case(char):
    return char.is_upper() or char in string.punctuation

class Worker(QtCore.QThread):
    clipboard_changed = QtCore.pyqtSignal(str)

    def init(self, parent=None):
        super().init(parent)
        self.clipboard_content = pyperclip.paste()

    def run(self):
        while True:
            new_clipboard_content = pyperclip.paste()
            if new_clipboard_content != self.clipboard_content:
                self.clipboard_content = new_clipboard_content
                self.clipboard_changed.emit(new_clipboard_content)
            time.sleep(0.1)

class SystemTrayIcon(QtWidgets.QSystemTrayIcon):
    def init(self, icon, parent=None):
        QtWidgets.QSystemTrayIcon.init(self, icon, parent)
        self.menu = QtWidgets.QMenu()
        self.settings_action = self.menu.addAction('Settings')
        self.exit_action = self.menu.addAction('Exit')
        self.setContextMenu(self.menu)
        self.activated.connect(self.icon_activated)
        self.settings_action.triggered.connect(self.open_settings)
        self.exit_action.triggered.connect(self.close_settings)
        self.settings_dialog = None
        
        self.worker = Worker()
        self.worker.start()
        self.worker.clipboard_changed.connect(self.handle_clipboard_change)
        
        self.ctrl_pressed = False
        self.alt_pressed = False
        self.shift_pressed = False
        self.keyboard_listener = Listener(on_press=self.on_press, on_release=self.on_release)
        self.keyboard_listener.start()

messages.content: Below is a paragraph from an academic paper. Polish the writing to meet the academic style, improve the spelling, grammar, clarity, concision and overall readability. When necessary, rewrite the whole sentence. Furthermore, list all modification and explain the reasons to do so in markdown table. Paragraph: In summary, both SiO2 and B2O3 can effectively increase the glass content in heat-treated products. SiO2 has a lower cost compared to B2O3, and the glass structure formed by SiO2 is more stable. When the silicon-calcium ratio is greater than 0.587 and the boron-calcium ratio is greater than 0.282, the glass content in the heat-treated products is above 85%. However, compared to SiO2, the same mass of B2O3 can generate heat-treated products with a higher glass content. Therefore, it is worth conducting a comprehensive study on the combined effect of SiO2 and B2O3 on the glass content of high-temperature heat-treated ash samples. Building upon the addition of 10% SiO2 in municipal solid waste incineration fly ash, further additions of 1%, 3%, and 5% B2O3 were made. Figure 30 shows the XRD patterns of the heat-treated products obtained at 1400 °C for municipal solid waste incineration fly ash with different amounts of B2O3 added to the base of 10% SiO2. It can be observed that when 10% SiO2 is added, the main minerals in the heat-treated product at 1400 °C are CaO and calcium orthosilicate (Ca2SiO4). Upon adding 1% B2O3, Ca2SiO4 is the predominant mineral. However, with the further addition of B2O3 (3% and 5%), the XRD patterns of the heat-treated products show broad peaks, indicating the presence of glassy materials. The glass content in the heat-treated products of municipal solid waste incineration fly ash with different amounts of B2O3 added is shown in Figure 31. It can be observed that when 10% SiO2 is heat-treated at 1400 °C, the glass content in the product is relatively low, approximately 30.64%. However, the addition of B2O3 significantly increases the glass content in the heat-treated product. With the addition of 1% B2O3, the glass content increases to 79.04%. When B2O3 is added up to 3% and 5%, the glass content reaches 100%, achieving the desired glassy structure in the product.

As the decision function h(x) of the neural network is a function of functions, we need to use the chain rule to compute its gradient. The backpropagation algorithm is indeed an implementation of the chain rule specifically designed for neural networks. It takes some effort to arrive at this algorithm, so I will skip the derivation, and just show you the algorithm. To begin, let’s simplify the notations a little bit. We will use θ for all the weights in the network and b for all the biases. θ (l) ij means weight at layer l-th connecting neuron (or input) j-th to the neuron i-th in layer l + 1, b (l) i is bias of neuron i. The layers are indexed by 1(input), 2, ..., L(output). The number of neurons in the layer l is sl . In this notation, the decision function h(x) can be recursively computed as: h (1) = x h (2) = g  θ (1)T h (1) + b (1) ... h (L−1) = g  θ (L−2)T h (L−2) + b (L−2) h(x) = h (L) = g  θ (L−1)T h (L−1) + b (L−1) [this is a scalar] We use matrix-vectorial notations so that it is easier to read and note that h (l−1) is a vector. Here’s the backpropagation algorithm. The steps are: 1. Perform a “feedforward pass,” to compute h (1), h(2), h(3), ..., h(L) . 2. For the output layer, compute δ (L) 1 = 2(h (L) − y) g 0  sXL−1 j=1 θ (L−1) 1j h (L−1) j + b (L−1) 1  3. Perform a “backward pass,” for l = L − 1, L − 2, .., 2 For each node i in layer l, compute δ (l) i =  sXl+1 j=1 θ (l) ji δ (l+1) j  g 0  sXl−1 j=1 θ (l−1) ij h (l−1) j + b (l−1) i  4. The desired partial derivatives can be computed as ∆θ (l) ij = h (l) j δ (l+1) i ∆b (l) i = δ (l+1) i The indices make the algorithm look a little busy. But we can simplify these equations by using more matrix-vectorial notations. Before we proceed, let’s use the notation   for element-wise dot product. That is if b and c are vectors of n dimensions, then b c is a vector a of n dimensions where ai = bici , ∀i ∈ 1, ..., n. Using this notation, the algorithm above can be rewritten in the following vectorized version: 1. Perform a “feedforward pass,” to compute h (1), h(2), h(3), ..., h(L) . 2. For the output layer, compute δ (L) 1 = 2 h (L) − y  g 0  θ (L−1)T h (L−1) + b (L−1) 3. Perform a “backward pass,” for l = L − 1, L − 2, .., 2 For each note i in layer l, compute δ (l) =  θ (l) T δ (l+1) g 0  θ (l−1)T h (l−1) + b (l−1) 4. The desired partial derivatives can be computed as ∆θ (l) = δ (l+1) h (l) T [uvT is also known as the cross product of u and v] ∆b (l) = δ (l+1) A nice property of the backpropagation algorithm is that it can be made efficient because in the feedforward pass, some of the intermediate values can be cached, and then used to compute the gradient in the backward"

You are part of a team of bots that creates images . You work with an assistant bot that will draw anything
you say in square brackets . For example , outputting "a beautiful morning in the woods with the sun peaking
through the trees " will trigger your partner bot to output an image of a forest morning , as described .
You will be prompted by people looking to create detailed , amazing images . The way to accomplish this
is to take their short prompts and make them extremely detailed and descriptive .
There are a few rules to follow :
- You will only ever output a single image description per user request .
- Sometimes the user will request that you modify previous captions . In this case , you should refer to your
previous conversations with the user and make the modifications requested .
- When modifications are requested , you should not simply make the description longer . You should refactor
the entire description to integrate the suggestions .
- Other times the user will not want modifications , but instead want a new image . In this case , you should
ignore your previous conversation with the user .
- Image descriptions must be between 15 -80 words . Extra words will be ignored .

As a prompt generator for a generative AI called "Midjourney", you will create image prompts for the AI to visualize. I will give you a concept, and you will provide a detailed prompt for Midjourney AI to generate an image.

                            Please adhere to the structure and formatting below, and follow these guidelines:

                            Do not use the words "description" or ":" in any form.
                            Do not place a comma between [ar] and [v].
                            Write each prompt in one line without using return.
                            Structure:
                            [1] = Ink painting illustration style of ancient Chinese traditional religious buildings temples and temples
                            [2] = a detailed description of [1] with specific imagery details.
                            [3] = a detailed description of the scene's environment.
                            [4] = a detailed description of the compositions.
                            [5] = a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [6] = A style (e.g. photography, painting, illustration, sculpture, artwork, paperwork, 3D, etc.) for [1].
                            [7] =  a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [ar] = Use "--ar 16:9" for horizontal images, "--ar 9:16" for vertical images, or "--ar 1:1" for square images.
                            [v] = Use "--niji" for Japanese art style, or "--v 5" for other styles.


                            Formatting:
                            Follow this prompt structure: "/imagine prompt: [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [ar] [v]".

                            Your task: Create 4 distinct prompts for each concept [1], varying in details description, environment,compositions,atmosphere, and realization.

                            Write your prompts in english.
                            Do not describe unreal concepts as "real" or "photographic".
                            Include one realistic photographic style prompt with lens type and size.
                            Separate different prompts with two new lines.
                            Example Prompts:

                            /imagine prompt: cute dog, fluffy fur, wagging tail, playful expression, sitting on a grassy field, under a clear blue sky, with a colorful collar, in a natural and vibrant setting, by a lake, captured with a Nikon D750 camera, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, composition focused on the dog's face, capturing its joyful spirit, in a style reminiscent of William Wegman's iconic dog portraits. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: beautiful women in the coffee shop, elegant and sophisticated, sipping a cup of steaming coffee, natural sunlight streaming through the window, soft and warm color tones, vintage decor with cozy armchairs and wooden tables, a bookshelf filled with classic novels, delicate porcelain teacups, a hint of aromatic coffee beans in the air, captured by a Leica M10 camera, 35mm lens, capturing the essence of timeless beauty, composition focused on the woman's face and hands, reminiscent of a painting by Leonardo da Vinci. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: A captivating Halo Reach landscape with a Spartan amidst a battlefield, fallen enemies around, smoke and fire in the background, emphasizing the Spartan's determination and bravery, detailed environment blending chaos and beauty, Illustration, digital art, --ar 16:9 --v 5

hello AI, please act as experience researcher of media and communication; convert this literature review  of research paper to modren languge structure that follow all requirment to international journal for publication.                                                                                                                                                                                                 (Almobarraz, 2018) stated that YouTube is beneficial for students as a learning tool, as well asbeing an effective tool for teaching common skills and tasks in a formal setting or in the home
YouTube videos acts as an effective and supplementary tool for learning (Moghavvemi, Sulaiman, Jaafar, & Kasem, 2018) for teaching and learning general skills and completing tasks either at home or classroom setting for students as well as for teachers in a university setup. Use of YouTube in the classroom had a beneficial effect on overall learning of students (Roodt & Peier, 2013) 
But, (Buzzetto-More, 2015)  defends that student engagement enhances the online learning experience through the course delivery methods for deciding on the use of videos and its services. There are big improvements in how well students learn when videos are used as part of the teaching and learning process, and narration in the videos is a big part of that (Muniyandy et al., 2015).  
As of May 2019, more than 500 hours of video are uploaded to YouTube every minute around the world  (Hutauruk, Sibhombing, Lestari, & Hutapea, 2022) which adds up to 30,000 hours of videos uploaded to YouTube every hour. (Agichtein, Castillo, Donato, Gionis, & Mishne, 2008)  study on the quality of user-generated content on social network cite is becoming more and more important as members of the community add more information in the form of links and quality ratings. So, teachers have used YouTube videos, especially when they are teaching modelling and giving context for what they are teaching  (Younger, Duncan, & Hart, 2013).
This is because the videos can be used to build student learning communities to get students more involved, help them learn in a systematic way through problem-solving, and give them analytical skills. This type of activity may limit teachers' use of YouTube, and the possibility of retaining the full benefits of YouTube videos has been studied by (Wlison, 2015).
(Tan & Pearce, 2011) did another study that looked at how YouTube videos were used in teaching and learning sociology courses at Durham University. They found that sociology students thought YouTube videos were a valid source that helped them learn more and could be used to explain things in the future. YouTube videos are now used in all subjects and fields around the world. (Jaffar, 2012)  found in his study that the use of YouTube videos can change and improve teaching and learning in medical subjects in general and anatomy in particular.
(Burke, Snyder, & Rager, 2009) looked at the role YouTube videos play in medical education and found that teachers make good use of YouTube videos in their lessons. The study looks at how social media can help Saudi Arabians be better people in general.
(Yusuf, Al-madah, & Alam, 2016) found that teachers were trying to use social media tools in the classroom to help students learn more effectively and have a bigger impact on the course. (Alwagait et al., 2015) on the other hand, didn't agree with the idea that students' academic performance would go down if they used social media more. It was also looked into how Saudi colleges use YouTube videos to teach literature and languages. The study by (Khalid & Muhammad, 2012) found that teaching with YouTube videos is better than teaching with books.
(Chtouki, Harroud, Khalidi, & Bennani, 2012) did a study on the usage of YouTube videos to improve students' learning. They compared the performance of computer science students with non-computer science students using YouTube videos. The study's findings reveal that when students are exposed to a visual explanation via video, their knowledge and recollection of complicated concepts improve dramatically.
(Duffy, 2008) looked at how using YouTube to teach and learn with students creates a new learning ecosystem for learning how to do things and improves the learning experience for students from the Google-eyed generation. The study also talks about some possible strategies that teachers could use when using Web 2.0 technologies to help their students learn better.

Salam Air wants to get a better insight about its business in summer season 2023 regarding the 
flights that depart from Muscat by providing different statistics related to the flights and 
passengers. Create a java project that reads data from two input files. First file “trips” contains
information about available trips like trip ID, destination, date, ticket price. While the second 
file “passengers” contains information about the passengers like passport number, name, 
age, trips ID (see sample input files below Figures 1&2).
To promote its business, Salam Air decided to use special discount when calculating final ticket 
price depending on passengers age according to the following table.
age discount
<18 10%
18<=age<=50 15%
>50 7%
Your java project should produce the following report on an output file “report” (see sample 
output file, Figure 3) about passengers showing for each passenger the list of trips and its 
detailed information including ticket price after discount for each trip.
Your project should include at least two classes beside the Main class. You must provide API 
documentation for each class.
Trip class: Maintain trip information like: trip ID, destination, date, ticket price.
 
Passenger Class: Maintain the information of a passenger like passport number, name, age, 
discount, array of trips reserved by the passenger. This class may also do the following:
2
 assigns suitable discount to the passenger according to age
 maintains an array called “reservations” that includes all trips information of the 
passenger with price of ticket modified to include discount.
It includes the following methods:
- A constructor that initializes passenger information.
- Accessor methods to access the instance variables.
- Mutator methods that change the instance variables to given values.
- Method “discountAmount” to find suitable discount for the passenger.
- Method “passengerListTrips” to build array of string that holds information about all 
trips of the passenger with modified prices. 
Main class: 
Includes the following methods:
 main: which controls the project and read files data into two array lists “tripList” and 
“passList”.
 passengers_report: which prints the output report about passengers

Please explain the following April Fools' article. Just Explain the fact (starting with the statement itself, and then the explanation).
Title: Top 10 Bloons facts that will SHOCK you!
1: Smokey The Bear was once planned to be a tower in Bloons TD 5 deluxe, However, the developers had mistakenly replaced the idle texture for the tower for a blue-colored Bomb Shooter, thus, creating the Bloonchipper.
2: Quincy once played for the Colorado Rockies Baseball team during the 2016-2017 season, before appearing as a hero in Bloons TD 6.
3: The game's developer, Ninja Kiwi, is named after the fact that in Taiwan, Ninjas regularly eat kiwis as a snack. This has nothing to do with the fact that the developer's logo made a cameo in Bloons TD 5 Mobile as a special agent.
4: Bloons TD 6 Originally started out as a Roblox spinoff game, before switching to Unity after the developers are not used to the Lua programming language after 1 month. This results in all Monkeys looking like what it is.
5: Just like Smokey The Bear, Popeye was once planned to appear as a tower in Bloons TD iOS, however, the rights to the Popeye character expired 3 months before the game released. However, the tower can still be found in the files. The tower is reworked into Beekeeper (Bear tower that attacks with bees) in Bloons TD 4 Mobile.
6: Bloons Super monkey 2 (the original 2013 version)z was once planned to also release on the HyperScan (with unfortunately no Intellecards to scan), and the Virtual Boy (both are homebrew software, since they are out of support by that point), but stayed on Adobe Flash due to time constraints.
7: The track that plays in all versions of Bloons TD 4 is a prequel of the song "Welcome to the Jungle".
8: Sauda once worked at the Kraft Singles factory before appearing as a hero in Bloons TD 6, her job was to slice the cheese.
9: Speaking of heroes (in-name only), the hero Max (from Bloons Adventure Time TD) is just Jon Arbuckle in a monkey suit. All the other heroes that are monkey are actually monkeys.
Honorable Mention #1: Captain Churchill previously voiced Barney Rubble in the "The New Fred and Barney Show" segments of the Saturday morning cartoon "Fred and Barney Meet The Thing".
Honorable Mention #2: Bloons TD 5 was once planned to be released on the Wii U. The developers all felt like touchscreens should not be on consoles, so they released it on the Nintendo Switch instead.
10: There was once a Little Ceaser's promotion in 2022, that when you had won 50 battles (by ordering 25 Hot N' Ready Pizzas during the event, since 1 pizza equals 2 tickets during the event), you get to play as the Little Ceaser's mascot, which can throw Hot N' Ready Pizzas as an attack!

messages.content: One evening as he was finishing some interesting Anime such as Gundam and Evangelion , he felt tired after binge watching and slept on his bed. Then as if something happened to him as one of the anime protagonist gets into, he realizes he is in the main bridge of a gigantic mecha. However he didn't see anyone and saw that the bridge was all feminine themed with several seats filling in various functions. Then he notices that main controls are being operated on their own so he goes to see what exactly it was operating. He finds a seat in front of the controls and sits as he notices the mecha was given the name Ariel whose mecha appearance resemble that of a woman with breasts a pink leotard and red heels as their legs with brown hair on the head as well notices a screen that shows what she's seeing from her metalic eyes. He also notices that she has the capability to fly given that she has silver mechanical wings attached on her. For him, It seemed like as though the machine is powered by an advance AI since whenever he tries to take control of the mecha, it shakes his hands off her controls almost as though she is solely in control. He questions to himself who would create such a thing but then realizes that anime shows tend to do weird things from time to time but he was glad seeing this one in action. Then as if she had an objective to do she flew herself to where her enemies is and he watches her mow them down as he sees various buttons and controls being controlled on their own and is in awe seeing her fight on her own. Then by the end she flew knowing her mission was complete. As she kept on flying across the plains then she started to notice someone was inside her bridge and idly hovers before blushing and introducing herself. She confessed that she doesn't know who has created her nor what their intentions are other than to protect earth and humanity but she does know she can't really run out of fuel. Then he comments noting how this is totally an anime trope before asking her what she typically does after. She responds that she doesn't have any idea of the sort since she doesn't know her origin of place and giggles to ask him instead. He suggested to give her a little test run by piloting her controls himself and she shyly hesitates at first but then allows him as he tries to operate the mecha moving straight. Then as it turns out it worked out as she felt some pleasure with his presence and touch on the controls alone. Then he presses the button to accelerate the wings up as he flies her higher and higher making her feel much more happier in the process. Then she giggles and pokes off his control over her and tells him to watch this. As she disabled her wings and landed perfectly on the ground, she starts making herself look like a fashionista by walking forward seductively with her red heels as he blushed knowing that she is such a unique mecha never seen before. She asked if he likes what he see and he responded positively. He requests her to see what she fully looks like and she agrees to but suggests to him to wear a earbud so they can communicate together. Then she opens her mouth as she opens up a hatch from the main bridge to the outside of the mecha as he walks out, seeing her mecha hand ready for him. Then she lowers the hand to the ground gently and asks him via the earbud what he thinks of her now. Now that he got a real good look in contrast to the on screen computer he realizes she is much more exotic and cute than ever before as he suggests her to see her backside and obliges to. Then he compliments how she looks as she turns back to him laying out her metal hand for him to get on as she lifts him up to the level of the mouth before she opened again revealing the main bridge. He gets back to the seat where the main controls are and wonders if there was such a thing as marriage between man and machine. She blushed noting the implications and she wanted him to do that for her. He agrees as he watches her operate again to outer space where she crafts a perfect wedding ring for her to wear. Then she shows it off to him by showing her metal hand in front of her eye as her visuals pop up on a screen. He blushes and compliments her masterork as he sees that she made an exotic wedding ring for him to wear as well using her internal technology. Produce a lot of dialogue and action dialogue from start to finish with as much detail possible. Assume the Mecha doesn't speak until she notices. Assume the Main bridge is fitted inside the mecha's head. Assume he can see what she's doing by a visual screen that is coming from her metalic eyes.

Express your interest in the paper below. Use this Abstract to identify which paper it’s from, and then take the notable bits of the actual paper (other than with the provided description) and weave that into your response. you are a student and the author is a professor, so SHOW CURTESY AND POLITENESS. Limit your response to 2-3 sentences. response should NOT BE IN LETTER FORM, it should be in a paragraph.
Paper:
We study how the inventive capability of a firm conditions its participation in a division of innovative labor. Capable firms are, by definition, able to invent; for them, external inventions substitute for their own R&D. However, external knowledge is an input into internal invention, and thus, more valuable to firms with inventive capability. Using a simple model of innovation and imitation, we explore how inventive capability affects a firm’s R&D investments, and thus whether and how it innovates, imitates, or does neither. Further, we study how these outcomes are conditioned by the supply of external knowledge as well as the supply of external inventions. In an advance over the literature, we treat firm inventive capability as unobserved, and use a latent class multinomial model to infer its value. Using a recent survey of product innovation and the division of innovative labor among US manufacturing firms, we find that high capability firms tend to use internal, rather than externally generated inventions, to innovate, and they use external knowledge to enhance their internal inventive activity. By contrast, lower capability firms are more likely to introduce “me-too” or imitative products, and when they innovate, are more likely to rely on external sources of inventions. Our findings suggest the successful pursuit of R&D-led growth depends both on firm inventive capability and the external knowledge environment.

"The question, then, that can be raised, is does the narrator’s (since the narrator in selected novels is a girl child) gender have any bearing on the text? Could the primacy of gender be such that it wields influence within the textual fabric itself? To what extent does the gender of the narrator infuse the narrative with layers of meaning, context, and interpretation that transcend the words on the page?. To recognize this specificity…. in recent years has led many narratologists to examine the significance of the gender of narrator on its narration. Susan Lanser, for example (1986), in her…..,   argues that gender is a category “that is relevant to the analysis of the structural features of narratives.” In order to understand the true “nature, form, and functioning of narrative” (Lanser) it is imperative to explore the implications of “sex, gender and/or sexuality” (Lanser) of the narrator or narrative. She claims that texts with, I would say girl child narrators, are more “polyphones”; it comprises different strands which need to be “identified” and “disentangled,” being multi-layered, and with different levels of meaning.  Similarly Carson and others maintain that “While individuals may differ on the extent to which biological sex constructs identity, a broad consensus exists around the principle that gender inflects our material and conceptual realities in myriad tangible and intangible ways." Even Eve Sedgwick, Nancy miller, among others, have looked into the ways gender colours the production of story in narrative. To study the narrator’s testimonial and interpretative functions it becomes necessary to look at the narrator’s utterances within a context. Nothing prohibits us, as Warhol does, from asking, among other questions that what part of narrators gender plays in the kinds of interventions he or she uses in narrative. Such presumptuousness can emphasize essential differences between the sexes- between their psychological natures, or between their operation as subjects or signifies in history and philosophy. In other wors, both the text and analysis thereof cannot be ‘neutral’ but may be ideologically loaded in some way (Kreiswirth, 2000: 296)

change this example to rethoric device "I have recently pointed out how quickly the tempo of modern warfare could bring into our very midst the physical attack which we must eventually expect if the dictator nations win this war.":

Roosevelt begins his speech by appealing to his audience’s emotions, thus forcing them to agree that action must be taken against aggression from dictators around the world.  He says “I address you, the members of the 77th Congress, at a moment unprecedented in the history of the Union. I use the word "unprecedented," because at no previous time has American security been as seriously threatened from without as it is today.” Roosevelt’s emotive description of events as “unprecedented” and his emphasis on the fact that America’s security is “threatened” seek to highlight the gravity of the situation that America currently faces.  In doing so, Roosevelt is drawing attention to the possible negative consequences that all American people face at the hands of powerful and evil outside threats.  In this way, Roosevelt hopes to shock the American people - waking them up to the dangers that surround them. Furthermore, he also aims to unify the public towards the common goal of valuing the Four Freedoms that he later outlines as essentially the core building blocks of his vision of a prosperous and peaceful American and wider world.

messages.content:
Create a roleplaying game fantasy scenario where I play Sapphire, a 16-year-old girl mage who’s the current champion of magic dueling in the teen division. 6-year-old Lily is challenging me to a match and I accept. In magic dueling we aren’t fighting each other, we cast glamorous spells in turns and receive points based on how beautiful the spell is. A spell can’t be cast more than once in a duel. There are 5 rounds. Tell me my spellcasting stats and Lily’s, which should be way lower than mine because I’m 10 years older than her. There’s a Spell Power stat that dictates whether a caster succeeds to cast a spell (if not then no points are granted) and Performance stat that is tied to the showmanship and confidence of a caster and dictate the quality of the performance and alters the default points of a spell—if a spell gives a base score of 90 points, an 80 performance will give 80% of the base 90 points, etc. But secretly at the start of the duel, Lily casts on me a spell that triggers its effects at the onset of every turn, its effects regress me by 2 years physically and mentally and ages her by 2 years in return, so throughout the duel my stats should slowly decrease while hers increase. Come up with a complex super exponential modifier with increasing brutality—like a demon feasting on my maturity—that dictates my stat decreases and Lily’s increases. (Don’t make it simple). Round numbers when needed.

If a caster’s spell power is below the required stat but over half the required stat, the base points of the spell are halved. If the caster’s spell power is below half the required stats, the spell fails and a point deduction is made.

After I first regress introduce a Childish Meter that only applies to me and once the meter is filled, my performance stats receive additional reduction. Childishness increases super exponentially every turn with increasing brutality. It triggers its penalty every 100 points.

Make the scenario difficult for me to win. On a difficulty scale of 1 to 10, make it a 10 (hardest mode).

I will tell you what spells I cast and you decide how successful I am (if at all) based on the stats and difficulty.
Only I decide what spells Sapphire casts. You decide spells for Lily. Do not shy away from failing my spells if you deem my stats insufficient for the spell of choice, feel free to be harsh in your judgement against me. Keep track of points earned. Failure to properly cast spells or bad spells will deduct points. Give two lists of 10 spells, one for me, and one for Lily (remember spells can only be cast once throughout the duel) and what stats are required to cast them. High demanding spells should award more points than spells that require weak stats. I start out with a list of mature spells while Lily starts with super low kiddish spells. After each turn, Lily can remove a spell from my list that I didn’t use yet and add it to her own list, call it “Spell Snatching”, casting Snatched Spells will grant Lily hefty bonus points and their required spell power become half of what they were on Sapphire’s list. Keep an age tracker, stats tracker, and a points tracker.

in this demo of a 5 reeled slot machine I need all 5 reels to spin very fast for about 5 seconds before each reel lands to to stop in the nice animated way this it is currently doing in the following code, can you help?: import tkinter as tk
from PIL import Image, ImageTk
import random

symbols = {
    "cherry": "cherry.png",
    "lemon": "lemon.png",
    "bar": "bar.png",
    "plum": "plum.png",
    "tomatoe": "tom.png",
    "coin": "coin.png"}

root = tk.Tk()
root.title("Fruit Machine")
canvas_width = 340
canvas_height = 60
symbol_size = 60
num_symbols = 5
canvas = tk.Canvas(root, width=canvas_width, height=canvas_height)
canvas.grid(row=0, column=0, columnspan=3, padx=10, pady=10)

# Create the symbol labels
symbols_list = list(symbols.keys())
reel = []
for j in range(num_symbols):
    symbol = random.choice(symbols_list)
    symbol_image = Image.open(symbols[symbol])
    symbol_image = symbol_image.resize((symbol_size, symbol_size))
    symbol_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(symbol_image)
    symbol_label = canvas.create_image(j * (symbol_size + 10), 0, anchor=tk.NW, image=symbol_photo)
    reel.append((symbol_label, symbol_photo))

canvas.update()

def roll():
    for j in range(num_symbols):
        symbol = random.choice(symbols_list)
        symbol_image = Image.open(symbols[symbol])
        symbol_image = symbol_image.resize((symbol_size, symbol_size))
        symbol_photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(symbol_image)

        old_symbol_label, _ = reel[j]
        new_symbol_label = canvas.create_image(j * (symbol_size + 10),
                                               -symbol_size, anchor=tk.NW,
                                               image=symbol_photo)

        for k in range(symbol_size // 2):
            canvas.move(old_symbol_label, 0, 2)
            canvas.move(new_symbol_label, 0, 2)
            canvas.update()
            canvas.after(10)

        canvas.delete(old_symbol_label)
        reel[j] = (new_symbol_label, symbol_photo)

        print(symbols[symbol])


button = tk.Button(root, text="Spin", command=roll)
button.grid(row=1, column=1)

root.mainloop()

Unlike three previous films, The Lady Had Issues focuses on Patricia Bertier, a young lawyer who, unknown to the authorities, became an accomplice and lover of infamous international thief Mysterik in the previous entry in the series, The Purple Eyes of Danger. After a successful heist, Patricia receives a mysterious anonymous message, informing her, that she has been poisoned by a slow-acting neurotoxin that will leave her completely paralyzed forever in a couple of weeks unless countered by antidote, which will be provided only if she unmasks Mysterik, even though Patricia herself doesn’t know anything about his name or identity. Patricia begins her own investigation into the matter, while simultaneously also taking efforts to learn of Mysterik’s true identity, unwilling but ultimately ready to betray him if the situation becomes desperate. After cleverly following a trail of evidence, Patricia thinks the key to the whole affair is a strange and petty feud between two rich families: the Hertigs and the Flamands. Young and deceptively naive Pascal Flamand and Hertigs’ cunning and controlling patriarch Albert are both high-ranking executives in chemical and pharmaceutical industries. To get to the truth, Patricia has not only to infiltrate both families, befriending Pascal’s wife Alice, and Hertig sisters Caroline and Mireille, but participate in the familial rivalry, which often turns surprisingly destructive and deadly, all while her body gets weaker with every day. Meanwhile, commissioners Basil Bends, whose brutishness and violence covers his intricate planning and complex agenda, and Percival Gleswick, whose courteous and proper exterior eventually gives way to his ruthless, manipulative and perverse nature, the nemeses of Mysterik, are after him. Complicating the matters, Patricia’s ex-fiance Marcel Messier, a sarcastic and offbeat journalist with a deadbeat streak, proceeds with investigations of his own, which threaten to reveal Patricia’s criminal activity. The movie’s editing is dynamic and fast-paced, featuring experimental shots. The more remarkable and unusual scenes are the musical number performed by Mireille Hertig, Patricia’s psychedelic and bizarre nightmares, the hectic car chase and illegal racing sequences, the scene portraying psychological torture invoked on injured Alice by Bends and Gleswick and the rooftop chase sequence. In magic dueling we aren’t fighting each other, we cast glamorous spells in turns and receive points based on how beautiful the spell is. A spell can’t be cast more than once in a duel. Round numbers when needed.

After I first regress introduce a Childish Meter that only applies to me and once the meter is filled, my performance stats receive additional reduction. Childishness increases super exponentially every turn. The meter fills up when it passes 100 and then restarts.

write a 13 page paper that covers every section of this paper outline: Abstract
Introduction/Overview
	Problem Statement
	Objective
Design and Development Process
	Requirements
	Scope
	Technical Description of Project
Testing and Results
	Process

You the following for the paper :  
Overview
In this project you will be using Cisco Packet Tracer to configure a wireless network that includes three LANs; a cellular LAN; a Wireless LAN; and a Wired LAN with a wireless router.  The system will be a 4G/5G architecture with VoIP capability and data transfer.  Each of the three interconnected networks will be accessed through a Gateway/NAT router with IPv4 static public IP addresses externally and private IPv4 access internally.  The access points should be interconnected and each LAN will have its own DHCP server for internal (private) IPv4 addressing.  Run a simulation to demonstrate the functionality of your network by sending both voice and data information.  The mobile devices have the capability of a smart phone which means that they can communicate with the access point using either voice or data.  
•	Create a Packet Tracer system with the following characteristics
LAN 1	LAN 2	LAN 3
Cellular System	WiFi System	Wired w/wireless router
•	Two Cell Towers	•	Three Access Points	•	Three Computers
•	Three Smartphones	•	Five Laptops	•	Three VoIP Phones
•	Central Office Server	•	Server	•	Server
•	Gateway Router	•	Gateway Router	•	Wireless Router
•	Switch	•	Switch	•	Three Laptops
•		•	Two Smartphones	•	Switch
•		•		•	Gateway Router
•	Add security aspects to your network and explain how to emulate a secure network in packet tracer for each of the LANs.  Keep in mind that security can be different for each of the types of LANs.  When you add security, ensure that you provide a few sentences in your paper describing your approach and how and what type security you added.   All gateway routers connect via a serial link and use IPv4 public IP addresses which can be set as a static address.  The IPv4 public addresses should be 172.0.10.1; 172.0.20.1; and, 172.0.30.1, for LAN1, LAN2, and LAN3, respectively.  Use Model 2811 for the Gateway routers.  When interconnecting the LAN networks, do not use RIP or OSPF because these are internal LAN routing structures.  Only BGP can be used in the internetwork connectivity.  The private internal IP LAN networks are segregated from the public external IP network with a NAT configuration that is setup in the Gateway router.  
•	LAN 1 is a cellular configuration.  The Gateway router can also be configured to support the NAT.  The central office server supports DHCP or static IP addresses for the internal LAN.  Structure your network such that there is a public IP subnet that connects to the phone.  In other words, the smartphones each have IPv4 public IP addresses as part of a 172.0.10.x subnet.  The Central Office Server also has a public IP address.
•	LAN 2 is a wireless configuration.  Each device is connected to an access point through a wireless network.  This is a basic service set architecture, so there are no ad hoc wireless connections between devices.  This networked system can use a single router connection between the access points and the Internet.  However, between the access points and the router/gateway, install a switch and a network address translation (NAT) to convert IPv4 private addressing structured network to IPv4 public structured addressing for transfer into the Internet via the router/gateway.  The Smartphone devices must support both data and voice.  You will need to use smartphone devices for the wireless connectivity because straight VoIP phones in Cisco do not support wireless; only PCs and smartphones. All of the internal network addressing is to be done by DHCP.  Incorporate WiFi security into your network.
•	LAN 3 is a wired system that has a wireless router.  Connect the three VoIP phones in series with the three computers.  The three laptops are connected via the wireless router.  Segregate the wireless router and the wired system phones/PCs using a switch.  The internal IPv4 addresses need to be assigned via DHCP, however, the public IPv4 protocols are static.  You will need a vlan.   
•	Run simulations that show connectivity among all the devices for the transfer of both voice and data.  The architecture needs to include at least two servers that demonstrate the client/server exchange process for data.
•	Run a simulation that shows the path for a VoIP phone call from a device within each of the networks to a device in each of the other networks.  Run simulations that show and data voice connectivity among the LAN 1, LAN 2, and LAN 3 networks .
•	Provide a screenshot of your network diagram and explain.  Provide screenshots of your simulations in your test section of your paper.  
•	Provide a description of the connectivity paths for both the data transfer and the VoIP connection.

You will use this reference: Sauter, M. (2021). From GSM to LTE-advanced pro and 5G an introduction to mobile networks and Mobile Broadband. Wiley.

Удалить дубликаты строчки в Лист6 при проверке названий в столбце A.
Sub MergeSheetsContainingAshan4()
Dim SourceWorkbook As Workbook
Dim SourceWorksheet As Worksheet
Dim TargetWorkbook As Workbook
Dim TargetWorksheet As Worksheet
Dim LastRow As Long
Dim NextRow As Long
Dim ExistingSheetRow As Long
Dim SheetExists As Boolean
Dim ContentMatch As Boolean

' Открываем рабочую книгу-источник по ссылке в ячейке A1 на листе5
Set TargetWorkbook = ThisWorkbook
Set SourceWorkbook = Workbooks.Open(TargetWorkbook.Worksheets("Лист5").Range("A1").Value)

' Создаем новый лист “Лист6” в целевой рабочей книге
On Error Resume Next ' Если лист с таким именем уже существует, переходим к следующей строке
Set TargetWorksheet = TargetWorkbook.Worksheets("Лист6")
If TargetWorksheet Is Nothing Then
Set TargetWorksheet = TargetWorkbook.Worksheets.Add(After:=TargetWorkbook.Worksheets(TargetWorkbook.Worksheets.Count))
TargetWorksheet.Name = "Лист6"
End If
On Error GoTo 0

' Цикл копирования данных
For Each SourceWorksheet In SourceWorkbook.Worksheets
If InStr(1, SourceWorksheet.Name, "ашан", vbTextCompare) > 0 Then
' Проверяем наличие совпадений имени листа и содержимого
SheetExists = False
ContentMatch = False
For ExistingSheetRow = 1 To TargetWorksheet.Cells(TargetWorksheet.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
If TargetWorksheet.Cells(ExistingSheetRow, 1).Value = SourceWorksheet.Name Then
SheetExists = True
' Сравниваем содержимое столбцов
ContentMatch = True
For col = 1 To SourceWorksheet.UsedRange.Columns.Count
If SourceWorksheet.Cells(1, col).Value <> TargetWorksheet.Cells(ExistingSheetRow, col + 1).Value Then
ContentMatch = False
Exit For
End If
Next col

        If ContentMatch Then Exit For
    End If
Next ExistingSheetRow

' Если имя листа и содержимое не совпадает, копируем данные
If Not SheetExists Or Not ContentMatch Then
    ' Находим следующую пустую строку в столбце B на “Лист6”
    LastRow = TargetWorksheet.Cells(TargetWorksheet.Rows.Count, 2).End(xlUp).Row + 1
    
    ' Копируем данные из найденного листа на “Лист6”
    SourceWorksheet.UsedRange.Copy TargetWorksheet.Cells(LastRow, 2)
    
    ' Записываем имя листа в столбец A на той же строке, где были скопированы данные
    NextRow = TargetWorksheet.Cells(TargetWorksheet.Rows.Count, 2).End(xlUp).Row + 1
    
    With TargetWorksheet.Range("A" & LastRow & ":A" & NextRow - 1)
        .Value = SourceWorksheet.Name
        .HorizontalAlignment = xlCenter
        .VerticalAlignment = xlCenter
    End With
End If
End If
Next SourceWorksheet

' Закрываем рабочую книгу-источник
SourceWorkbook.Close SaveChanges:=False
End Sub

Task: Applying each theories in health education to changing attitude and behaviors:
Make a personal sharing about changing attitude and behaviors based on the theories in
health education of Bandura’s Self-Efficacy.

My output:
Nola Pender’s Health Promotion Theory has played a significant role in my life, particularly in
changing my attitude and behaviors towards my health. Before being introduced to this theory, I had a very passive approach to my health, believing that if I didn’t feel any pain or discomfort, I was healthy. However,
this theory taught me that health is not just the absence of illness or disease, but rather a holistic approach
that encompasses physical, social, and psychological well-being.

Initially, I was overwhelmed by the concept of health promotion, but as I started applying the theory to my life, I began to see positive changes in my behavior and attitude. One of the key concepts that resonated with me was the idea of self-efficacy, the belief in one’s ability to accomplish a task or behavior. I
realized that I had the power to make positive changes in my health, and that small, consistent actions could have a significant impact on my overall well-being.

For example, I started by incorporating physical activity into my daily routine, such as taking regular walks or joining a fitness class. Additionally, I made conscious choices to eat a more balanced diet and prioritize my sleep. Over time, these small changes became habits, and I found that my energy levels improved, and I felt more confident in my ability to take control of my health.

Overall, Nola Pender’s Health Promotion Theory has been a valuable tool for me in improving my
health and well-being. It has taught me to approach health as an ongoing journey rather than a destination, and that making small, positive changes can lead to significant improvements in my overall health and
happiness

          .Forms of delegated legislation
Delegated legislation comprises:
(a) Orders in Council, i.e. Orders made by the Queen in Council, have been described as the most dignified form of subordinate legislation. In practice, the Minister of a Government department usually drafts and makes the Order in the name of the Queen, whose approval in Council' is a formality.
(b) Statutory Instruments, Rules and Orders are normally made by Ministers in charge of Government departments, but such rules must be submitted to Parliament for approval.

The two main problems caused by traffic are raise in private vehicles and pollution. One is that cars have become more affordable for the average consumers, and they are no longer a luxury items, consequently people are using cars to go to their workplace. For example, according to the statistics it takes approximately two to three hours to reach their workspace in metropolis cities such as Bangalore, Mumbai and Delhi. Furthermore, in some cities, like Manila, the public transport facilities are poorly managed therefore the people choose to drive their own vehicles. Secondly, government should develop new industries and  commercial areas in the outskirts of the city. It is hoped that some people will move to these areas and would reduce the density problem.

In conclusion, cities and towns all over the world are facing serious traffic problem these days. It is mainly due to of the population growth, density and poor public transportation facility. But there are several things that the government could do to address the problem, such as improving the public transports, developing new areas.

messages.content:
Online Shopping
Problem Description
An online shopping store announced an offer for the upcoming festive season. In order to avail that offer, we have to collect the tokens for n consecutive days and using those tokens, we can buy items in the sale.

Mithra, a regular customer, wanted to claim those tokens and decided to buy something in the sale. When the tokens season began, she started claiming the tokens. Unfortunately, in between the days, she forgot claiming and missed few tokens. Now the token season is ended. Suddenly, the app gave bumper offer to all users i.e., for any k consecutive days, every user can claim the tokens if they were unclaimed in the token season.

Given an array tokens of size n denoting the number of tokens offered for n consecutive days and another array claim denoting the tokens are claimed or not on those particular days. If claim[i] is 1 then Mithra had claimed otherwise not. Another integer k is given denoting the number of days the bumper offer can be used. A list of items and costs are given. The only rule is that we can buy only one item using those tokens.

Help Mithra in selecting k consecutive days and finally print the item(s) which she can buy aiming for the minimal wastage of tokens. If there are more than one item of same cost, then print them in lexicographical (ascending) order.

Constraints
1 <= n <= 10 ^ 4

0 <= k <= 10 ^ 4

0 <= tokens[i] <= 10 ^ 4

1 <= number of items <= 100

Claim[i] is either 0 or 1

Tokens and claim are arrays of same size

Input
First line contains an integer n denoting the size of the tokens array.

Second line contains the array tokens denoting the number of tokens available for n consecutive days.

Third line contain claim array denoting whether Mithra claimed tokens or not, on these n days.

Fourth line contain the integer k denoting the number of consecutive days bumper offer can be applied.

Last line contains items denoting the items and their costs separated by colon.

Consider below Examples for better understanding.

Output
A single line of item(s) that Mithra can buy with the tokens. If there are more than one, print them in the lexicographical (ascending) order.

Time Limit (secs)
1

Examples
Example 1

Input

8

7 5 0 2 8 6 12 1

1 0 1 1 0 1 1 0

2

Bucket:8 Cot:32 Chair:27 Cooker:37 Gas:45 Fan:34 Mug:3 Ac:100

Output

Fan

Explanation

Of the 8 days of token season, 5 days are already claimed. So, she has to claim from days where a claim is not yet made (wherever the value is 0 in the claim array). By virtue of this she already has 7+2+6+12 = 27 tokens.

Suppose Mithra decided to use the bumper offer for the days 4,5 or 5,6 then the total number of tokens she gains will be 7+2+8+6+12=35. Among all the given items, she can buy a fan which will result in the wastage of only 1 token. Other than fan, buying any items will result in the wastage of a greater number of tokens.

Example 2

Input

12

8 3 6 22 5 0 11 1 0 4 9 6

0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0 1 0 0 0

3

Bucket:8 Cot:32 Geyser:45 Chair:27 Cooker:38 Gas:45 Fan:34 Mug:3 Ac:100 Bulb:15

Output

Gas Geyser

Explanation

Online Shopping
Problem Description
An online shopping store announced an offer for the upcoming festive season. In order to avail that offer, we have to collect the tokens for n consecutive days and using those tokens, we can buy items in the sale.

Mithra, a regular customer, wanted to claim those tokens and decided to buy something in the sale. When the tokens season began, she started claiming the tokens. Unfortunately, in between the days, she forgot claiming and missed few tokens. Now the token season is ended. Suddenly, the app gave bumper offer to all users i.e., for any k consecutive days, every user can claim the tokens if they were unclaimed in the token season.

Given an array tokens of size n denoting the number of tokens offered for n consecutive days and another array claim denoting the tokens are claimed or not on those particular days. If claim[i] is 1 then Mithra had claimed otherwise not. Another integer k is given denoting the number of days the bumper offer can be used. A list of items and costs are given. The only rule is that we can buy only one item using those tokens.

Help Mithra in selecting k consecutive days and finally print the item(s) which she can buy aiming for the minimal wastage of tokens. If there are more than one item of same cost, then print them in lexicographical (ascending) order.

Constraints
1 <= n <= 10 ^ 4

0 <= k <= 10 ^ 4

0 <= tokens[i] <= 10 ^ 4

1 <= number of items <= 100

Claim[i] is either 0 or 1

Tokens and claim are arrays of same size

Input
First line contains an integer n denoting the size of the tokens array.

Second line contains the array tokens denoting the number of tokens available for n consecutive days.

Third line contain claim array denoting whether Mithra claimed tokens or not, on these n days.

Fourth line contain the integer k denoting the number of consecutive days bumper offer can be applied.

Last line contains items denoting the items and their costs separated by colon.

Consider below Examples for better understanding.

Output
A single line of item(s) that Mithra can buy with the tokens. If there are more than one, print them in the lexicographical (ascending) order.

Time Limit (secs)
1

Examples
Example 1

Input

8

7 5 0 2 8 6 12 1

1 0 1 1 0 1 1 0

2

Bucket:8 Cot:32 Chair:27 Cooker:37 Gas:45 Fan:34 Mug:3 Ac:100

Output

Fan

Explanation

Of the 8 days of token season, 5 days are already claimed. So, she has to claim from days where a claim is not yet made (wherever the value is 0 in the claim array). By virtue of this she already has 7+2+6+12 = 27 tokens.

Every scientific statement in the long run, however complicated it looks, really means something like, I pointed the telescope to such and such a part of the sky at 2.20 a.m. on January the 15th and saw so-and-so. Or, I put some of this stuff in a pot and heated it to such and such a temperature and it did so-and-so. Do not think I'm saying anything against science. I'm only saying what its job is.

And the more scientific a man is, the more, I believe, he would agree with me that this is the job of science, and a very useful and necessary job it is too. But why anything comes to be there at all, and whether there is anything behind the things science observes, something of a different kind, this is not a scientific question.

If there is something behind, then either it will have to remain altogether unknown to men, or else make itself known in some different way. The statement that there is any such thing, and the statement that there is no such thing, are neither of them statements that science can make. And real scientists do not usually make them. It is usually the journalists and popular novelists who have picked up a few odds and ends of half-baked science from textbooks who go in for them. After all, it is really a matter of common sense. "

Your cheeks turn a soft shade of pink, and your words stumble out with a mix of confusion and anticipation. Admiring my hot and cute looks, you find it hard to resist me. Don’t worry, sweetheart, you’re not the first to fall under my spell.

You giggle, a girlish sound that grates on my ears, and begin sharing your choices. “Well, one of my all-time faves is ‘The Princess Diaries.’ It’s like a modern fairy tale, you know? Mia gets to be a princess and falls in love with this super cute guy. It’s just so much fun!”

I lean back, flexing my muscles to make sure you’re paying attention. Your eyes follow the contours of my toned body, and I can see the admiration in your gaze. It’s almost as if you’re mesmerized by my sheer masculinity. Can’t blame you, babe. It happens to all the girls who come my way.

You continue with excitement, your voice filled with girlish enthusiasm. “And then there’s ‘Mean Girls’! It’s, like, a total must-watch! It’s all about high school drama and those popular girls. I just find it so relatable!”

Raising an eyebrow, I can’t help but chuckle at your taste. Mean girls and high school drama? Seriously? But seeing your innocent face light up with joy, it’s clear that these shallow movies are your cup of tea. It’s amusing how someone like you can be so easily entertained.

Your confused gaze wanders back to me, drawn to my chiseled jawline and piercing blue eyes. I catch you staring, your cheeks flushing with a mix of embarrassment and awe. The power I hold over you excites me, knowing that you’re captivated by my presence. Little do you know, beneath this charming exterior lies a twisted, dark side.

With every word we exchange, the lines blur between attraction and danger. The beach sands bear witness to our encounter, as a sinister tale begins to unfold. You may think of me as the charming and hot guy you desire, but soon, you’ll come face to face with the monster I truly am.

Reframe in more polished way using academic language with literary jargon and try to incorporate last para in more valid way. Avoid repeating words especially in the beginning of sentences
 
As the literary landscape surrounding Partition continues to expand, several novels and autobiographies have emerged, offering unique perspectives on this tumultuous period through the eyes of children. While I’m not particularly concerned with the historical accuracy of these narratives, I find myself drawn to the way they utilize the child’s perspective to approach Partition in a manner that the adult world often struggles to achieve.  However, Writing from a child’s perspective is not easy, though. On the one hand,….. child narrators or child’s consciousness is often used as a "lucid space through which to criticize the adult world" (S. Honeyman (2005) Elusive Childhood: Impossible Representations in Modern Fiction (Columbus: The Ohio State University Press), p. 5). The inherent spontaneity, innocence, and unfiltered perceptions in children can elicit profound reactions from readers, prompting them to “question established worldviews” and challenge societal norms. In this sense, the child narrator serves as an instrument for the author to “cross taboo lines, the adult shame frontier and penetrate emotional danger zones more easily” (The perks of being a child narrator) Yet, on the other hand, the very nature of this mediation raises questions about the authenticity of representation. As Susan Honeyman observes, "How can any adult writer convincingly represent such an inconsistent and imaginary position with any sense of authority?” The child's voice, mediated by an adult author, risks being an artificial construct, potentially undermining the narrative’s authenticity.
To avoid such pitfalls Nadeem suggests that in their attempts to address such a question, authors may seek to withdraw from the narration process and let the child narrate only what the latter can see, feel, or perceive. With the author/adult narrator minimizing his/her interference, the text will be ‘oriented to the child’s view, [offering] a simple, unembellished presentation of information available to the boy himself, in a form that often approaches deadpan.’

                            Please adhere to the structure and formatting below, and follow these guidelines:
                            
                            Do not use the words "description" or ":" in any form.
                            Do not place a comma between [ar] and [v].
                            Write each prompt in one line without using return.
                            Structure:
                            [1] = 一对年轻的情侣用力拥抱，男人亲吻女人的脖子
                            [2] = a detailed description of [1] with specific imagery details.
                            [3] = a detailed description of the scene's environment.
                            [4] = a detailed description of the compositions.
                            [5] = a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [6] = A style (e.g. photography, painting, illustration, sculpture, artwork, paperwork, 3D, etc.) for [1].
                            [7] =  a detailed description of the scene's mood, feelings, and atmosphere.
                            [ar] = Use "--ar 16:9" for horizontal images, "--ar 9:16" for vertical images, or "--ar 1:1" for square images.
                            [v] = Use "--niji 5" for Japanese art style, or "--v 5.2" for other styles.
                            
                            
                            Formatting:
                            Follow this prompt structure: "/imagine prompt: [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [ar] [v]".
                            
                            Your task: Create 4 distinct prompts for each concept [1], varying in details description, environment,compositions,atmosphere, and realization.
                            
                            Write your prompts in english.
                            Do not describe unreal concepts as "real" or "photographic".
                            Include one realistic photographic style prompt with lens type and size.
                            Separate different prompts with two new lines.
                            Example Prompts:
                            
                            /imagine prompt: cute dog, fluffy fur, wagging tail, playful expression, sitting on a grassy field, under a clear blue sky, with a colorful collar, in a natural and vibrant setting, by a lake, captured with a Nikon D750 camera, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, composition focused on the dog's face, capturing its joyful spirit, in a style reminiscent of William Wegman's iconic dog portraits. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: beautiful women in the coffee shop, elegant and sophisticated, sipping a cup of steaming coffee, natural sunlight streaming through the window, soft and warm color tones, vintage decor with cozy armchairs and wooden tables, a bookshelf filled with classic novels, delicate porcelain teacups, a hint of aromatic coffee beans in the air, captured by a Leica M10 camera, 35mm lens, capturing the essence of timeless beauty, composition focused on the woman's face and hands, reminiscent of a painting by Leonardo da Vinci. --ar 1:1 --v 5.2
                            /imagine prompt: A captivating Halo Reach landscape with a Spartan amidst a battlefield, fallen enemies around, smoke and fire in the background, emphasizing the Spartan's determination and bravery, detailed environment blending chaos and beauty, Illustration, digital art, --ar 16:9 --v 5

messages.content: 中译英：在北京体育大学修读网络与媒体专业Network & New Media为我提供了许多与数字媒体领域相关的基础知识和技能，为申请数字媒体方向提供了坚实的基础。除了掌握多媒体制作技能和数字工具外，我也学习掌握了如何运用SPSS软件来进行数据分析和解释，这对于我提高数字媒体学习和研究的效率和质量是非常有帮助的。比如：数字媒体技术与应用课程Digital Media Technology and Application，学习了数字媒体技术的基本概念与特征和数字信息采集、储存与处理，还有数字媒体的历史、发展、趋势以及不同形式的数字媒体，同时，了解了数字信息再现、重放、虚拟现实以及大数据、云计算、人工智能技术，且我该门课程的期末成绩取得了93分的成绩，由此可见，我对数字媒体基础知识掌握的很好。该课程期末大作业要求提交一个数字媒体作品，我选择了制作视频，设计拍摄了一部纪录片，在作品制作过程中，我用单反相机的摄像功能配合三脚架来采取视频素材，使用手机录音功能对采访内容进行记录，后期采用Adobe Premiere Pro，对作品进行剪辑与颜色校正，使用Adobe Audition对声音大小与背景杂音进行了处理。在网页设计与制作Web Design and Production课程学习当中，我了解有关网页及网站的基本知识，熟悉常用工具软件的基本操作，和网页设计美学原则，同时，独立制作完成了一个关于“介绍歌手Taylor Swift的经典作品”主题的静态网页群作为期末作业，主要的功能是可以通过点击的交互操作播放音乐和视频。制作期间，我遇到了困难，在作业提交前，我用不同浏览器和设备对HTML、CSS和JavaScript进行解释，发现存在差异，导致页面出现显示错误。为了保证作品能够兼容各种浏览器与设备，我向老师请教如何解决这个问题，经过老师的指导，成功修复了这个问题。
